title: Filter-normalized direction crashes when device="cuda"
description: `FilterNormalizedDirection.build` draws the random direction on the CPU (`torch.randn(param.shape, generator=generator)` with a CPU `torch.Generator`) but normalizes it against `param`, which lives on `self.config.device`. When `device="cuda"` the division `flat_w.norm(...) / flat_d.norm(...)` mixes a CUDA (N,1) tensor with a CPU (N,1) tensor and PyTorch raises "Expected all tensors to be on the same device". `device` is an explicitly exposed field for this entry (webui/launch_layout.py:1342 lists "device" under map_loss_landscape), so this is a reachable configuration, not a hypothetical. The rest of the class is already device-aware (`_apply` does `dir1[name].to(param.device)`), which shows the CPU/GPU split was intended — only `build` was missed.
suggested_fix: Build the direction on the parameter's device (`torch.randn(param.shape, generator=generator, device=...)` with a device-matched generator) or move `flat_w` to CPU before computing `scale`, e.g. `flat_w = param.detach().reshape(param.shape[0], -1).cpu()`.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source and empirically.

1. Device reaches the model's parameters. `LossLandscapeRun._load_run` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/loss_landscape.py:120-127) passes `device=self.config.device` into `RunLoader.load`, which does `model = model.to(device)` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/loader.py:219) and then wraps it in `ModelWrapper`. `ModelWrapper.module` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/model_wrapper.py:27-29) returns exactly that moved model, and `run()` at line 164-167 feeds it to `FilterNormalizedDirection.build`. So with `device="cuda"` every `param` inside `build` is a CUDA tensor.

2. `build` draws the direction on CPU: `torch.Generator()` (line 23, CPU generator) and `torch.randn(param.shape, generator=generator)` (line 31) with no `device=` argument, so `random`/`flat_d` are CPU while `flat_w` is CUDA.

3. Line 35 divides a CUDA (N,1) tensor by a CPU (N,1) tensor. This is not the allowed CPU-0-dim-scalar promotion case, so PyTorch raises. Verified in the project env (torch 2.11.0+cu130, GTX 1650):
   `RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device, but found at least two devices, cuda:0 and cpu!`
   (Line 36's `flat_d * scale` would fail for the same reason if line 35 were fixed in isolation — the correct fix is to draw `random` on `param.device`, e.g. a device-matched generator or `.to(param.device)`.)

4. Reachability confirmed: `device` is a plain `str = "cpu"` field on `LossLandscapeConfig` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/configuration/diagnostics.py:317-334), overridable via `ConfigCli` in main/analysis/map_loss_landscape.py, and explicitly listed in the webui "Landscape" field group at /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/launch_layout.py:1330-1348. So `device=cuda` is an offered, one-click configuration.

5. Tests do not cover it: /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/backbone_inference/test_loss_landscape.py builds only CPU `_TinyConv`/`Linear` models, so the CPU/GPU split is never exercised. `LandscapeEvaluator._apply` doing `dir1[name].to(param.device)` (line 55) confirms the author expected direction tensors to possibly live off-device, i.e. `build` was simply written CPU-only.

This is not one of the listed known non-issues (no legacy shim, no dynamic dispatch, no deliberate quirk).
correction: Mechanism, file and line are all accurate. Only the severity is overstated. This is an optional offline diagnostics entry (main/analysis/map_loss_landscape.py), not a training/inference production path; the default config value is `device="cpu"`, so out-of-the-box runs are unaffected. When the non-default `cuda` is selected the entry aborts immediately and loudly with a clear device-mismatch RuntimeError before any output is written — no silent corruption, no bad artifacts, no wasted GPU hours. That is a "major" (broken feature under a documented, exposed option), not a "critical". The complete fix must also cover line 36 (`flat_d * scale`), which mismatches for the same reason; the clean repair is to create the random tensor on `param.device` (device-matched `torch.Generator(device=param.device)` or `torch.randn(param.shape, generator=generator).to(param.device)` before the norm computation).

title: Cross-validation orchestration tracks `fold_N/seedM` but backbone/JEPA workers write to `<training_tag>_fold_N/seedM`
description: `FoldTrainingStage`/`FoldInferenceStage` build items from `FoldNaming.name(index)` (`fold_0`, `fold_0/seed1`, ...) and derive every completion/resume/log path as `stage_dir / item` (`<run>/folds/fold_0/seed1`). The worker instead resolves the run directory via `CrossValidationWorker.fold_run_name` (pipelines/cross_validation/workers.py:115-126), which for training_type in {backbone, jepa} prefixes the RunNaming training tag, so the real directory is `<run>/folds/resunet-conv-hungarian-K_5-hv-A-param_l1_1-.../fold_0/seed1`; `CompletionMarker.stamp` is written there (tools/training/trainer.py:487). Consequences on the default config (training_type='backbone', seeds=[0..4], resume=True): (a) `QueuedInferenceStage._training_complete` (tools/orchestration/stages.py:161) never finds a marker, so every fold/split is reported SKIPPED and CV inference never runs; (b) `QueuedTrainingStage._is_complete` (tools/orchestration/stages.py:82) never finds one either, so resume retrains every fold; (c) the GPU queue creates `folds/fold_0/seed1/worker.log` (tools/orchestration/gpu_queue.py:316), so `FoldCollector` (inherited `TrialCollector._run_dirs`) collects those log-only dirs as extra empty folds and `CrossValidationReport._require_all_folds` (cv_report.py:61) then raises because it sees 2*n_folds records; (d) training_results.json is keyed `fold_0/seed1` while collected records are `<tag>_fold_0/seed1`, so `record.training_result` is always {} and `_fold_base_record` (workers.py:73) reports PARTIAL with duration None for every fold. Only training_type='profile_autoencoder' works, because `fold_run_name` returns the bare `fold_N` there. The tests only ever build directories literally named `fold_0` (tests/cross_validation/test_stages.py:122, test_workers.py:39-40), so the backbone path is never exercised. Sibling harnesses do not diverge: patch_sweep passes the unit name straight through as run_name (pipelines/patch_sweep/workers.py:46) and benchmark uses `SeedExpandedStage.unit_base` for both item and run name.
evidence:
if not self._training_complete(run_name):
                self.logger.warning(f"{run_name}: training incomplete, inference skipped")
suggested_fix: Make stage items and worker run names agree: either have the stages derive their item/path from a shared `fold_run_name` helper in folds.py, or drop the RunNaming prefix so the fold directory is literally `fold_N[/seedM]` and record the model tag in run metadata. Add a regression test that stamps completion through the worker's own naming and asserts the stage sees it.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source, end to end.

1. Item naming (orchestrator side). `FoldTrainingStage.__init__` (pipelines/cross_validation/stages.py:22-25) and `FoldInferenceStage.__init__` (:53-56) build items from `FoldNaming.name(index)` + `SeedSet.units`, i.e. literally `fold_0/seed0 ... fold_4/seed4` (folds.py:113-121, seed_sweep.py:20-37). Every path they derive is `stage_dir / item` = `<run>/folds/fold_0/seed0`: the job log (stages.py:45), `QueuedTrainingStage._is_complete` / `_purge_unfinished` / `_cached_result` (tools/orchestration/stages.py:82-104), `QueuedInferenceStage._training_complete` (:160-161), and `_has_split_inference` / `_purge_unfinished_split` / `_split_log` (stages.py:60-85).

2. Worker side. `CrossValidationWorker.fold_run_name` (workers.py:115-126) prefixes `RunNaming.training_tag(...)` for training_type in {backbone, jepa}. `FoldTrainingWorker._run_backbone` passes that as `run_name` with `logdir=<run>/folds` (workers.py:136, 149); `TrainingRunMetadata` sets `run_directory = base_logdir / run_name` (pipelines/shared/config/run_metadata.py:26-28), and `Trainer` stamps `CompletionMarker.stamp(self.run_dir, ...)` there (tools/training/trainer.py:487). `FoldInferenceWorker.run` also resolves `<run>/folds/<fold_run_name>` (workers.py:233).

3. Concrete value with default config (verified by executing it in the Dune env): training_type='backbone', seeds=[0..4], resume=True, resunet/conv, and `RunNaming.compose(training_tag, 'fold_0/seed1')` = `resunet-conv-hungarian-K_5-hv-A-param_l1_1-covariance_match_0.05-coherence_resyn_0.05-cosine_curve_0.05_fold_0/seed1`. So the marker lands in `<run>/folds/resunet-conv-...-cosine_curve_0.05_fold_0/seed1/`, while the stage looks in `<run>/folds/fold_0/seed1/`.

Consequences all hold:
(a) `QueuedInferenceStage._training_complete` never sees a marker, so `FoldInferenceStage.run` (stages.py:111-115) reports every fold/split SKIPPED and CV inference never runs for backbone/jepa.
(b) `_is_complete` never sees one either, so resume=True retrains every fold and `_purge_unfinished` deletes the log-only `folds/fold_0/seed1` dir each time.
(c) `GpuQueue._launch` mkdirs the log parent (tools/orchestration/gpu_queue.py:316), creating `folds/fold_0/seedN/worker.log`. `TrialCollector._run_dirs` (trial_collection.py:179-192) walks `<run>/folds` and yields both `<tag>_fold_i/seedN` and the log-only `fold_i/seedN`; `FoldCollector._group_by_fold` groups on `FoldNaming.base`, producing two groups per fold index (2*n_folds base records), and `CrossValidationReport._require_all_folds` (cv_report.py:56-61) raises ValueError.
(d) `training_results.json` is keyed by the stage items (`fold_0/seed1`) while collected record names are `<tag>_fold_0/seed1`, so `record.training_result` is `{}` and `_fold_base_record` (workers.py:68-79) yields status PARTIAL, duration None.

Only training_type='profile_autoencoder' is coherent, since `fold_run_name` returns the bare fold there. Tests never exercise the divergence: tests/cross_validation/test_stages.py builds dirs literally named `fold_0`, and test_workers.py:234-238 asserts the tagged directory for the inference worker only (self-consistent within the worker). The tag prefix was introduced in commit 9965cd1 ("Name every training run model_head_matchingstrategy_lossfunction via a shared RunNaming") without updating the stage side. No symlink/rename reconciles the two, and `FoldTrainingStage`/`FoldInferenceStage` have no other subclass or override.
correction: Details are accurate; two refinements. (i) The exact prefix on defaults is the full curriculum-final loss tag, e.g. `resunet-conv-hungarian-K_5-hv-A-param_l1_1-covariance_match_0.05-coherence_resyn_0.05-cosine_curve_0.05_fold_0/seed1` (RunNaming.training_tag uses `curriculum.active_stages()[-1]`), not just the short stem quoted in the claim. (ii) The bug is one-sided: the workers are internally consistent and tested (FoldTrainingWorker and FoldInferenceWorker both use `fold_run_name`), so the divergence is in pipelines/cross_validation/stages.py, which must derive its item/paths from the same `fold_run_name` (or the naming must be dropped from the worker). The cited line 111 is the symptom site; the root cause lines are stages.py:22-25 and 53-56.

title: JEPA run summary stores the embedding dim as out_channels, so inference derives a bogus n_gaussians
description:
A JEPA run coupled to a profile autoencoder writes `out_channels = autoencoder_cfg.embedding_dim` into meta/run_summary.json (pipelines/jepa/training/pipeline.py:249,259). `JepaRunLoader` inherits `RunLoader.load`, which derives the Gaussian count purely from that field: `n_gaussians = out_channels_total // 3` (pipelines/backbone/inference/loader.py:213-215) and never reads the correctly-persisted `run_summary["n_gaussians"]`. The derived value is then used (a) to build the PatchDataset ground-truth channel selection and (b) as `run.n_gaussians` in `JepaCurvePredictor._forward_pass` (pipelines/jepa/inference/predictor.py:14,29-34), `JepaEmbeddingEvaluator._gt_curves` (pipelines/jepa/inference/embedding.py:22-28) and `Metrics(result, x_axis, run.n_gaussians)`.

With the shipped profile-autoencoder default `embedding_dim = 24` (configuration/architectures/profile_autoencoder.py:12) and the standard K=5 extraction, inference computes n_gaussians = 8 and PatchDataset aborts with a misleading message blaming the n_gaussians configuration. Worse, whenever `embedding_dim // 3 < K` (e.g. embedding_dim 12 with K=5) nothing raises: the GT curves are rebuilt from only the first 4 Gaussians and every JEPA curve metric, figure and report number is silently wrong.

No test exercises `JepaRunLoader.load` end to end (tests/jepa/test_inference.py builds fake Run objects with n_gaussians injected by hand), so the path is uncovered.
suggested_fix: Read `run_summary["n_gaussians"]` in `RunLoader.load` (falling back to out_channels//3 only for backbone runs that predate the field is not allowed by the no-legacy-fallback policy, so make it required), or override `load`/`_run_n_gaussians` in `JepaRunLoader` so the Gaussian count comes from the persisted `n_gaussians` rather than from the embedding width.
verdict_notes:
I reproduced the whole chain from source.

1. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/jepa/training/pipeline.py:249,259 — `backbone_out = self.autoencoder_cfg.embedding_dim if self.autoencoder_cfg is not None else self._gaussian_out_channels()` and that value is passed as `out_channels=` to `save_run_summary(...)`, while the correct K goes into the separate `n_gaussians=gaussian_cfg.n_default_gaussians` field. run_metadata.py:87-101 confirms both keys land in meta/run_summary.json.

2. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/jepa/inference/loader.py — `JepaRunLoader` overrides only `_image_frontend`, `_build_model`, `_wrap_model`. It does NOT override `load`.

3. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/loader.py:213-215 — `out_channels_total = int(run_summary["out_channels"]); n_gaussians = out_channels_total // 3`. `run_summary["n_gaussians"]` is never read anywhere in the loader (grep of n_gaussians in the inference package shows only the derived value and `dataset_creation_config.json`'s `payload["n_gaussians"]`, which is stored on DatasetConfig at line 98 but is not used to build the inference PatchDataset — line 232 passes the derived value).

4. That derived value flows to `_build_dataset(... n_gaussians=n_gaussians ...)` (line 232) and into `Run(n_gaussians=...)` (line 271), and from `run.n_gaussians` into JepaCurvePredictor._forward_pass (`gt_params_b[:, :n_K*3]`, reshape to (B, n_K, 3, H, W)), JepaEmbeddingEvaluator._gt_curves, and `Metrics(result, x_axis, run.n_gaussians)`.

5. Concrete failure with shipped defaults: profile AE `embedding_dim = 24` (configuration/architectures/profile_autoencoder.py:12) → n_gaussians = 8; a K=5 extraction gives gt_parameters with 15 channels; PatchDataset (pipelines/backbone/dataset/datasets.py:64-70) computes `selected_indices(8)` → max index 23, required 24 > available 15 → ValueError "Configured n_gaussians=8 indexes ground-truth parameter channel 23 but the dataset provides only 15 (5 Gaussians). Set n_gaussians to match the parameter extraction used for this dataset." — a misleading message pointing at the extraction config rather than at the run_summary field. This path runs for every profile-AE-coupled JEPA run: InferenceComponentsResolver.for_run returns JEPA_INFERENCE_COMPONENTS whenever a ProfileAutoencoderConfigIO file exists in meta (pipelines/shared/inference/inference_components.py:16-19), used by main/inference/infer_backbone.py, inference_dispatch, cross_validation/workers.py and by JEPA train-then-infer (pipelines/jepa/training/pipeline.py:330-333).

6. Coverage: tests/jepa/test_inference.py only builds loaders with `JepaRunLoader.__new__` and calls `_build_model`/`_wrap_model`; no test drives `load`, and no jepa test touches run_summary/out_channels. Confirmed uncovered.

The JepaParamRunLoader (image-AE-only) path is unaffected because `backbone_out` falls back to `_gaussian_out_channels()` there.
correction: The mechanism is right but the "silently wrong metrics" sub-case is narrower than the auditor states. Silent truncation needs embedding_dim // 3 < K. The profile AE embedding_dim is tuned over {16, 24, 32, 48} (configuration/architectures/profile_autoencoder.py:31), so with the standard K=5 the outcomes are: 16 → n_gaussians 5 (accidentally correct), 24/32/48 → 8/10/16 → loud but misleading PatchDataset crash. Silent GT truncation only happens for a manual embedding_dim below the tunable range (the auditor's 12-with-K=5 example) or for an extraction with K > embedding_dim//3 (e.g. K=6+ with embedding_dim 16). So in shipped configurations the realistic damage is that profile-AE-coupled JEPA inference is dead at the default embedding_dim=24 with a misleading error, not silent number corruption. The primary anchor is better cited as pipelines/backbone/inference/loader.py:214 (the derivation that ignores run_summary["n_gaussians"]), with pipelines/jepa/training/pipeline.py:249/259 as the origin of the overloaded field.

title: SwinUNet tuning search space offers embedding_dim values the model rejects
description: `SwinUNetConfig.num_heads` is fixed at `(2, 5, 10, 20)` (line 425) and `SwinUNet.__init__` computes stage dims as `embedding_dim * 2**i`, raising `ValueError` unless every stage dim is divisible by its head count (models/backbone/swin_unet.py:310-315). Stage 1 needs `2*embedding_dim % 5 == 0`, i.e. `embedding_dim` must be a multiple of 5. Of the four tunable choices `[48, 80, 96, 128]`, only 80 satisfies this, so 3 of 4 sampled trials construct an invalid model. `pipelines/tuning/tuners.py` calls `study.optimize(...)` with no `catch=`, so the raised ValueError propagates and kills the tuning worker rather than pruning the trial. swin_unet is included in the default tuning model list (`TuningEntryConfig.skip_models = []`, the scheduler enumerates the whole registry).
suggested_fix: Restrict the choices to multiples of 5 that keep every stage divisible (e.g. [40, 80, 120, 160]), or make `num_heads` part of the search space and validate the pair before returning the config.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced end to end from source, plus two live experiments.

1. Config (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/configuration/architectures/backbone.py): `SwinUNetConfig.num_heads` defaults to `[2, 5, 10, 20]` (line 425) and is NOT in `tunable_lr_params()` or `tunable_arch_params()`, so tuning never changes it. Line 461 offers `"embedding_dim": {"type": "categorical", "choices": [48, 80, 96, 128]}`.

2. Model (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/models/backbone/swin_unet.py:309-315): `dims = [embedding_dim * 2**i ...]` then `if dim % heads != 0: raise ValueError(...)`. Stage 1 needs `2*embedding_dim % 5 == 0`.

3. Live check in the Dune env, instantiating `SwinUNet(SwinUNetConfig())` with each tunable choice:
   48 -> ValueError "Stage 1: embedding dim (96) must be divisible by num_heads (5)"; 80 -> OK; 96 -> ValueError (192); 128 -> ValueError (256). So 3 of the 4 categorical values are unbuildable; the search dimension is effectively a single point.

4. Propagation: `Tuner._objective` (pipelines/tuning/tuners.py:105-136) constructs `self.model_config_cls()`, sets sampled params, and calls `TrialPipeline(...).run()` with no try/except; `Tuner.run` calls `study.optimize(self._objective, n_trials=..., gc_after_trial=True, callbacks=[self.best_writer])` (line 151) with no `catch=`. I confirmed with a live optuna run in the same env that a ValueError inside the objective is recorded as a FAIL trial and then re-raised out of `study.optimize`, so the worker process dies at its first offending sample (~75% chance on the very first trial). Only optuna's TrialPruned is handled (pipelines/tuning/trial.py), and that is for pruning, not invalid configs.

5. Reachability: swin_unet is in `BACKBONE_CONFIG_REGISTRY` (models/backbone/__init__.py:53), `TuningEntryConfig.training_type` defaults to "backbone" with `skip_models: list = []` (configuration/tuning/general.py:41-50), and `TuningScheduler._model_keys()` enumerates the whole registry crossed with `heads` (pipelines/tuning/pipeline.py:54-62). So a default `tune` sweep reaches swin_unet.

6. Why tests miss it: tests/models_backbone/_helpers.py:12 constructs swin_unet with an overridden `num_heads: [1, 2, 4, 8]` and `embedding_dim: 24`, so the default head list is never combined with the tuned embedding dims. tests/configuration/test_registries.py only checks that tunable keys are real dataclass fields, never that the sampled values build a model.

No refutation found: no sanitizer, no `__post_init__` fix-up, no head recomputation in ModelBuilder, and this is not one of the listed known non-issues (it is not a legacy-fallback or loud-breakage-by-design case; it is an internally inconsistent search space).
correction: Mechanism is as described; two refinements. (a) The concrete effect is that the tuning WORKER process exits non-zero at its first invalid sample, losing that worker's remaining trials; optuna still records the trial as FAIL, and `TuningScheduler._tune_model` then reports the model as PARTIAL/FAILED and moves on to the next model, so the whole sweep is not aborted — only swin_unet tuning is effectively unusable (and GPU worker slots are wasted). (b) The same broken space is also reached through `JepaTuner`, which uses `BACKBONE_CONFIG_REGISTRY` for its model config (pipelines/tuning/workers.py:96-105), so training_type "jepa" with swin_unet fails identically. Minimal fix: restrict the choices to multiples of 5 (e.g. [80, 160, 240]) or make `num_heads` derived from `embedding_dim`; independently, `study.optimize(..., catch=(ValueError,))` would stop invalid samples from killing workers.

title: Model Probe passes WebLogger into RunLoader, which requires the project Logger API — the Microscope tab can never load a run
description: `ModelProbe._load_worker` calls `RunLoader(Path(run_path), logger=self.logger)` where `self.logger` is the `WebLogger` instance created in `web_ui_server.py:68`. `RunLoader.load()` immediately calls `self.logger.section(...)` (pipelines/backbone/inference/loader.py:200), then `subsection`, `kv_table`, and passes the same logger down into `Layout` and `Cropper`. `WebLogger` only defines `info/ok/warning/error/muted/banner` and has no `__getattr__` fallback, so every load raises `AttributeError: 'WebLogger' object has no attribute 'section'`. The exception is swallowed by the broad `except Exception` at line 101 and surfaced as a generic error status, so the failure looks like a bad run directory rather than a wiring bug. tests/webui/test_model_probe.py never exercises this path — it injects `probe.loaded` directly and uses a `_SilentLogger` stub with `__getattr__`, which is exactly why the defect is invisible to the suite. Fix by constructing the real `tools.monitoring.logger.Logger` for the pipeline call (or by adding the section/subsection/kv_table surface to WebLogger).
suggested_fix: Build a real `Logger` inside `_load_worker` for the RunLoader/Layout/Cropper call chain, and keep `WebLogger` only for the webui-facing status messages. Add a test that drives `_load_worker` against a fixture run directory instead of pre-populating `probe.loaded`.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced directly from source and by execution.

1. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/web_ui_server.py:68 creates `self.logger = WebLogger()` and line 104 passes it into `ModelProbe(self.paths, self.logger)`.
2. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/model_probe.py:57 does `RunLoader(Path(run_path), logger=self.logger).load(...)`. `RunLoader.__init__` is typed `logger: Logger` (tools.monitoring.logger.Logger).
3. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/loader.py:200 — the very first statement of `RunLoader.load()` — is `self.logger.section("[Inference: Load Run]")`, followed by `subsection` (line 201) and several `kv_table` calls; the same logger is also handed to `Stats.load`, `Layout`, `Cropper`.
4. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/web_logger.py is 51 lines total and defines only `info/ok/warning/error/muted/banner` plus `_emit`; there is no `section`, `subsection`, `kv_table`, and no `__getattr__` fallback. Verified at runtime: `hasattr(WebLogger(), 'section') -> False`.
5. Executed the real path with the Dune env: `RunLoader(Path('/nonexistent/run'), logger=WebLogger()).load(split='test', ...)` raises `AttributeError: 'WebLogger' object has no attribute 'section'` — and it raises before any filesystem access, so it fails identically for every run directory, valid or not. The POST route /api/probe/load (webui/request_router.py:655) and webui/static/js/microscope.js:193 confirm this is the only entry point the Microscope tab has, so the tab can never reach a "ready" state.
6. tests/webui/test_model_probe.py never calls `start_load`/`_load_worker`; all three tests build `ModelProbe(ProjectPaths(), _SilentLogger())` (a stub with `__getattr__` returning a no-op) and assign `probe.loaded` by hand, so the suite cannot see this. model_probe.py:57 is also the only place in webui/ that passes a WebLogger into a pipeline component requiring the project Logger API (the only other `self.logger` hand-off, `GpuPoolFile` in process_manager.py:682, uses `info` only).

This is not covered by any of the known non-issues: it is a live wiring defect, not a legacy-fallback or dynamic-dispatch artifact.
correction: Two details in the claim are slightly off. (a) The failure is not truly "swallowed and surfaced as a generic error": webui/model_probe.py:104 formats the status error as f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}", so the frontend hint (microscope.js `_pollStatus`) displays the literal text "AttributeError: 'WebLogger' object has no attribute 'section'" — misleading in that it looks like a probe bug rather than pointing at the wiring, but it is not disguised as a bad run directory. (b) The AttributeError fires at loader.py:200 before any file is read, so the tab fails for every input path, not only for real runs; the fix is either constructing a real tools.monitoring.logger.Logger inside _load_worker or extending WebLogger with section/subsection/kv_table.

title: training.snapshot_every_n_epochs is read from the entry config but never reaches the trainer
description: `TrainingQueueConfig.snapshot_every_n_epochs` is an entry-level knob: it is a dataclass field (configuration/training/general/run.py:49), it is claimed by the webui launch form (webui/launch_layout.py:217), it is documented in webui/config_descriptions.json, and main/analysis/animate_training.py plus pipelines/backbone/inference/training_evolution.py:57 both tell the user to "train with snapshot_every_n_epochs > 0". But `ConfigFactory.training_trainer_config` (the only place `TrainingLoopConfig` is constructed outside tests) does not forward it, so `BaseTrainer._maybe_snapshot` (tools/training/trainer.py:364) always reads the `TrainingLoopConfig` default of 0. Setting it on the backbone or dual entry silently does nothing and no epoch snapshots are ever written. Affects both configuration/training/backbone.py and configuration/training/dual.py entries.

                epochs                      = training.epochs,
                validation_frequency        = training.validation_frequency,
                use_amp                     = training.use_amp,
                gradient_accumulation_steps = training.gradient_accumulation_steps,
suggested_fix: Add `snapshot_every_n_epochs = training.snapshot_every_n_epochs` to the TrainingLoopConfig construction in ConfigFactory.training_trainer_config, and add a test asserting the entry value round-trips into trainer.config.training.

ConfigCli overrides apply to the entry config path and no generic field-copy bridges queue -> loop; the AE pipelines' `inherit_shared_from(base)` just carries the already-defaulted loop config forward. title: Reach capacity check builds the arms with the registry default out_channels, not the run's Gaussian count
description: `ReachTrialPlanner._parameters` instantiates each rung with `in_channels` and `head` but never passes `out_channels`, so every backbone config falls back to its registry default of 6 (configuration/architectures/backbone.py: `out_channels : int = 6`, i.e. K=2). Training instead builds each arm with `GaussianHead.total_channels(ppg, n_default_gaussians)` derived from the dataset (pipelines/backbone/training/pipeline.py:198). For the `set_pred` head the output stage is `n_gaussians` PixelMLPs of size `embedding_channels x (embedding_channels//2)` plus an existence head (models/blocks.py:351), so its parameter count scales with K and with each arm's very different `embedding_channels` (the default rungs are local_cnn features=479 vs unet). The 1% `match_tolerance` is therefore verified against a model that is not the one trained whenever n_gaussians != 2. The asymmetry is clearly unintended: `_validate` explicitly guards `in_channels` with the message "training builds every arm at the dataset width, so the capacity check would count the wrong first layer", but says nothing about the output width.
suggested_fix: Thread the resolved out_channels (ppg * n_default_gaussians) into ReachTrialPlanner from the launcher, pass it to get_backbone in _parameters, and validate it against the configured Gaussian count the same way in_channels is validated.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source and numerically.

1. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/training/experiments.py:444 — `ReachTrialPlanner._parameters` calls `get_backbone(rung["backbone"], in_channels=self.trials.in_channels, head=self.head, **sizing, **self._overrides(rung))`. No `out_channels`, and the default rungs (`_default_reach_rungs`, configuration/training/backbone.py:109-113) carry only `features`/`dropout`/`trunk_wd`, so every arm is built at the registry default `out_channels = 6` (configuration/architectures/backbone.py), i.e. K=2.

2. Training builds at the dataset's K: pipelines/backbone/training/pipeline.py:197-201 sets `out_channels = GaussianHead.total_channels(ppg, gaussian_cfg.n_default_gaussians)` and pipeline.py:128-132 `_model_overrides` forces `out_channels` into the model config. `n_default_gaussians` is not a config constant — GaussianConfig.from_dataset reads `k_max` from param_extraction_meta.json, so K=5 runs are routine (K=2|K=5 are both project standards).

3. Head parameters scale with K for every head except "none": `_resolve_gaussian_layout` derives `n_gaussians = out_channels // ppg`, and `_build_set_prediction_heads` (models/blocks.py:349-353) builds K PixelMLPs of embedding_channels x max(E//2,16) plus an existence head. The default head is `backbone_head = "set_pred"` (configuration/training/backbone.py:227).

4. Measured with the repo's own code (Dune env, default reach rungs, patch (32,32), in_channels 9):
   - set_pred: K=2 -> {cnn33: 31,374,744, unet: 31,047,530}, deviation 1.054 %; K=5 -> {cnn33: 31,721,787, unet: 31,054,169}, deviation 2.150 %.
   - conv: K=2 0.032 %, K=5 0.020 % (small, but still a different model than the one checked).
   Concrete false pass: local_cnn features [477]*8 vs the default unet rung gives 0.213 % at K=2 (planner accepts, tolerance 1 %) but 1.299 % at K=5, i.e. the arms actually trained are outside tolerance and the guard never fires. The mirror case exists too: features [474]*8 is rejected at 1.052 % while the trained K=5 pair matches to 0.035 %.

5. The asymmetry is clearly unintended: `_validate` (experiments.py:433-434) explicitly refuses a mismatched `in_channels` with "training builds every arm at the dataset width, so the capacity check would count the wrong first layer", while the output width is left at the registry default.

Tests (tests/backbone_training/test_experiments.py:373-440) all pass head="conv" and never exercise a non-default K, so nothing encodes the omitted output width as intended; the 9 reach tests currently pass, so this is not the known pre-existing reach size-match test failure, and it is not covered by any listed known non-issue.
correction: Scope is wider than stated: the same omission exists in `DualReachTrialPlanner._parameters` (pipelines/dual/training/experiments.py:57-77), which calls `get_dual(...)` with `params_overrides`/`existence_overrides` that also never carry `out_channels`, while pipelines/dual/training/pipeline.py:72-79 inherits the backbone `_model_overrides` and forces the dataset-derived `out_channels` at train time. Also worth noting the effect is not confined to set_pred: conv, multihead and per_gaussian heads all size their output stage from `out_channels // params_per_gaussian`, so all of them are counted at K=2 (the magnitude is just much smaller for conv). Line 444 and the described mechanism are otherwise accurate; severity major stands (the capacity match is the entire premise of the reach experiment, and the check can both false-pass and false-reject).

title: GT μ/σ are NaN-masked before metrics, so every "inactive" per-slot GT statistic is NaN and "global" silently equals "active"
description: `Predictor._finalize_results` overwrites μ and σ of every GT slot whose amplitude is below `ACTIVE_AMP_THR` with NaN (lines 312-316). `Metrics._param_population_stats` (metrics.py:325-350) then computes per-slot statistics for the scopes `active` / `inactive` / `global` and filters with `vals = values[mask & np.isfinite(values)]`. Because the inactive μ/σ entries are NaN, `slot_k_mu_inactive_gt_mean`, `slot_k_sig_inactive_gt_*` are always NaN, and `slot_k_{mu,sig}_global_gt_*` collapse to exactly the `active` values — the `global` row is a duplicate, not a global average. Report §2.5 (report.py:338-347) explicitly states "GT columns average the ground-truth parameter maps directly, so the inactive rows expose the placeholder fill and the active-vs-global gap shows how much it dilutes unconditioned averages", which this data path can never deliver. The unit test `tests/backbone_inference/test_metrics.py::test_param_population_stats_active_inactive_global_means` passes only because it feeds a hand-built GT with 0.0 placeholders instead of the NaN-masked cube the pipeline actually produces, so the regression is invisible to the suite. Only the `amp` rows (channel 3k, not masked) carry real inactive/global numbers.
evidence:
params_gt_cube[3 * k + 1][mask_gt] = np.nan
            params_gt_cube[3 * k + 2][mask_gt] = np.nan
suggested_fix: Either stop NaN-masking the GT parameter cube inside the predictor (keep the placeholder fill and let consumers mask), or drop the `inactive`/`global` scopes for μ/σ and update the §2.5 narrative to say only the active population is measurable. Add a metrics test that runs on a NaN-masked GT cube so the intent is pinned.

1. `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/predictor.py:311-316` — inside `_finalize_results`, after `finalize_cube()` and before anything consumes the cube, every GT slot whose amplitude is not `> ParamMatcher.ACTIVE_AMP_THR` has channels `3k+1` (mu) and `3k+2` (sig) overwritten with `np.nan`. The amplitude channel `3k` is untouched. The masked array is what goes into `Result.params_gt` (line 351) and into `params_gt.npy` (line 329).

2. `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/pipeline.py:114` builds `Metrics(result, ...)` from exactly that returned `Result`, so `Metrics._param_population_stats` sees the masked cube. There is no re-read of an unmasked source.

3. `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/metrics.py:332-348` — `finite`/`active`/`inactive` are derived from the GT *amplitude* channel, but the per-parameter filter is `vals = values[mask & np.isfinite(values)]`. For `param in ("mu","sig")` the GT values are NaN exactly on the `inactive` set, so: `inactive` -> `vals.size == 0` -> NaN; `global` (mask = `finite` over amp) -> reduces to the active subset.

4. Repro with the pipeline's own masking rule applied to the test's fixture (script at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-bard/bc79d8b1-4642-451c-ada3-6efc2657779a/scratchpad/repro.py, run under the Dune env):
   slot_0_amp_active/inactive/global_gt_mean = 2.0 / 0.0 / 1.0 (amp is fine)
   slot_0_mu_active/inactive/global_gt_mean = 10.0 / nan / 10.0
   slot_0_sig_active/inactive/global_gt_mean = 4.0 / nan / 4.0
   slot_0_mu_active_gt_std == slot_0_mu_global_gt_std == 0.0
   i.e. the GT `global` row is byte-identical to the `active` row for mu and sig, and the GT `inactive` row is always NaN.

The test `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/backbone_inference/test_metrics.py:276-304` asserts `slot_0_mu_global_gt_mean == 5.0` (10.0 averaged with the 0.0 placeholder over half the pixels) — only reachable with an unmasked GT cube. It hand-builds `gt` with 0.0 placeholders and never applies the predictor's NaN mask, so it encodes the intended semantics while the production path cannot produce them. The auditor's characterisation of the test is accurate.

6. Report prose at `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/report.py:338-347` states the GT columns "average the ground-truth parameter maps directly, so the inactive rows expose the placeholder fill and the active-vs-global gap shows how much it dilutes unconditioned averages" — for mu/sig the gap is structurally zero and the inactive cell is structurally blank, so a reader is invited to conclude "no dilution" from a row that carries no information.

Refutation attempts that failed: the mask is not undone anywhere (grep of `params_gt` across pipelines/backbone/inference); Metrics is not fed an unmasked cube; denormalization is affine/log1p-invertible so physically-zero GT amplitudes come back as ~0 and the active/inactive split is genuinely non-degenerate; the NaN does not corrupt other GT consumers (`_matched_gaussian_metrics` metrics.py:366-368 and `FailureModes.pair_predictions` failure_modes.py:41-42 gate everything on `act_gt`, and NaN comparisons are False).

Severity: no training, checkpoint, or headline-metric value is wrong — every number printed is a correctly computed mean over the finite values present; the harm is confined to two structurally uninformative rows per slot in the diagnostic report plus a prose claim they cannot support. That is minor rather than major, though it is borderline because the duplicated "global" row silently invites a false "the placeholder does not dilute anything" reading.

title: The permutation-search Gaussian assignment is recomputed ~9 times over the full stitched cube in one inference run
description: `GaussianMatcher.assignment` is an O(K! · n_pixels) chunked permutation search over the whole (H×W) split region. Within `Metrics.compute` alone it runs four times on identical inputs: `_active_count_stats` (metrics.py:283, via `aligned_prediction`), `_param_population_stats` (metrics.py:329, via `aligned_prediction`), `_matched_gaussian_metrics` (metrics.py:357), and `_slot_organization_stats` (metrics.py:461, via `SlotOrganization.assignment_matrix`). The figure stage repeats it five more times on the same `params_pred`/`params_gt`: plots/param.py:29, 170, 232, 279 and plots/organization.py:140. For the default test split (azimuth 14564-16000 × range 500-4000 ≈ 5.0M pixels) with K=5 this is nine full 120-permutation sweeps producing byte-identical results.
suggested_fix: Compute `sel = GaussianMatcher().assignment(...)` and the aligned prediction once (e.g. in `Predictor._finalize_results`, stored on `Result`), and have `Metrics`, `SlotOrganization` and the parameter plotters accept the precomputed assignment instead of re-deriving it.

Reproduced from source and measured.

Mechanism. `GaussianMatcher.assignment` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tools/metrics/gaussian_matching.py:26-49) is a stateless, deterministic brute-force permutation search: it builds `perms = list(permutations(range(n_K)))` (K! = 120 for K=5) and, per 250k-pixel chunk, evaluates `np.stack([cost[:, idx, perm].sum(axis=1) for perm in perms], axis=1).argmin(axis=1)`. `aligned_prediction` (line 51) calls `assignment` internally. No caching or memoization exists anywhere on the class or module.

Call sites in one backbone inference run (all on the identical stitched `result.params_pred` / `result.params_gt`; `result.params_pred[: n_K*3]` in figures.py is a no-op slice because loader.py:214-215 sets `out_channels = 3 * n_gaussians`, so the arrays are byte-identical):
- pipelines/backbone/inference/metrics.py:283 `_active_count_stats` (via aligned_prediction)
- metrics.py:329 `_param_population_stats` (via aligned_prediction)
- metrics.py:357 `_matched_gaussian_metrics`
- metrics.py:461 `_slot_organization_stats` -> SlotOrganization.assignment_matrix -> assignment (slot_organization.py:51; same default amp_threshold = ParamMatcher.ACTIVE_AMP_THR, so identical result)
- pipelines/backbone/inference/failure_modes.py:32 (invoked unconditionally from pipeline.py:282 `_classify_failures` whenever param cubes exist) — MISSED BY THE AUDITOR
- plots/param.py:29, 170, 232, 279 (figures.py:194, 201, 208, 217 — all four run unconditionally in `_compose_param_plots`)
- plots/organization.py:140 (figures.py:250, same default threshold)

That is 10 identical full-region permutation sweeps, not 9. All four metrics.py calls happen inside a single `Metrics.compute` (metrics.py:507-511, called once at pipeline.py:114 with `param_space=self.components.param_space`).

Measured cost. Benchmarked the real `GaussianMatcher` from the repo in the Dune env on the default test split shape (azimuth 14564-16000 x range 500-4000 = 1436 x 3500 = 5,026,000 pixels), K=5: `assignment` = 9.60 s, `aligned_prediction` = 11.25 s. So ~96-100 s per inference run, of which ~87-90 s is pure duplicate work producing byte-identical output. Scaling is factorial in K as claimed (K=2: 0.30 s, K=3: 0.72 s), so the waste is negligible for the K=2 arm and real only for K=5.

Severity adjustment. The claim is factually correct, but this is a once-per-trained-run offline analysis stage, not a training step, per-epoch loop, or per-request handler. The same inference pipeline also runs full-cube SSIM over every elevation/range/azimuth slice under a ProcessPoolExecutor and writes hundreds of figures, so ~90 s is a real but non-dominant fraction. It multiplies across batched trial/seed inference (infer_at_end), which is what keeps it worth fixing. (1) The count is 10, not 9: the auditor missed pipelines/backbone/inference/failure_modes.py:32, which calls `GaussianMatcher().assignment(self.params_pred, self.params_gt, n_K)` on the same arrays and is invoked unconditionally from pipeline.py:282 whenever parameter cubes exist. (2) The cost is factorial in K, so the impact is configuration-dependent: measured 9.60 s per `assignment` (11.25 s per `aligned_prediction`) at K=5 on the 5.03M-pixel default test split, but only 0.30 s at K=2. title: _slice_ssim materialises float64 copies of every slice along all three axes before submitting any work
description: `_enqueue_tasks` appends `p_sl.astype(np.float64)` and `r_sl.astype(np.float64)` for every index it is given, and the pipeline passes `all_elev_idx`, `all_range_idx` and `all_az_idx` (pipeline.py:114-119), i.e. every slice on every axis. The `tasks` list therefore holds 2 (pred+ref) × 3 (axes) × cube_elements float64 values — 48 bytes per cube element — fully resident in the parent process before `ProcessPoolExecutor` is even created, and each is then pickled again into a worker. With the default test split (≈1436 × 3500 pixels) and ~100 elevation bins that is ~24 GB of transient float64 for a 2 GB float32 cube, and `_slice_ssim` is invoked three times per run (`gt`, `norm` in `compute`, `red` in `reduced_comparison`). The float64 upcast is not needed either — `skimage.metrics.structural_similarity` works on float32.
suggested_fix: Pass only `(key, axis, index)` to the workers and have them slice from a shared-memory / memmapped view of the cube, or at minimum keep the slices in the cube's native float32 and submit in bounded batches instead of enqueueing every slice up front.

Every element of both the pred and ref cubes is therefore duplicated as float64 once per axis: 2 arrays x 3 axes x 8 bytes = 48 bytes per cube element, fully resident before ProcessPoolExecutor is created at line 198. `worker_args` at line 195 only re-references those arrays, so there is no second copy, but both lists stay alive for the whole `with` block, so the peak is not amortised by the executor's bounded call queue.

The caller does pass every index: pipeline.py:108-110 builds all_elev_idx/all_range_idx/all_az_idx as np.arange over the full cube, and both _evaluate_metrics (114-119) and _synthesize_reduced (160-165) pass those rather than the 5-element slice_*_idx derived from n_elevation_slices/n_range_slices/n_azimuth_slices (default 5, configuration/inference/general.py:58-60).

Default test split is azimuth (14564, 16000) = 1436 lines (configuration/training/general/run.py:77) by range 500-4000 = 3500 samples (configuration/sar/processing_config.py:139-142), and the npy header of the local dataset twin (test_data/data/tomogram_full.npy: shape (150, 1000, 500)) gives 150 elevation bins. So N ~ 7.5e8 elements, the float32 cube is ~3.0 GB, and `tasks` holds ~36 GB of float64 - 12x the cube - in the parent process.

The float64 upcast is not required: skimage.metrics.structural_similarity accepts float32 and data_range is passed explicitly at line 243, so no dtype-range inference is involved. Even if float64 were wanted for variance-cancellation reasons, the cast belongs inside _ssim_worker (line 238) rather than in the parent.

This is not one of the listed known non-issues, and it is not a genuinely cold path: inference runs per (config, seed) and is batched over all trials by infer_at_end, and _slice_ssim is entered three times per run (gt, norm, red). Computing SSIM for every slice is itself intentional - the per-slice keys ssim_{prefix}_{axis}_{i} feed figures.py:433-435 plot_ssim_curves, and Report._is_per_slice_ssim exists to filter them out of report tables - so the finding is correctly scoped to the eager float64 materialisation, not to the all-slices policy.

Line 139 calls `PhysicalLoss.coherence_resynthesis_pp_map`, which (tools/loss/physical_loss.py lines 147-151) loops over all tracks computing `gp = synthesise_track(pred, kz[:,t])/p0c` and `gt = synthesise_track(target, kz[:,t])/t0c`, accumulates `|gp-gt|^2`, and returns only the track-mean plus the mask — the per-track terms are discarded. 2T steering evaluations.
2. Lines 152-154 recompute exactly the same `gp`/`gs` in an explicit per-track loop (same `p0c`/`t0c`, computed identically at lines 146-147 versus 142-143). Another 2T evaluations.
3. Lines 164-167 call `_synth_unit` (line 105-108) for both `gt_t` and `pred_t` on every non-reference track: a third `synthesise_track` per source. Another 2(T-1) evaluations.

Numerical check in the Dune env confirms both redundancies are exact:
- `gamma/(|gamma|+1e-30)` vs `gp/(|gp|+1e-30)` with `gp = gamma/p0c`: max abs diff 1.3e-07 (float32 rounding only) — since `p0c`/`t0c` are real and clamped at `physics_floor > 0`, `_synth_unit` needs no new steering evaluation at all.
- `coherence_resynthesis_pp_map(...)[0]` vs the mean over tracks of `(gp-gs).abs()**2` built in the explicit loop: max abs diff 0.0 — the line-139 call is exactly the track-mean of what the loop already produces, and `mask` is just `(t0 > floor)`.

So per chunk the coherence branch performs 6T-2 steering syntheses where 2T suffice (T=5 tracks: 28 instead of 10). Alongside the covariance branch's T(T+1) pair syntheses (30 at T=5), the stage does ~58 large complex tensor builds per chunk instead of ~40, i.e. roughly 45% avoidable extra GPU work, scaling with the whole cube.

Tests (tests/backbone_inference/test_data_consistency.py) assert only output metrics (zero error on identical curves, per-track metric presence, sign detection), so deduplication would not change any locked behavior. None of the KNOWN NON-ISSUES apply.
correction:
Two details in the claim need adjusting. (a) The magnitude is understated for the coherence branch and overstated for the stage: the coherence branch is roughly tripled (6T-2 vs 2T syntheses), but because `covariance_matching_pp_map` (T(T+1) pair syntheses, 30 at T=5) dominates the stage, total savings are ~30-45% of the data-consistency stage, not a doubling of the whole physics path. (b) The removable call is line 139, not lines 152-154: `coherence_resynthesis_pp_map` returns only the track-mean, so the per-track breakdown at 152-158 cannot be derived from it — the clean fix is to keep the explicit loop, set `coherence_map[a0:a1]` to the mean of the per-track `err` arrays, compute `mask` locally as `t0 > floor`, and replace `_synth_unit` with `gp/(gp.abs()+eps)` / `gs/(gs.abs()+eps)`.

Severity: this is a one-shot whole-cube evaluation executed once per inference run (pipelines/backbone/inference/pipeline.py `_evaluate_data_consistency`, default `compute_data_consistency=True`), not a training step, per-epoch loop, or per-request handler. Real but cold-ish, hence minor rather than major.

title: Every patch's rendered curves for the whole split are held in RAM simultaneously before stitching
description: `_compute_metrics` submits one task per batch for the entire dataset at once and keeps every worker result alive in `results` until `_stitch_results` consumes them. Each result contains `pred_curves` and `gt_curves` at full patch resolution, so the peak footprint is (overlap factor) × 2 × cube size — with the standard (64,32) patch / (32,16) stride the overlap factor is 4, giving ~8 stitched-cube-equivalents of float32 resident at once, on top of `all_pred_params`/`all_gt_params` which are also retained from `_forward_pass`. Nothing is released incrementally even though `add_patch` could consume each batch as it completes.
evidence: futures = {pool.submit(Predictor._cpu_worker, t): i for i, t in enumerate(tasks)}
suggested_fix: Stitch inside the `as_completed` loop (keep only the batch indices needed to place each patch) and drop each result after `add_patch`, or bound the number of in-flight futures to a small multiple of `cpu_workers`.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. In pipelines/backbone/inference/predictor.py, _compute_metrics (lines 197-213) submits one task per batch for the whole split in a single dict comprehension (line 207) and stores every completed payload in results[idx] (line 210); the list is returned intact and only consumed in _stitch_results (line 267), staying alive through _finalize_results while the four output cubes are materialised. Each payload contains pred_curves and gt_curves at full patch resolution — GaussianReconstructor.reconstruct_batch returns (B, n_elev, ph, pw) float32 (tools/data/gaussians.py:80-87). With the project defaults patch_size=(64,32)/stride=(32,16) (configuration/training/general/run.py:73-74) the patch grid oversamples by 2048/512 = 4x, so the resident curve payload is 4 x 2 = 8 stitched-cube-equivalents, matching the claim. Concrete scale: test_data/data/dataset.json crop 1000x500 with a 600 MB tomogram implies profile_length 300, and the default test split (test_azimuth 14564-16000 = 1436 lines x crop range width ~500) gives ~0.86 GB per cube, i.e. ~7 GB resident in `results` plus ~1.7 GB of finalized curve cubes alive at the same moment. The design intent to bound memory is explicit elsewhere in the same file: CubeStitcher/SelectStitcher take memmap_path and save_cubes defaults to True in configuration/inference/backbone.py, so the 1-cube accumulators go to disk while the 8-cube worker buffer stays in RAM. Incremental consumption is trivially available: futures[fut] already yields the task index i and all_indices[i] gives the patch indices, so the stitchers could be built before the pool and add_patch called inside the as_completed loop. No test encodes the batch-at-once behaviour (tests/backbone_inference/test_predictor.py uses a single 16x16 batch), and this is not one of the listed known non-issues. Only qualification: this is a per-run path rather than a per-step loop, and the retained all_pred_params/all_gt_params are only ~0.2 cube-equivalents (15 channels vs 300), so they are a minor term, not co-equal as the description implies.
correction: Line and mechanism are correct (predictor.py:197-213, evidence line 207). Refinements: (1) the peak is ~8 cube-equivalents of curves plus ~2 more once _finalize_results materialises pred/gt cubes while `results` is still referenced, not 8 total; (2) all_pred_params/all_gt_params contribute only ~0.2 cube-equivalents (3K=15 channels vs n_elev~300), so they are a marginal term rather than a comparable one; (3) the strongest supporting evidence is the memmap_path option on CubeStitcher/SelectStitcher with save_cubes=True by default — the file already offloads the 1-cube accumulators to disk while holding the 8-cube worker buffer in RAM; (4) the same accumulate-everything pattern is inherited by JepaCurvePredictor (pipelines/jepa/inference/predictor.py:14-42), which builds the curve lists in the forward pass; (5) this is a once-per-run path, so the cost is a multi-GB RAM peak (aggravated by per-(config,seed) inference fan-out and infer_at_end batching), not repeated CPU waste.

title: CKA loads every selected run fully into memory at once
description: `CkaComparison.run` materializes all runs before collecting any features. Each `Run` returned by `RunLoader.load` carries the whole split's complex input stack (`complex_inputs = arrays["inputs"]`) and the whole raw tomogram cube (`full_curves = arrays["tomogram"]`, loaded unconditionally by `loader._build_dataset` via `cropper.load_split(region, load_tomogram=True)`), plus its own `PatchDataset` and `DataLoader` over the same underlying data. For a typical split region (n_elev x H x W float32) that is gigabytes per run; with `selector.all()` selecting a dozen runs the process OOMs. None of that payload is used by CKA — `_collect` only needs `run.model.module` and `run.loader`, and `_validate_alignment` only needs `split_region` / `dataset_config` metadata.
evidence:
runs     = [self._load(run_dir) for run_dir in run_dirs]
        self._validate_alignment(runs)
suggested_fix: Load, validate, collect features, and release one run at a time (features are small); or validate alignment from the metadata JSONs first and then stream `for run_dir in run_dirs: run = self._load(run_dir); features.append(self._collect(run)); del run`.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source.

1. `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/representation_cka.py:208` — `runs = [self._load(run_dir) for run_dir in run_dirs]` builds every selected run before line 209 validates alignment and before line 212 collects features. The `runs` list stays referenced for the whole `run()` body, so all N runs are alive at once; nothing frees a run after `_collect`.

2. `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/loader.py:143` — `RunLoader._build_dataset` calls `cropper.load_split(region, load_tomogram=True)` with the flag hardcoded; `load()` exposes no way to skip it (grep for `load_tomogram` shows exactly one call site, and `Cropper.load_split` defaults to False elsewhere). `Cropper._load_tomogram` (`pipelines/backbone/dataset/spatial.py:84-86`) does `np.ascontiguousarray(np.abs(tomogram[:, az, rg]).astype(np.float32))`, i.e. a real in-RAM materialization of the whole split cube, not a memmap view. `Run.full_curves` (loader.py:283) keeps it alive for the lifetime of the Run.

3. CKA never touches it: `_collect` (lines 149-182) uses only `run.model.module` and `run.loader`, `_probe_layers` only the module, `_validate_alignment` only `run.split_region` / `run.dataset_config`.

Size check with the project's own defaults: global crop az 1000-16000, rg 500-4000 (`configuration/sar/processing_config.py:139-143`), test split az 14564-16000 (`configuration/training/general/run.py:77`) → 1436 x 3500 ≈ 5.0e6 pixels. `test_data/data/tomogram_full.npy` is 600 MB for 5e5 pixels → 300 elevation bins, so the test-split tomogram is ~5.0e6 x 300 x 4 B ≈ 6.0 GB per run, versus ~0.36 GB for the 9-layer complex input stack and ~0.3 GB for K=5 parameters. The unused tomogram is ~90% of each Run's footprint, and only ~32 patches (batch_size 4 x max_batches 4, `configuration/diagnostics.py:307-308`) are ever consumed.

Reachability: `_select_runs` falls back to `selector.all()` whenever stdin is not a tty (line 113-116), which is exactly how the webui launches it (`webui/script_catalog.py:170`, `webui/launch_layout.py:1355` — the run filter is an optional multi-select). `RunSelector.all()` rglobs every `best_model.pt` under `runs_dir`, so a dozen-plus runs is the normal case, i.e. tens of GB of RAM for data the tool never reads. The all-up-front ordering also means a misaligned-runs `ValueError` at line 209 is paid only after every run is fully loaded.

Tests (`tests/backbone_inference/test_representation_cka.py`) cover only `CkaComputation` math; nothing encodes the eager-load ordering as intended behaviour. Not one of the listed known non-issues.
correction:
Mechanism needs two corrections. (a) `complex_inputs` is not extra memory: it is the same object `PatchDataset` stores as `self.inputs` (loader.py:152/280, datasets.py:33) and the DataLoader genuinely reads from it, as it does the `parameters` array. The dominant *unused* payload is `full_curves` / `arrays["tomogram"]` alone — roughly 300 elevation bins x split pixels x 4 B, ~6 GB per run at production crop, ~90% of a Run. (b) The waste is therefore two separate things: per-run dead weight (the tomogram, fixable with a `load_tomogram` parameter on `RunLoader.load`) multiplied by N because CKA is the only RunLoader consumer that holds several Runs simultaneously (fixable by loading, collecting features, and dropping each run inside one loop, keeping only the small `split_region`/`patch`/`stride` metadata for `_validate_alignment`). Also worth noting the eager list means the alignment error at line 209 fires only after paying the full N-run load.

Severity: keeping "major" — this is not throughput waste on a cold path but a memory blow-up that scales linearly with the number of runs and can OOM the process on the tool's own default non-tty `selector.all()` path, which is how the webui launches it.

title: Paper figure pack silently drops every vector figure it tells you to generate
description: `PaperFigurePackConfig.patterns` matches only `*.png` (`["pixel_maps/*.png", "param_scatter/*.png", "stratified/*.png", "profiles/*.png", "data_consistency/*.png"]`, configuration/diagnostics.py), while `PlotBase._save` (tools/reporting/plotting.py:100) rewrites the extension to `.pdf` whenever `PlotBase.style == "paper"` and the figure contains no raster axes: `if PlotBase.style == "paper" and path.suffix == ".png" and not any(ax.images for ax in fig.axes): path = path.with_suffix(".pdf")`. Every line/scatter figure (profiles, param_scatter, stratified, most data_consistency curves) therefore lands as `.pdf` and is skipped by the glob. Because `pixel_maps/*.png` (imshow figures) still match, `_collect_run` does not raise — the pack silently ships only the raster maps. The manifest note explicitly instructs the user into exactly this failure mode.
evidence: "note"       : "Figures are copied as rendered by each run's inference; re-run inference with figure_style=paper for publication styling before packing.",
suggested_fix: Make the patterns extension-agnostic (`pixel_maps/*`, `param_scatter/*`, ...) or glob both suffixes per pattern, and assert per-pattern that at least one file matched so a style/extension mismatch fails loudly instead of thinning the pack.
verdict_notes:
I reproduced the claim independently.

1. `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tools/reporting/plotting.py:99-101` — `PlotBase._save` does exactly what the auditor quotes: `if PlotBase.style == "paper" and path.suffix == ".png" and not any(ax.images for ax in fig.axes): path = path.with_suffix(".pdf")`. This is intended behaviour, encoded in tests: `tests/reporting/test_plotting.py:437` `test_paper_save_upgrades_line_plot_to_pdf` asserts `out == tmp_path / "line.pdf"`, and `test_paper_save_keeps_png_for_images` asserts imshow figures stay `.png`.

2. The figures that land in the packed subdirectories are line/scatter figures with no `AxesImage`:
   - `pipelines/backbone/inference/plots/slice.py:17-73` `plot_profiles` — only `ax.plot`, saved to `figures/profiles/*.png` (`figures.py:99-106`).
   - `pipelines/backbone/inference/plots/param.py:160-211` `plot_param_scatter` — `ax.scatter` (rasterized=True does not create `ax.images`), saved to `figures/param_scatter/`.
   - `pipelines/backbone/inference/plots/stratified.py:21-42` `plot_error_curve` — `ax.plot`, saved to `figures/stratified/`; the only imshow figures from that plotter (`plot_failure_mode_map` etc.) are written to `pixel_maps/`, not `stratified/`.
   - `figures.py:536-589` `data_consistency/` mixes imshow maps (`coherence_error_map.png`, `covariance_error_map.png`) with pure curve figures (`residual_vs_kz`, `phase_spread_vs_kz`, `phase_agreement_*`).
   So under `figure_style=paper`, `profiles/`, `param_scatter/`, `stratified/` become 100% `.pdf`, and `data_consistency/` becomes partly `.pdf`.

3. `PaperFigurePackConfig.patterns` (`configuration/diagnostics.py:384`) is `["pixel_maps/*.png", "param_scatter/*.png", "stratified/*.png", "profiles/*.png", "data_consistency/*.png"]` — `.png` only, and `_collect_run` (`pipelines/backbone/inference/paper_figures.py:48-55`) globs those patterns verbatim, raising only when the *total* entry list is empty. Since `pixel_maps/*.png` (imshow) still matches, the guard never fires.

4. Executed repro (Dune env, `PYTHONPATH` at repo root) with a run tree shaped exactly as paper-style inference would leave it (png rasters + pdf vectors). Result: `packed: ['run_a__pixel_maps__mse.png', 'run_a__pixel_maps__r2.png', 'run_a__data_consistency__coherence_error_map.png']` — every `.pdf` (profiles, param_scatter, stratified, residual_vs_kz) silently dropped, no error, manifest reports success.

5. The workflow that triggers it is the one the repo itself instructs: `paper_figures.py:74` manifest note, `main/analysis/export_paper_figures.py:17` CLI description, and `webui/script_catalog.py:198` all say "render in paper style first by running inference with figure_style=paper". Nothing anywhere in the repo globs `*.pdf` (`grep -rn '\*.pdf' --include=*.py` returns nothing), and the existing test `tests/backbone_inference/test_paper_figures.py` only ever writes `.png` fixtures, so it cannot catch this.

This is not one of the listed known non-issues; it is a silent partial-output path, which the project's "break loudly" policy treats as a defect rather than a design choice.
correction: The mechanism is right but the anchor line is not where the defect lives. Line 74 is only the misleading note; the actual defect is the `.png`-only default at /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/configuration/diagnostics.py:384 combined with the glob-and-only-raise-if-totally-empty logic at /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/paper_figures.py:48-55. Two scope refinements: (a) `stratified/` loses everything because its only non-curve figures (`plot_failure_mode_map`, `plot_miss_by_separation`, `plot_presence_reliability`) are written to `pixel_maps/`, not `stratified/`; (b) `data_consistency/` is partially packed (the two imshow error maps survive; `residual_vs_kz`, `phase_spread_vs_kz`, `phase_agreement_*` are dropped). Fix is to extend the patterns to cover both suffixes (e.g. `profiles/*.p*` or explicit `.pdf` entries) or to have `_collect_run` verify each pattern individually so an empty pattern raises. Existing test coverage cannot catch it because `tests/backbone_inference/test_paper_figures.py` only creates `.png` fixtures.

title: Attention capture leaves a process-global tap enabled and the model monkey-patched if the forward raises
description: `AttentionCaptureRun._capture` calls `capture.attach()`, runs a forward, then `capture.detach()` with no `try/finally`. `attach()` sets `AttentionTap._sink` — a *class-level* global in models/blocks.py:496 — and replaces `module.forward` on every `nn.MultiheadAttention`. If the forward raises (shape mismatch, OOM, bad batch) neither is undone: `AttentionTap.record` keeps appending a CPU copy of every softmax matrix produced anywhere in the process into the abandoned list, and the MHA modules stay wrapped. The same pattern is in the test helper (tests/backbone_inference/test_attention_capture.py:18-23), where a failure leaks the tap into the rest of the pytest session. Related: `detach()` restores with `module.forward = original`, which leaves a permanent instance attribute shadowing the class method rather than removing it — `test_capture_detach_restores_the_model` passes only because bound methods compare equal.
evidence:
capture = AttentionCapture(run.model.module)
        capture.attach()

        with torch.no_grad():
            run.model(next(iter(run.loader))[0])

        capture.detach()
suggested_fix: Wrap the forward in `try: ... finally: capture.detach()` (or make `AttentionCapture` a context manager), and in `detach()` use `del module.forward` to restore the class-level method instead of re-binding an instance attribute.
verdict_notes:
The code facts in the claim are all reproducible from source, but the claimed blast radius is not.

Verified mechanism:
- /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/attention_capture.py:185-193 — `_capture` is exactly `capture.attach()` / forward / `capture.detach()` with no `try/finally`. Nothing in the file contains an `except` (grep confirms zero).
- `attach()` (lines 66-81) calls `AttentionTap.enable(self._tap_sink)`, which at /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/models/blocks.py:495-509 sets the *class-level* `AttentionTap._sink`, and `scaled_dot_product` (blocks.py:512-522) calls `AttentionTap.record(...)` unconditionally for every softmax in the process, appending `weights.detach().cpu()` whenever `_sink is not None`. `attach()` also monkey-patches `module.forward` on every `nn.MultiheadAttention` (lines 51-64). So if the forward at line 190 raises, both the class-global sink and the per-module patches survive — accurate.
- The `detach()` restore detail is also accurate: `module.forward = original` (line 91) writes a bound method into the module's instance `__dict__` (nn.Module.__setattr__ falls through to object.__setattr__ for plain values) rather than `del module.forward`, and tests/backbone_inference/test_attention_capture.py:70 passes because bound methods compare equal by (__self__, __func__).

Where the claim overstates: the only production caller is /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/main/analysis/capture_attention.py, which builds `AttentionCaptureBatch(config, logger).run()`; that loop (attention_capture.py:283-291) has no per-run try/except either, and neither does `AttentionCaptureRun.run()` or main(). The webui only launches this as a subprocess (webui/script_catalog.py:160, webui/project_paths.py:117 — no in-process import). So a raising forward propagates straight out of main() and the process dies with a traceback; there is no surviving process in which "AttentionTap.record keeps appending a CPU copy of every softmax matrix produced anywhere in the process" can actually happen, and no further inference runs on the still-patched modules. I could not construct a production failure.

The one real residual failure is the test helper (tests/backbone_inference/test_attention_capture.py:13-24): pytest catches the exception, so a failing capture test leaves `AttentionTap._sink` pointing at an abandoned list for the rest of the session, and every later test that runs MultiHeadSelfAttention/WindowAttention (swin/vit/segformer backbone suites) appends CPU attention copies into it — unbounded growth and slowdown until the next `attach()` re-points `_sink`. It cannot corrupt results (the next `attach()` installs a fresh list, and `records()` reads only its own `_tap_sink`/`_tap_order`), so it degrades an already-failing run rather than producing wrong output.

So: a genuine unguarded-global-state defect worth a `try/finally` (the repo already uses exactly that idiom for restore-after-mutation, e.g. pipelines/backbone/inference/loss_landscape.py:62-69), but the concrete impact is confined to a pytest session after an already-failing test. That is minor, not major.
correction: Line/mechanism are right (attention_capture.py:185-193; AttentionTap._sink is class-global at models/blocks.py:496 and is fed by scaled_dot_product at blocks.py:519), but the impact statement is wrong. There is no exception handling anywhere on the path — `AttentionCaptureBatch.run`, `AttentionCaptureRun.run`, and `main/analysis/capture_attention.py` all let the exception escape, and the webui runs this script as a subprocess — so in production a raising forward terminates the process and the leaked tap/patches are never observed. The only demonstrable harm is inside a pytest session via the test helper (tests/backbone_inference/test_attention_capture.py:13-24), where a failing capture leaves the tap enabled and later attention tests append CPU softmax copies into an abandoned list until the next `attach()` re-points `_sink`; it slows/bloats an already-failing run but cannot corrupt any capture's output. The `module.forward = original` restore likewise leaves an instance attribute shadowing the class method (and a self-referential cycle), which is cosmetically wrong but functionally identical since nn.Module.__call__ resolves `self.forward` through the instance dict. Fix is a `try/finally` around the forward in `_capture` and in the test helper, and `del module.forward` (falling back to nothing else) in `detach()`.

title: Hungarian slot matching recomputed four times per inference with identical arguments
description: `ParamPlotter` calls `GaussianMatcher().aligned_prediction(params_pred, params_gt, n_gaussians)` independently in `plot_param_distributions` (line 29), `plot_param_scatter` (line 170), `plot_param_error_maps` (line 232) and `plot_param_error_hists` (line 279). figures.py `_compose_param_plots` (lines 194-222) invokes all four back to back with byte-identical `result.params_pred[:3K]`, `result.params_gt[:3K]`, `run.n_gaussians`. Each call runs `GaussianMatcher.assignment`, which enumerates all K! permutations and builds a (chunk, K!) cost array over the entire split region in 250k-pixel chunks — the dominant cost of the figure stage, paid four times for one answer. metrics.py adds two more `aligned_prediction` calls plus one `assignment` on the same cubes.
suggested_fix: Compute the aligned cube once in `FigureComposer._compose_param_plots` (or cache it on `Result` next to `params_pred`) and pass it into the four plotting methods; reuse the same cube in metrics.py and failure_modes.py.
verdict_notes:
The redundancy is real and reproducible from source, but the claim's magnitude ("dominant cost of the figure stage") is wrong, so severity drops.

Mechanism verified:
- /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tools/metrics/gaussian_matching.py: `GaussianMatcher` is a stateless, deterministic pure function object with no memoization (`__init__` only stores ppg/amp_threshold/big/chunk_size). `assignment` (lines 26-49) builds `perms = permutations(range(n_K))` (K! rows), then per 250k-pixel chunk builds `cost` of shape (chunk, K, K) and `perm_costs` of shape (chunk, K!) via a 120-iteration Python loop of fancy-index gathers. `aligned_prediction` (line 51) calls `assignment` every time; a fresh `GaussianMatcher()` is constructed at each call site, so nothing is reused.
- /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/plots/param.py: four independent calls at lines 29, 170, 232, 279, exactly as quoted.
- /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/figures.py `_compose_param_plots` (lines 188-222) invokes all four back to back with byte-identical `result.params_pred[:3K]`, `result.params_gt[:3K]`, `run.n_gaussians`. Confirmed.
- The claim actually undercounts: metrics.py has 2 `aligned_prediction` calls (lines 283, 329), a direct `assignment` (line 357), and a fourth through `SlotOrganization.assignment_matrix` (line 461 -> tools/metrics/slot_organization.py:50). figures.py `_compose_slot_organization` (line 249) adds a fifth via `plot_assignment_matrix`. So one inference run recomputes the same assignment about 9 times over the same cubes, not 4+3.

Magnitude measured (Dune env, this machine), which refutes the "dominant cost" framing:
- test_data param cube header is `shape: (15, 1000, 500)` i.e. K=5 and 500k pixels for the WHOLE scene; the inference split region is a strict subset of that.
- Benchmarked `aligned_prediction`: K=5, 1000x500 -> 1.25 s; K=5, 400x500 -> 0.47 s; K=2, 1000x500 -> 0.06 s.
- Benchmarked matplotlib for the same stage: ~0.15 s per scatter figure and ~0.21 s per imshow figure; the four param plot functions emit ~3K figures each (~60 figures at K=5), so ~10 s of rendering for the param block alone, and the full figure stage (tracks, profiles, pixel maps, slices, SSIM, reduced, physics, GIFs) is far larger.
So the redundant matching costs roughly 3-4 s in the figure stage and ~5 s more across metrics per inference run — real waste, but an order of magnitude below the figure stage's own cost, not its dominant term.

Path frequency: `FigureComposer.compose` runs exactly once per inference run (pipeline.py line 395), not per training step, per epoch, or per request. It is a cold path by the audit protocol's own criterion. The fix is trivial (compute the alignment once in `_compose_param_plots`/`Metrics` and pass it down), which is why I keep it as a finding rather than dismissing it, but "major" is not supportable.
correction: Two corrections. (1) Scope is larger than stated: the same assignment is recomputed about 9 times per inference run, not 4 (+2 aligned_prediction +1 assignment). The additional sites are pipelines/backbone/inference/metrics.py:357 (`GaussianMatcher().assignment`), metrics.py:461 via `SlotOrganization.assignment_matrix` (tools/metrics/slot_organization.py:50), and figures.py:249 `_compose_slot_organization` -> `plot_assignment_matrix`. (2) The cost characterization is wrong: measured on this machine at the maximum realistic size (K=5, full 1000x500 test_data scene) one `aligned_prediction` takes 1.25 s (K=2: 0.06 s), while the param figure block alone spends ~10 s in matplotlib and the whole figure stage far more. The redundancy wastes roughly 4 s in figures plus ~5 s in metrics per inference run, on a once-per-run path -- it is not "the dominant cost of the figure stage".

title: Fit-metrics stage loads the whole tomogram into RAM, defeating the chunked ContrastEstimator and allocating 3 more full-size cubes
description: `FittingMetricsCalculator._load_tomogram` reads the complete tomogram with `np.load` (no mmap) and materialises `np.abs(...)` of it. `ContrastEstimator.run` (line 39-46) then loops over range chunks and calls `np.abs(tomogram[:, :, r_start:r_end])` again — that per-chunk `np.abs` only makes sense if it were handed a memory-mapped complex cube (which is exactly how the test `tests/processing/test_param_extraction.py::test_snr_estimator_runs` calls it), so the chunking is now pure overhead on already-real data. Afterwards `ProfilePreprocessor.apply` (line 289) allocates another full-size copy and `_compute_r2_map` allocates `pred` at full cube size (line 164). For a production crop (e.g. 3600 az x 3500 rg x ~200 elevation bins) that is ~20 GB complex + three ~10 GB float32 cubes live at once, whereas the extractor that produced these very parameters deliberately memory-maps and works in range batches. The whole stage can be done range-chunk by range-chunk against a memmap.
suggested_fix: Open the tomogram with `mmap_mode="r"` and drive contrast, preprocessing and the R2 accumulation through the same range-chunk loop already present in `ContrastEstimator.run`, accumulating ss_res/ss_tot per chunk instead of allocating a full `pred` cube.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. (1) pipelines/processing/param_extraction/metrics.py:152 `_load_tomogram` calls `np.load` with no `mmap_mode`, so the entire complex64 tomogram enters RAM, and `np.abs(...)` allocates a full float32 cube while the complex cube is still referenced (12 bytes/element momentarily; verified np.abs(complex64)->float32). (2) The same file is memory-mapped everywhere else in the same subsystem: `SigmaFittingExtractor._prepare_data` (sigma/extractor.py:117, `mmap_mode="r"`, range-batched `[:, :, r0:r1]` loads) and `ExampleFitPlotter._extract_pixel_profiles` (plots/examples.py:66, `mmap_mode="r"`). So the metrics stage is the lone outlier, not a deliberate design. (3) `ContrastEstimator.run` (lines 39-46) receives already-real float32 data from `run()` line 286, so its per-chunk `np.abs(...).astype(np.float32)` is two redundant chunk-sized copies; I confirmed with numpy that `np.abs` on a float32 array copies. The test `tests/processing/test_param_extraction.py::test_snr_estimator_runs` (line 415) does pass a complex window, confirming the chunked-abs was written for a memmapped complex cube, as the auditor argues. (4) Downstream full-size allocations are real: `ProfilePreprocessor.apply` (tools/data/preprocessing.py) with the default threshold_factor=0.25 builds a full-size bool mask plus a new full float32 cube via np.where (9 bytes/elt live), and `_compute_r2_map` allocates `pred = np.empty_like(tomogram)`. (5) The memory accounting is actually worse than claimed: `R2.pixel_map` (tools/metrics/scoring.py:57-63) computes `ref.mean(..., dtype=np.float64)`, so `(ref - ref_mean)` and its square are FULL-SIZE float64 temporaries (I verified the dtype promotion in numpy) — 16 bytes/elt on top of `pred` + `tomogram`, giving a peak around 24 bytes per cube element. (6) Scale: the production dataset default is az1000-16000 x rg500-4000 (configuration/training/general/run.py:9, configuration/sar/processing_config.py:139-142) with H=150 elevation bins (test twin header confirms 150 bins for height_range [-20,80]), i.e. 7.9e9 elements = 63 GB complex on disk and a ~190 GB transient peak in this stage — far above the auditor's own estimate. (7) Frequency: `ParamExtractionInferenceScheduler` runs one `ParamRunInferencePipeline` per extraction trial and the default `fit_modes` list has 3 entries, so the whole cube is re-loaded from scratch once per trial. Every stage of `run()` (contrast, preprocess, R2) is per-pixel over the elevation axis and therefore trivially chunkable in range against a memmap, exactly as the extractor does. This is not one of the listed known non-issues.
correction: Two details in the claim are off, both in the conservative direction. (a) Peak memory is larger than stated: besides the complex cube, the abs cube, the ProfilePreprocessor copy and `pred`, `R2.pixel_map` promotes `(ref - ref_mean)` and its square to FULL-SIZE float64 arrays because `ref.mean(..., dtype=np.float64)` is float64 — roughly 24 bytes per cube element at peak, not ~12. (b) The production crop is bigger than the auditor's example: the repo default is 15000 az x 3500 rg x 150 elevation bins (~63 GB complex, ~31.5 GB per float32 cube, ~190 GB peak), not 3600 x 3500 x 200.
