title: snap_repomap.js waits for networkidle on a page the project documents as never idling
description: `RepoMapSnapper.orchestrate()` navigates the live console with `waitUntil: "networkidle"`. Playwright resolves networkidle only after 500 ms with no in-flight requests, but `StatusBoard.start()` (webui/static/js/home.js:156) fires `/api/system` every 250 ms from app boot on every route, so the network never idles. The sibling tool's own README documents exactly this: "Network-idle waits are deliberately avoided: the status board polls /api/system every 250 ms from app boot, so the network never idles" (webui/tools/visual/README.md:34-35), and snap_ui.js correctly uses `domcontentloaded`. render_diagram.js can safely use networkidle because it loads a static file:// harness with no polling.
suggested_fix: Use `waitUntil: "domcontentloaded"` followed by the existing `waitForSelector("#view")`, matching snap_ui.js.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source and empirically.

Source chain:
- /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/tools/visual/snap_repomap.js:89 — `await page.goto(base, { waitUntil: "networkidle" });` against the live console at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`.
- /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/static/js/app.js:490 `DOMContentLoaded -> new App().init()`, which reaches `_loadProject()` (line 121) -> `_initStatus()` (line 159) -> `this.statusBoard.start()` (line 168). This runs unconditionally at app boot on every hash route (single-page app; there is no per-route gating).
- /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/static/js/home.js:154-161 — `StatusBoard.start()` calls `_poll()` immediately and then `setInterval(..., 250)`, plus 5 s job polls and 20 s guard-history polls. `_poll()` issues `window.apiGet("/api/system")` (home.js:182), which is a real `fetch` (app.js:3-11), so Playwright counts it as an in-flight request. With a 250 ms period, the longest gap with zero in-flight requests is < 250 ms, never the 500 ms Playwright requires to emit the `networkidle` lifecycle event. The `_polling` re-entrancy guard only lengthens request occupancy; it cannot create a 500 ms hole. `_serverDown` (home.js:490) is the only stop condition and only trips when the backend dies.

Empirical proof: started the real console (`webui/run.sh 8811`), then ran the tool unmodified:
  `node snap_repomap.js --port 8811 --out <dir> backbone:backbone-inference`
  -> `page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded. Call log: - navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:8811/", waiting until "networkidle"` and no PNG produced.
Running a byte-identical copy with only `networkidle` -> `domcontentloaded` on line 89 succeeded and wrote `backbone__backbone-inference.png`. Test server was killed afterwards; no repo files were modified (the temp copy was removed).

The auditor's supporting points also check out: webui/tools/visual/README.md:34-35 documents exactly this hazard ("Network-idle waits are deliberately avoided: the status board polls /api/system every 250 ms from app boot, so the network never idles"), snap_ui.js:68 uses `domcontentloaded`, and render_diagram.js:85 uses `networkidle` only against a `file://` harness (repomap_harness.html) with no polling, so it is unaffected. This is not one of the listed known non-issues.

Note: the tool is dead on arrival, not flaky — it has never been able to complete a single navigation since it was added (commit b3b2659). The subsequent `waitForSelector("#view")`, hash switch, and screenshot loop are all unreachable.
correction: Mechanism and line are exact; one refinement: the failure is deterministic and total (100% of invocations abort with a 30 s TimeoutError before any screenshot), not a race. Severity stays "major" as an audit/dev-tooling defect — it does not affect the shipped console, training, or inference paths, only the repo-map screenshot harness. Fix is a one-word change on line 89 to `waitUntil: "domcontentloaded"`, matching snap_ui.js:68; verified to work.

title: /api/system polled at 4 Hz from every open tab on every route, forking two nvidia-smi processes per request
description: `StatusBoard.start()` polls `/api/system` every 250 ms. The handler (webui/request_router.py:541) calls `SystemMonitor.snapshot()`, which is uncached and per request runs `gpu_occupancy()` (an `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` subprocess) plus `_gpu_cards()` → `_gpu_devices()` (a second `nvidia-smi --query-gpu` subprocess), then `_procs()`, which scans all of /proc and reads `/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup` for every own process (`ProcStats.pss`, a full page-table walk). That is ~8 nvidia-smi forks per second per open browser tab, on a shared training box, regardless of which page is showing — the guard is only `document.hidden`, and there is no `leave()` that stops the interval when the user navigates away from Home. The same endpoint is also re-fetched by `GpuCardSelect.load()` (webui/static/js/launch_widgets.js:4119) for every GpuPicker instance, every console tile GPU panel, and on every Feed Tuner `enter()`.
suggested_fix: Poll at 1 Hz or slower, gate on the Home page being active (as tensorboard.js/tomogram.js do with enter/leave), and cache the GPU/proc snapshot server-side behind a short TTL so concurrent callers share one nvidia-smi sample.
verdict_notes: Reproduced end to end from source. webui/static/js/home.js:156 is verbatim `setInterval(() => { if (!document.hidden) this._poll(); }, 250);` inside StatusBoard.start(). StatusBoard is constructed once in App._initStatus() (app.js:163-168) at boot and is never referenced by the router's _onRoute (app.js:458-486), which does have enter()/leave() for other views — so there is no route-based stop, exactly as claimed. The DOM it drives (#status-host/#status-sum/#status-board) sits entirely inside <section data-page="home"> in static/index.html:57-75, so the 4 Hz poll keeps updating an invisible page on every other route. window.apiGet (app.js:3) is a bare fetch with no caching or in-flight dedup. Server side, request_router.py:541 calls self.system.snapshot() with no cache/TTL/rate limit, on a ThreadingHTTPServer (web_ui_server.py:43-46), so N tabs issue N concurrent snapshots. SystemMonitor.snapshot() (system_monitor.py:342) calls gpu_occupancy() (line 217), which forks _compute_apps() (nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps, line 161) and _gpu_devices() (nvidia-smi --query-gpu, line 136) — two subprocess forks per request, each with timeout=3 — then _procs() (line 74), which lists all of /proc, stats every entry, and reads /proc/<pid>/stat and /proc/<pid>/cmdline for every own PID. The lock at line 345 does not cover the GPU calls. Two forks x 4 Hz x tabs, on a shared training box, on a per-request handler path — the waste is real and on a hot path. Not covered by any KNOWN NON-ISSUE. No test encodes the interval or an uncached contract (tests/webui/test_system_history.py:81-91 and test_active_users.py:135 merely call snapshot()), so a TTL cache would not violate intended behavior. Secondary claim also verified: GpuCardSelect.load() (launch_widgets.js:4119) fetches the whole /api/system payload per picker instance just to read payload.gpus.
correction: Three mechanism details are off. (1) _gpu_cards() is NOT a second nvidia-smi path: it is a pure reformat of the occupancy list already fetched (system_monitor.py:291). The two forks per request are _compute_apps() and _gpu_devices(), both inside gpu_occupancy(). The count of two is right, the attribution is not. (2) ProcStats.pss/smaps_rollup is read only for the top PROC_LIMIT = 30 rows after sorting (system_monitor.py:121-126), not "for every own process"; the per-request /proc cost is the full directory scan plus stat+cmdline reads for every own PID. (3) The effective rate is min(4 Hz, 1/RTT) per tab, not a hard 4 Hz, because _poll() has a `this._polling` re-entrancy guard (home.js:176-178) — so ~6-8 forks/s per tab rather than exactly 8. Worth adding to the finding: SystemHistory.sample_loop already forks _gpu_devices() every SAMPLE_PERIOD_S = 0.5 s server-side with zero clients connected (system_monitor.py:395,417-420), so a ~1 s TTL cache on snapshot() — or having the handler reuse the history sampler's device list — fixes both the client-driven and the baseline fork load in one change. GpuCardSelect should also get a lighter endpoint or share the cached payload instead of pulling the full snapshot per instance.

title: Fit Lab 'Run fit' button stays permanently disabled if a dataset load interrupts a running fit
description: `_runFit()` disables `runBtn` and shows the fit progress bar before entering the poll loop. `_select()` (dataset pick) bumps the shared `this.pollToken`, which breaks the fit `while (token === this.pollToken)` loop; control then reaches the bail-out at line 451 and returns without restoring `runBtn.disabled = false` or hiding `fitProgress`. The only code that re-enables the button is the success/error path further down and `_ready()` does not touch it, so the Fit Lab becomes unusable until a full page reload.
suggested_fix: Restore the UI in a `finally` (or before every early return): `this.refs.runBtn.disabled = false; this.refs.fitProgress.hidden = true;`. Better, give load and fit separate tokens instead of sharing `pollToken`.
verdict_notes:
The code mechanism is exactly as quoted: fit_lab.js line 434-435 disables runBtn and shows fitProgress, line 437 takes `const token = ++this.pollToken`, and line 451 `if (token !== this.pollToken) return;` exits without restoring either. Repo-wide grep shows `runBtn.disabled` is written only at lines 434/441/453 in fit_lab.js, and `_ready()` (line 275) never touches it, so a bail-out at 451 does leave the Fit Lab unusable until a page reload. `_select()` at line 256 bumps the same shared `this.pollToken`, so it can break the fit loop.

However, the auditor's stated trigger — "a dataset load interrupts a running fit" — is mostly blocked server-side. webui/fit_lab.py `start_load` (lines 55-60) refuses with `{"ok": False, "error": "a fit is running; wait for it to finish"}` whenever `fit_state["state"] == "fitting"`, and `_select` returns at its `if (!res.ok)` branch BEFORE `++this.pollToken`. So a dataset click during an actually-running fit never bumps the token. `start_fit` sets `fit_state = "fitting"` synchronously under the lock before returning ok, so there is no gap right after the fit is submitted either.

The defect is still reachable, but only as a race: `_fit_worker` writes `fit_state` = done/error from the worker thread, while the client only observes it on its next poll (350 ms sleep plus request latency). A dataset click landing in that gap passes start_load's guard, bumps pollToken, the fit `while` loop exits at the top, control reaches line 451 and returns with runBtn still disabled and fitProgress still visible. The symmetric case also exists: starting a fit while a load poll is in flight bumps the token at line 437 and strands `_select`'s loop, leaving `refs.progress` visible and `_ready()` never called (meta stays null, stage stays hidden). Root cause is one shared pollToken driving two independent poll loops with no cleanup on the interrupted branch (microscope.js uses the same pattern but has no UI state to restore, so it is unaffected).

No JS tests exist; tests/webui/test_fit_lab.py covers only the Python side and encodes the two mutual-exclusion guards, which is why the wide window the auditor describes does not exist. Confirmed as a real UI-state leak, downgraded to minor because it requires a sub-second timing race rather than an ordinary click.
correction: Mechanism is right but reachability is overstated. webui/fit_lab.py `start_load` refuses while `fit_state == "fitting"`, and `_select` returns before bumping `pollToken` on a refused load, so picking a dataset during a running fit does NOT break the fit loop. The stuck-button state is only reachable in the poll-interval race: after the backend fit worker sets state to done/error but before the client's next 350 ms `fit_status` poll observes it, a dataset click is accepted, bumps `pollToken`, and the fit loop bails at line 451 leaving `runBtn.disabled = true` and `fitProgress` visible. The inverse race exists too (a fit started in the gap after a load finishes bumps the token at line 437 and strands `_select`'s loop with `refs.progress` visible and `_ready()` never called). The real defect is a single shared `pollToken` serving two independent poll loops with no state cleanup on the interrupted branch; the fix is per-loop tokens (or restoring `runBtn.disabled`/`fitProgress.hidden` in the line-451 bail-out and `refs.progress.hidden` in `_select`'s).

title: NumberField builds and maintains a range slider that is never inserted into the DOM
description: `NumberField.build()` creates `slider` (`<input type="range">`, class `numfield__slider`), calls `_configureSlider()`, and keeps it in sync from the text input (line 3964), from every preset chip (line 4075) and from `_paint()` (line 4098) — but `slider` is never appended anywhere: `build()` only appends `input` and `presets` into `top`, and `top` into `el`. `css/styles.css` has no `.numfield__slider` rule either (only `.numfield__top` and `.numfield__presets`). Consequently `_fromSlider()` (line 4048) has zero callers, and the whole log-scale apparatus (`this.log`, `logMin`, `logMax`, `_toSlider`, `_configureSlider`, `spec.log`) exists only to update an orphaned element on every keystroke.
suggested_fix: Either append the slider (`top.appendChild(slider)`) and add the missing CSS, or delete `slider`, `_configureSlider`, `_toSlider`, `_fromSlider`, `logMin`/`logMax` and the `log` branch of `_fmt`.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source in /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/static/js/launch_widgets.js.

`NumberField.build()` (lines 3941-3975) does exactly what the claim says: it creates `top` (class `numfield__top`), creates `input` and appends it to `top` (line 3966), creates `slider` at 3955-3958 with class `numfield__slider` and calls `_configureSlider()` at 3959, appends `top` to `el` (3967), creates `presets` and appends it to `top` (3973), then returns `{ el, input, reset }`. `slider` is never passed to any `appendChild`/`append`/`insertBefore`/`replaceWith`, and it is not part of the returned object, so no caller can attach it either.

Caller check: the only construction site is line 4849 (`control = new window.NumberField(this, leaf, short, kind === "number" ? spec : null).build();`), and the caller only does `row.appendChild(control.el)` and stores `{leaf, reset: control.reset, input: control.input, setInactive: control.setInactive}` (line 4856). No access to `.slider`.

Repo-wide greps confirm isolation: `numfield__slider` appears exactly once in the whole repository (launch_widgets.js:3956). `webui/static/css/styles.css` has `.numfield`, `.numfield__top`, `.numfield__input`, `.numfield__presets`, `.numfield__chip` (lines 1580-1589) but no `.numfield__slider` rule. No reference to `.slider` anywhere else in webui/static, webui/*.py, or tests/. `NumberField` itself appears only at its definition (3923), the caller (4849), and the window export (5217). No test exercises the slider — tests/webui/test_launch_layout.py only greps launch_widgets.js for loss-component names.

`_fromSlider()` (4048) indeed has zero callers — it is the only reader of `this.slider.value` besides nothing, and `logMin`/`logMax` are written only in `_configureSlider()` and read only in `_toSlider`/`_fromSlider`, whose outputs go exclusively to the orphaned element. This is not dynamic dispatch: it is plain JS with no string-based lookup, and the exhaustive greps rule out external wiring. Not one of the listed known non-issues.
correction:
Line reference (3955) and the core mechanism are correct, with two refinements.

(1) The dead chain is narrower than described. `this.log` is NOT dead: `_resolve()` sets it (line 3986) and `_fmt()` reads it at line 4060 (`v.toPrecision(this.log ? 2 : 6)`), which controls preset-chip label precision and preset dedup keys in `_cleanPresets()`. So `spec.log` (set by `LaunchLayout.NUM_ETA_MIN = {"kind": "number", "log": True, ...}` in /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/launch_layout.py:26) does have a live, user-visible effect on how chips are labelled. The genuinely dead members are: `this.slider`, `_configureSlider()`, `_toSlider()`, `_fromSlider()`, `this.logMin`, `this.logMax`, and the three `slider.value = ...` assignments (3964, 4075, 4098).

(2) Severity should be minor, not major. There is no runtime failure or user-visible defect — an unparented `<input type="range">` is simply garbage-collected with the field; the wasted work is a handful of arithmetic ops per keystroke on a config form, not a hot path. The finding is a maintenance/intent issue (a slider control was evidently planned and either dropped or never wired up), plus possible latent intent that eta_min should be adjustable on a log slider.

title: Twelve tests assert on source text (inspect.getsource / read_text) instead of behaviour
description: A whole family of tests verifies implementation by grepping the source of the function under test. They pass whenever the substring appears anywhere — including in a comment, a docstring, a dead branch, or an unrelated call — and they break on harmless renames/refactors while staying green if the behaviour is silently inverted. Locations: tests/benchmark/test_batch_probe.py:40 (test_trial_uses_real_trainer_loss_not_surrogate), :49 (test_trial_measures_peak_reserved_memory), :56 (test_build_trainer_constructs_real_trainer), :63 (test_build_context_imports_real_dataset_and_trainer_pipeline), :109 (test_run_caps_the_ceiling_at_the_dataset_size), :115 (test_run_validates_size_match_channels_against_the_dataset), :121 (test_run_records_the_measured_context), :127 (test_build_context_probes_with_the_swept_loss_union); tests/dataloader_tuning/test_adapters.py:81 (test_feed_losses_are_mse_surrogates_not_trainer_loss); tests/entrypoints/test_main_entrypoints.py:154 (test_module_guards_execution_behind_name_main), :170 (test_seed_sweep_entries_hand_their_script_to_the_fanout), :177 (test_train_main_defers_heavy_imports). This is doubly bad for the batch-probe ones, because the known project rule is that the VRAM probe must run the real Trainer loss — that invariant is now guarded only by the literal string 'mse_loss' not appearing in a function body.
evidence:
def test_trial_uses_real_trainer_loss_not_surrogate():
    source = inspect.getsource(TrainStepMemoryProbe.__call__)

    assert "_compute_loss" in source
    assert "total_loss" in source
    assert "loss.backward()" in source
    assert "mse_loss" not in source
suggested_fix: Replace with behavioural assertions: monkeypatch/spy the Trainer so the probe records that `_compute_loss` was actually invoked and that peak memory was queried, and for the entrypoint ones import the module and assert the observable effect (no side effects at import, entry_script actually forwarded to the fanout) rather than grepping the file.
verdict_notes:
I reproduced every cited location from source; the claim's factual core is exact.

tests/benchmark/test_batch_probe.py — 8 tests call `inspect.getsource(...)` and assert on substrings:
- :40 `test_trial_uses_real_trainer_loss_not_surrogate` — asserts "_compute_loss", "total_loss", "loss.backward()" present and "mse_loss" absent in `TrainStepMemoryProbe.__call__`.
- :49 peak-memory test — asserts "reset_peak_memory_stats"/"max_memory_reserved" appear.
- :56 asserts "Trainer(" and "set_curriculum" appear in `MaxBatchProbe._build_trainer`.
- :63 asserts "DatasetPipeline" appears and regex-matches the literal import line in the module source.
- :109 asserts the literal `min(self.ceiling, len(dataset))` appears in `MaxBatchProbe.run`.
- :115 asserts the literal `dataset.input_channels != self.config.size_match.in_channels` appears.
- :121 asserts the literal `result["context_gb"] = self.context_gb` appears.
- :127 asserts two full literal call expressions appear in `_build_context`.
tests/dataloader_tuning/test_adapters.py:81 — asserts "mse_loss" in / "criterion" and "_compute_loss" not in the source of `FeedLosses.reconstruction` and `.supervised`.
tests/entrypoints/test_main_entrypoints.py:154 / :170 / :177 — `_script_path(name).read_text()` then substring assertions.

The failure mode is real and I can state it concretely. :109, :115, :121 are pure text echoes with no semantic power: e.g. `MaxBatchProbe.run` currently does `ceiling = min(self.ceiling, len(dataset))` and passes `ceiling=ceiling` to `BatchSizeFinder`; if someone kept that line but passed `ceiling=self.ceiling` to the finder, the cap would be silently gone and the test stays green. Same for :115 — change `raise RuntimeError(...)` to a logger warning while keeping the `!=` comparison and the guard is gone, test still green. The brittleness half is demonstrable too: :170 asserts the exact spelling `entry_script=pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve()`, and main/training/train_backbone.py:20, train_dual.py:20, train_unrolled.py:20 write the behaviourally identical `entry_script=Path(__file__).resolve()` — that spelling would fail the test despite identical behaviour.

The :154 `__name__ == "__main__"` grep is also redundant: tests/entrypoints/test_main_entrypoints.py:144-149 already tests that behaviourally by `runpy.run_path(script, run_name='launcher_import_check')` in a subprocess and asserting returncode 0.

Two things temper the claim without refuting it. (1) The project's global rule forbids comments and docstrings, so the "matches inside a comment/docstring" vector is mostly closed; the dead-branch / unrelated-call / string-literal vectors remain and are the ones I demonstrated. (2) `TrainStepMemoryProbe.__call__` calls `torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats` / `max_memory_reserved`, so a behavioural test needs CUDA or monkeypatched `torch.cuda` — a stub trainer recording `_compute_loss`/`backward`/`step` calls is entirely feasible (tests/training_runtime/test_pretrain_batch_finder.py already stubs `trial_step` this way), so the shortcut is not forced.

Not one of the listed KNOWN NON-ISSUES: the deferred-import policy is real, but :177 encodes it as a text grep on `source.split("def main")[0]`, which passes vacuously for `import pipelines.x` (no "from pipelines"); the finding is about the assertion technique, not the policy.
correction: Category is mislabelled. This is not "unintended-behavior" in production code — no runtime path misbehaves. It is a test-quality defect: tautological/implementation-echo assertions that provide false confidence and churn on renames. Also note the auditor's framing "stays green if the behaviour is silently inverted" is only partly right for :115 and :40 (the asserted literals include the operator/symbol names, so a direct inversion of `!=` or a swap to `mse_loss` would fail the grep); the realistic silent-failure path is keeping the matched line while making it dead or unused, which I confirmed is possible for :109, :115 and :121. Recommended fixes: for :109/:115/:121 assert behaviour on `MaxBatchProbe.run` with a stubbed `_build_context`/`_build_model`/`_build_trainer` and a recording `BatchSizeFinder`; for :40/:49 assert behaviour with a stub trainer plus monkeypatched `torch.cuda` counters; :154 can simply be deleted as redundant with test_script_imports_in_launcher_subprocess.

title: test_compare_runs_is_the_only_module_pinning_threads_at_import asserts stale behaviour and has a dead branch
description: The test is parametrized over DEFER_HEAVY_IMPORTS (lines 317-343), which does NOT contain "compare_runs". The `if name == "compare_runs": return` early-out and the `or name in {"compare_runs"}` disjunct are therefore unreachable, and the assertion collapses to `assert not pinned` for every case. Worse, the name encodes behaviour that is no longer true: main/analysis/compare_runs.py calls `EnvironmentPinner.threads()` inside `main()` (line 25), not at import — which is exactly what the very next test (test_compare_runs_has_no_module_level_side_effects, line 196) asserts. The two tests state contradictory intent and the misleading name will send a future reader hunting for a special case that no longer exists.
suggested_fix: Rename to test_import_does_not_pin_threads, drop the dead compare_runs branch and the tautological disjunct, leaving `assert not pinned`.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. tests/entrypoints/test_main_entrypoints.py lines 28-54 define DEFER_HEAVY_IMPORTS with 25 entries, none of which is "compare_runs" (that name appears only in CLI_MODULES line 72 and ENTRY_CONFIGS line 96). The test at line 184 is parametrized over DEFER_HEAVY_IMPORTS only, so `if name == "compare_runs": return` (191-192) is unreachable and the disjunct `or name in {"compare_runs"}` (193) is always False; the assertion collapses to `assert not pinned` for all 25 cases. main/analysis/compare_runs.py calls EnvironmentPinner.threads() at line 25 inside main(), not at import, so the test name is factually stale; a repo-wide grep of EnvironmentPinner shows every main/ script pins inside main(), so no module pins at import at all. The next test (line 196, test_compare_runs_has_no_module_level_side_effects) asserts the contradictory intent. I ran both under the Dune env: 26 passed, so nothing fails today.
correction: Two details are wrong or overstated. (1) Line range: DEFER_HEAVY_IMPORTS is at lines 28-54, not "317-343" (the file is only 301 lines). (2) "asserts stale behaviour" overstates the defect: the surviving assertion `assert not pinned` is correct and still valuable (it proves no main/ module pins BLAS threads at import time). What is actually wrong is the test NAME plus two unreachable branches, i.e. dead code and a misleading label, not a false assertion or a masked defect. No production behaviour is affected. Fix is to rename to something like test_no_module_pins_threads_at_import and delete lines 191-192 and the `or name in {"compare_runs"}` disjunct. Severity is test hygiene, hence minor rather than major.

title: test_context_manager_closes_writer verifies nothing about closing
description: The test enters and exits the TrainingRunMetadata context manager and then asserts exactly the same condition it asserted inside the block: that `meta.writer is not None`. Since `__exit__` never rebinds `writer` to None, this assertion holds whether or not `close()` runs, whether or not the SummaryWriter is flushed, and whether `__exit__` raises internally would be the only failure mode. A regression that stops closing/flushing the writer (leaking a file handle and losing buffered scalars) passes this test.
evidence:
with TrainingRunMetadata(trainer_config, "resunet", tmp_path / "runs", run_name="ctx") as meta:
        assert meta.writer is not None

    assert meta.writer is not None
suggested_fix: Assert the observable effect of closing: that the tensorboard event file exists and is non-empty after exit, or spy on writer.close() (e.g. wrap it) and assert it was called exactly once.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source.

/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/shared/config/run_metadata.py:
- `__exit__` (line 68-69) calls `self.close()`.
- `close()` (line 116-122) does `self.writer.flush(); self.writer.close()` and `self.logger.close()` if owned. It never rebinds `self.writer`, so the attribute keeps pointing at the (now closed) SummaryWriter object.

Therefore the post-block assertion at tests/entrypoints/test_run_metadata.py:106 (`assert meta.writer is not None`) is identical to the in-block assertion at line 104 and is true regardless of whether `close()`/`flush()` ran. I verified empirically in the Dune env that a SummaryWriter remains a non-None object after `close()` (only `writer.all_writers` flips from a 1-entry dict to `None`). So deleting the `self.close()` call from `__exit__`, or dropping the `flush()`, leaves this test green — the test only proves `__exit__` did not raise, not that anything was closed.

The same vacuity exists in the sibling test /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/pipelines_shared/test_run_metadata.py:77-81, where the post-block assertion is `meta.run_directory.is_dir()` — also unrelated to closing (the directory is created in `__init__` and never removed). No other test in the repo asserts the closed/flushed state, so the flush-on-exit behaviour is entirely uncovered.

Not a KNOWN NON-ISSUE: this is about test content, not entry-point import order, legacy fallbacks, or dynamic dispatch.

Corrections: the production code is correct — nothing is leaked at runtime — so this is a test-coverage gap, not a runtime bug, and "major" overstates it. An observable post-condition exists and would make the test meaningful: after the `with` block, assert `meta.writer.all_writers is None` (torch's SummaryWriter sets it to None in `close()`), and optionally that the tensorboard event file under `meta.tensorboard_dir` exists with non-zero size; for the owned-logger path, assert the logger's handlers were released.
correction: Claim is accurate on mechanism and line (tests/entrypoints/test_run_metadata.py:106) but mis-typed and over-rated. Category should be test-coverage, not bug: pipelines/shared/config/run_metadata.py `close()` does correctly flush and close the writer, so no file handle or scalar is actually lost today — the defect is that the test named `test_context_manager_closes_writer` cannot detect a future regression. The identical vacuity also affects tests/pipelines_shared/test_run_metadata.py:77-81, which the auditor did not mention. Severity minor. Fix: assert `meta.writer.all_writers is None` after the block (torch nulls it in `SummaryWriter.close()`), plus existence/non-zero size of the event file in `meta.tensorboard_dir`.

title: test_extraction_config_matches_param_extraction_meta_suffix never reads the metadata it claims to match
description: The test requests the `param_extraction_meta` session fixture but never touches it in the body; it just asserts a hardcoded literal suffix. The only effect of the fixture is to pull in `params_dir`, which calls `_require_data()` and skips when test_data/ is absent — so on a machine without the real data the test skips, and on a machine with it the test still ignores the file. It cannot detect the exact drift it is named for (k_max/lambda/sigma_divisor in param_extraction_meta.json diverging from ExtractionConfig's suffix), and it is also missing the `@pytest.mark.real_data` marker every other data-dependent test in the file/suite carries.
suggested_fix: Build the FitConfig from param_extraction_meta (k_max, lambda_k, sigma_init_divisor) and compare cfg.output_subdir_name against the real params_dir.name; add @pytest.mark.real_data.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. tests/configuration/test_param.py:163 declares the `param_extraction_meta` fixture parameter but the body never touches it; it asserts only that ExtractionConfig(k_max=5, sigma_init_divisor=4.0, lambda_k=1e-2).output_subdir_name equals the literal "params_k5_lam0.01_sig4_sigma" — the same class of pure-literal assertion already covered by tests at lines 133-148, with no reference to any on-disk metadata. tests/conftest.py:76-78 defines the fixture on top of `params_dir` (lines 55-58), which calls `_require_data()` and `pytest.skip`s when test_data/data/dataset.json is absent, so on a data-less machine the assertion does not run at all, and on a data-carrying machine the JSON is loaded and discarded. pipelines/processing/param_extraction/io.py:41-61 shows the meta does record k_max, lambda_k, sigma_init_divisor and output_suffix, i.e. exactly the drift the test name promises to catch, so the test cannot fail on that drift. The marker point also holds: every other fixture consumer (tests/data_layer/test_gaussians.py:210,222,237; tests/reporting/test_markdown.py:292; tests/reporting/test_reporting.py:211; tests/processing/test_param_extraction.py:241) carries @pytest.mark.real_data, this one does not, and README documents real_data as the deselection marker. This is not one of the listed known non-issues. Severity lowered to minor because no production code path is wrong: the impact is a vacuous test plus loss of the literal-suffix assertion on machines without test_data, and a marker taxonomy inconsistency.
correction: Mechanism is right but the naive fix would break: the real test_data/params/params_k5_lam0.01_sig4_sigma/param_extraction_meta.json records "output_suffix": "sigmaonly_k5_sig4_lam0p01" (legacy scheme; the directory was renamed but the meta was never regenerated), while configuration/param_extraction.py:102-115 now produces "k5_lam0.01_sig4_sigma". So asserting cfg.output_suffix_value == meta["output_suffix"] would fail on the shipped data. The meaningful repair is to add @pytest.mark.real_data and build the config from meta["k_max"], meta["lambda_k"], meta["sigma_init_divisor"] and the meta fit_sigma/fit_amplitude/fit_mean flags, then assert cfg.output_subdir_name == params_dir.name (requires also requesting the params_dir fixture). Severity is minor rather than major: test-quality/coverage gap, no production behavior affected.

title: kz-convention tests are blind to a sign inversion because the helper searches both signs
description: `_sampled()` beamforms with both `+1.0` and `-1.0` phase signs and keeps whichever gives the smaller peak error. Every test built on it (`test_beamformed_peaks_match_pyrat_tomogram_axis`, `test_height_convention_fits_at_least_as_well_as_slant`) therefore passes identically whether `GeometryField.kz()` returns the correct sign or the negated one. The file exists specifically to pin the PyRAT axis/phase convention (the project treats `capon_phase_sign = +1.0` as settled), so the one property it should guard is the one it cannot detect. Either assert the winning sign is `+1.0`, or drop the search and beamform with the production sign only.
suggested_fix: Return the winning sign from `_sampled` and assert it equals +1.0, or beamform only with the production convention so a sign regression fails the test.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source, and empirically on the shipped real data.

MECHANISM (confirmed). `_beamform_peaks` (tests/sar_geometry/test_pyrat_axis_convention.py:44-50) builds `phase = sign * kz_secondary * z`, so negating `kz` is exactly equivalent to flipping `sign`. `_sampled` (line 74) evaluates both `+1.0` and `-1.0` and keeps the smaller-error branch, so the returned `best_peaks` is *invariant* under `kz -> -kz`: the two branches simply swap. Verified numerically (peaks(+kz,+1) == peaks(-kz,-1) and peaks(+kz,-1) == peaks(-kz,+1), element-for-element). `reference` comes from the tomogram argmax only, so both `test_beamformed_peaks_match_pyrat_tomogram_axis` (line 108) and `test_height_convention_fits_at_least_as_well_as_slant` (line 122) — which calls `_sampled` once per convention, each with its own independent sign search — produce byte-identical numbers whether `GeometryField.kz()` returns the correct sign or its negation. The other three tests in the file (hand formula, reference-track zero, terrain-surface) are sign-symmetric too (`allclose` against a formula that would flip with it, and a tomogram-only check). So no test in the file can detect a kz sign inversion.

THE SEARCH IS NOT MARGINALIZING A NUISANCE. I ran the helper's exact computation against test_data/ (2000 clean pixels, 28 interferograms, 29 tracks):
  height  sign=+1 -> median_err 5.369 m, within-3 m 0.068
  height  sign=-1 -> median_err 0.671 m, within-3 m 0.940   (rayleigh = 1.535)
  slant   sign=+1 -> median_err 6.711 m, within-3 m 0.051
  slant   sign=-1 -> median_err 2.013 m, within-3 m 0.833   (rayleigh = 2.615)
The data discriminates the sign by an order of magnitude, and the `+1` branch would fail both asserts (5.369 > 1.535 rayleigh; 0.068 < 0.7 band). The test passes only because the search silently selects the other branch. The composite sign is determinate in-repo, not an open convention: interferograms are built with a fixed conjugation, `phasor = primary_slc * np.conj(deramped_secondary)` (pipelines/processing/generation/interferogram.py:147-148), and production steering is `exp(+1j * kz * z)` (tools/sar/tomo_geometry.py:33-34, tools/loss/physical_loss.py `_track_steering`/`synthesise_track`).

NOT A KNOWN NON-ISSUE: this is a test-coverage gap, not the settled `capon_phase_sign = +1.0` convention itself, and not one of the listed deliberate quirks.

BLAST RADIUS (why I downgrade to minor): nothing in training depends on the kz sign. The physics loss synthesizes coherence from *both* prediction and ground truth with the same kz, so a global flip cancels — and the repo already proves this (tests/loss_metrics/test_physical_loss_safety.py:201 `test_steering_terms_invariant_to_phase_sign`). The one place the sign meets measured data, `DataConsistencyEvaluator`, computes aligned and flipped agreement at runtime and logs the "capon_phase_sign is likely inverted" warning (pipelines/backbone/inference/data_consistency.py:174, 264). So the missing assertion leaves a hole in the test net but no currently-broken production path.
correction:
Two details in the claim need fixing.

1. The proposed remedy is backwards. The auditor says "assert the winning sign is +1.0, or drop the search and beamform with the production sign only". On the shipped test_data the winning sign is -1.0, by a wide margin (median error 0.671 m vs 5.369 m for the height convention). Asserting +1.0, or hard-coding the production steering sign, would make `test_beamformed_peaks_match_pyrat_tomogram_axis` fail immediately. The correct fix is to pin the sign that actually matches PyRAT's tomogram axis for this stack (-1.0 as measured) and additionally assert that the opposite sign is clearly worse (e.g. its median error exceeds the rayleigh resolution), so a future kz sign inversion flips the test red. Note the sign being pinned here is the composite of PyRAT's internal Capon convention, the repo's `primary * conj(secondary)` interferogram convention, and the sign of `GeometryField.kz()` — it is not the same quantity as `capon_phase_sign`, so the -1.0 result is not by itself evidence that the settled `capon_phase_sign = +1.0` is wrong.

2. Scope is slightly understated in one direction and overstated in another: all five tests in the file are sign-blind, not just the two named (the hand-formula and reference-track tests compare kz against a formula that would flip along with it); but the claim that the file's "one property it should guard" is the sign overstates its purpose — the tests do genuinely pin the height-axis span, units, and the height-over-slant preference, which a sign flip does not affect.

title: Three tests can never execute or assert anything
description: Three tests in scope are structurally incapable of verifying anything: (1) `tests/orchestration/test_dataloader_tuning.py:202` is an empty `pass` body behind `@pytest.mark.skip`; (2) `tests/sar_geometry/test_sar_launchers.py:135` calls `pytest.importorskip("pyrat")` and then `pytest.skip(...)` unconditionally, so it skips even when PyRAT is installed and it never touches `run_pyrat_job` (which it imports at line 16 solely for this); (3) `tests/jepa/test_training_pipeline.py:42` is decorated `@pytest.mark.slow @pytest.mark.real_data` but its whole body is `pytest.skip(...)`. All three inflate the collected-test count without exercising code.
suggested_fix: Delete the three placeholder tests (and the now-unused `run_pyrat_job` import); record the rationale in a comment or the module docstring instead of a permanently-skipped test.
verdict_notes:
All three cited locations reproduce exactly as described, at the exact line numbers given.

(1) /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/orchestration/test_dataloader_tuning.py:202-204 — `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="real multiprocessing dataloader timing requires hardware and is not deterministic")` decorating `def test_real_benchmark_timing_skipped():` whose entire body is `pass`. Even if the skip marker were removed, the test would pass vacuously; it asserts nothing.

(2) /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/sar_geometry/test_sar_launchers.py:135-138 — `test_run_pyrat_job_requires_pyrat_runtime()` calls `pytest.importorskip("pyrat", ...)` and then, on the very next statement, `pytest.skip("does not launch the real PyRAT job in unit tests")` unconditionally. So the outcome is "skipped" in every environment, PyRAT installed or not, and the test name's promise ("requires pyrat runtime") is never checked. I grepped the whole repo for `run_pyrat_job`: in this test file it appears only in the import at line 16 and in the test's own function name — it is never called anywhere in the file. So the import at line 16 is genuinely unused (real dead import). The symbol itself is alive in production (tools/sar/tomogram_worker.py:72, exported in tools/sar/__init__.py, called at pipelines/processing/generation/tomogram.py:102), so the finding is about the test, not the function.

(3) /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/jepa/test_training_pipeline.py:40-49 — `@pytest.mark.slow` + `@pytest.mark.real_data` on `test_training_pipeline_one_epoch_produces_checkpoint()`, whose whole body is a single `pytest.skip(...)` call. Both markers are properly registered in tests/conftest.py:23-24, so they are not the reason it skips — the body is. It never touches `TrainingPipeline` beyond the module import. Selecting `-m real_data` collects it and it still skips.

None of these fall under the known-non-issues list (they are not dynamic dispatch, not legacy-fallback policy, not entry-point import ordering). The dead-code characterization holds: three collected tests that can never exercise a line of production code.

On severity: I disagree with "major". There is zero production impact — no shipped behavior is broken, no silent fallback is introduced, and each skip carries an honest, documented reason explaining the missing fixture/hardware. The real cost is inflated collected-test count and a misleading coverage impression in a ~2800-test suite, plus one unused import. That is test-suite hygiene, i.e. minor.

I also found a fourth instance of the same anti-pattern the auditor did not list, which strengthens the finding as a pattern rather than three isolated slips.
correction:
Two corrections to the claim's details.

(a) The set is incomplete — there is a fourth, arguably worse instance: /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/backbone_inference/test_loader.py:169-173, `test_full_run_load_skips_without_run_dir()`. Its body probes `Path("/ste/rnd/User/vice_vi").is_dir()` and calls `pytest.skip(...)` in the true branch, then falls through to a second `pytest.skip(...)` — both branches skip, so the directory probe is pure decoration and `RunLoader.load` is never invoked. Any fix should cover this one too.

(b) Worth stating explicitly for case (2): tests/sar_geometry/test_sar_launchers.py:16 imports `run_pyrat_job` and no code in that file ever calls it, so removing the vacuous test also removes an unused import. The `run_pyrat_job` symbol itself is NOT dead in the codebase (tools/sar/tomogram_worker.py:72 -> pipelines/processing/generation/tomogram.py:102).

Suggested remediation: delete all four, or replace each with a test that actually asserts the guard it names (e.g. for (2), assert that `run_pyrat_job` raises/returns the documented failure code when the PyRAT runtime is absent, using monkeypatched imports rather than skipping).

title: Test writes a log file into a repo-relative logs/ directory instead of tmp_path
description: `test_fit_real_window_stats_finite_and_roundtrip` constructs `Logger(log_dir="logs", ...)` with a relative path while every other test in the same suite uses `tmp_path`. The logger creates `<cwd>/logs/norm_real.log` in whatever directory pytest was invoked from — normally the repo root, which already contains a real `logs/` tree used by the webui and GPU pools. The test also never calls `logger.close()`, so the file handle stays open for the rest of the session.
suggested_fix: Take `tmp_path` as a fixture argument and use `Logger(log_dir=str(tmp_path / "logs"), ...)`, closing it at the end like the neighbouring tests do.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source and from disk state.

1. The cited line is exactly as quoted: /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/pipelines_shared/test_normalization_backbone.py:209 has `logger = Logger(log_dir="logs", name="norm_real", level="ERROR")` inside `test_fit_real_window_stats_finite_and_roundtrip`.

2. `Logger.__init__` (tools/monitoring/logger.py:126-170) treats `log_dir` as a plain path: `os.makedirs(self.log_dir, exist_ok=True)` then `logging.FileHandler(os.path.join(self.log_dir, f'{name}.log'), mode="w")`. A relative "logs" resolves against the process cwd, i.e. the directory pytest was launched from (pyproject sets only `testpaths = ["tests"]`; no conftest chdirs). `_header()` then unconditionally writes a banner through `_file_raw`/`_to_file`, which call `FileHandler.handle`/`stream.write` directly and therefore bypass the ERROR level filter — so the file is always created and written even at level="ERROR".

3. Direct evidence the write happens: `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/logs/norm_real.log` exists on disk (2833 bytes, Aug 2 11:02), sitting alongside the real operational log tree (logs/gpu_guard, logs/benchmark, collect_reports.log, ...).

4. It is the only offender in the whole suite: `grep -rn 'log_dir="[^"/]' tests/` returns exactly this one line; all ~35 other test Logger constructions use `str(tmp_path / "logs")`, `str(tmp_path)`, or `tempfile.mkdtemp()`. So the test is non-hermetic and cwd-dependent (it would also fail with PermissionError if pytest were run from a read-only cwd).

5. The missing `logger.close()` is real (the FileHandler stays open until interpreter shutdown), though this is a weaker point: most other tests also skip close(), and `Logger.__init__` closes and removes pre-existing handlers on the same logger name, so no handler accumulates.

Why I downgrade severity: nothing functionally breaks. The filename `norm_real.log` collides with no real component, the `logs/` tree is gitignored, and the test still passes. The defect is test hygiene / pollution of the user's live logs directory outside tmp_path, not a correctness bug in shipped code — "minor" fits better than "major".
correction: Two details in the claim need adjusting. (a) "every other test in the same suite uses tmp_path" — within this file line 209 is the only Logger construction at all; the tmp_path convention is what the rest of tests/ (including sibling files tests/pipelines_shared/test_splitting.py, test_datasets.py, test_normalization_profile.py) uses. (b) The claim implies the file lands amid live logs and by implication risks clobbering them; the name norm_real.log is unique so no existing log is overwritten, and logs/ is gitignored so nothing is committed. The concrete harm is limited to a stray file plus a cwd-dependent, non-hermetic test (PermissionError if cwd is read-only). Fix is one line: `Logger(log_dir=str(tmp_path / "logs"), ...)` with `tmp_path` added to the test signature, plus `logger.close()`.

title: MemoryConfig cache-clearing knobs are documented and branched on but unreachable from any entry point
description: `BaseTrainer` branches on `config.memory.clear_cache_every_n_steps` (tools/training/trainer.py:225), `clear_cache_after_eval` (:337) and `clear_cache_after_epoch` (:460), logs all three in the loop banner (:114), and webui/config_descriptions.json:1429-1431 describes them as user-facing settings. But `MemoryConfig` is constructed in exactly one place in production (`grep -rn 'MemoryConfig(' --include=*.py` -> only this line) and only `reserve_vram`/`vram_keep_free_gb` are passed. No entry config exposes the three cache fields, so they are permanently 0/False/False and the three trainer branches are dead. Either they are settings (and need entry-config fields plumbed through here) or they are not (and the config fields, the trainer branches and the descriptions should go).
suggested_fix: Add clear_cache_every_n_steps / clear_cache_after_eval / clear_cache_after_epoch to TrainingQueueConfig and forward them here, or delete the three MemoryConfig fields, the trainer branches and their config_descriptions entries.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced the whole chain from source.

1. `MemoryConfig` (configuration/training/general/runtime.py:38-44) has five fields: `clear_cache_every_n_steps=0`, `clear_cache_after_eval=False`, `clear_cache_after_epoch=False`, `reserve_vram=False`, `vram_keep_free_gb=1.0`.

2. The only site that constructs it with non-default values is pipelines/shared/config/config_factory.py:90, and it passes only `reserve_vram` and `vram_keep_free_gb`. The other four occurrences (configuration/training/backbone.py:218, jepa.py:79, image_autoencoder.py:37, profile_autoencoder.py:36) are `field(default_factory=MemoryConfig)`, i.e. all-defaults — and every non-backbone pipeline then calls `trainer_config.inherit_shared_from(base)` (configuration/training/general/trainer.py:3-12 lists `"memory"` in `_SHARED_SUBCONFIGS`), so the JEPA / profile-AE / image-AE trainers all end up with the exact object built at config_factory.py:90. Every BaseTrainer-driven family therefore gets the three cache fields at 0/False/False.

3. No entry config exposes them. `TrainingQueueConfig` (configuration/training/general/run.py:51-52) and `UnrolledTrainingConfig` (configuration/training/unrolled.py:29-30) expose `reserve_vram`/`vram_keep_free_gb` and nothing about cache clearing; `BackboneEntryConfig` has no `memory` sub-config at all. `ConfigCli` (tools/runtime/config_cli.py:50-68, `_leaves`) only builds `--<dotted.path>` options from leaves of the entry config, so there is no CLI route either. webui/launch_layout.py mentions only `{"gate": "reserve_vram", "fields": ["vram_keep_free_gb"]}` (lines 243, 268). A repo-wide grep for `clear_cache` (excluding `torch.cuda.empty_cache` and the unrelated `jax.clear_caches()` in pipelines/processing/param_extraction/sigma/extractor.py:488) returns only the dataclass definition, the trainer, and config_descriptions.json — nothing in tests/, main/, webui/static/js, or any JSON registry sets them.

4. Consequently the three trainer branches never fire: tools/training/trainer.py:225 reads `clear_n = ...clear_cache_every_n_steps` and line 281 `if clear_n > 0 and self.global_step % clear_n == 0` is always false; line 337-338 `if self.config.memory.clear_cache_after_eval` always false; line 460-461 `if self.config.memory.clear_cache_after_epoch` always false. The banner at line 114 always prints `every_n_steps=0, after_eval=False, after_epoch=False`.

So the claim's substance holds: three documented knobs are permanently unsettable and three branches are unreachable. Effect on results is nil (the defaults are the "off" state); the harm is misleading config surface plus dead branches, which is why I adjust the severity down.
correction:
Three details in the claim need adjustment.

(a) "MemoryConfig is constructed in exactly one place in production" is imprecise — it is also instantiated via `field(default_factory=MemoryConfig)` in four trainer configs (configuration/training/backbone.py:218, jepa.py:79, image_autoencoder.py:37, profile_autoencoder.py:36). The conclusion survives because those defaults are all-off and every pipeline overwrites `memory` from the config_factory base through `inherit_shared_from` (`"memory"` is in `_SHARED_SUBCONFIGS`, configuration/training/general/trainer.py:5).

(b) The webui evidence is weaker than presented. config_descriptions.json is the Config-reference browser over the `configuration/` dataclasses, not the launch form, and tests/webui/test_config_registry_descriptions.py::test_every_field_has_a_description *requires* a description for every dataclass field. So lines 1429-1431 exist because the fields exist; they are not independent proof that anyone intended these as user-facing launch settings. (They do still mislead a reader of the Config tab, which is part of the harm.)

(c) `_clear_cuda_cache` itself is NOT dead — tools/training/trainer.py:412 calls it unconditionally at the start of `train()`, and it refills the VRAM reservation (tools/training/trainer.py:204-207), which is covered by tests/training_runtime/test_trainer.py:77-90. Only the three conditional call sites are unreachable, and the step-based one is at line 281 (line 225 merely reads the value into `clear_n`).

Also worth stating in the fix framing: since `reserve_vram` re-reservation happens inside `_clear_cuda_cache`, the periodic "re-claim VRAM during training" behavior described at config_descriptions.json:1432 ("and again after every CUDA cache clear") effectively never happens after the initial call at line 412 — the reservation is only refilled once per run.

title: FitSettings.max_fit_iterations is a config field nothing reads (its own webui description admits it)
description: `grep -rn 'max_fit_iterations\|max_nfev\|maxfev\|fit_iterations' --include=*.py --include=*.json --include=*.js .` returns exactly three hits: the declaration, a `> 0` smoke assertion in tests/configuration/test_param.py:36, and the webui description string. The extractor uses `adam_steps` instead. The webui text itself says "not read by the Adam extractor", i.e. the dead field is shipped to users as a knob with a note that it does nothing.
evidence:
max_fit_iterations : int       = 5000
...
webui/config_descriptions.json:143: "max_fit_iterations": "nominal iteration cap for the profile fit; not read by the Adam extractor, which uses adam_steps instead",
suggested_fix: Delete the field, its config_descriptions entry and the test assertion.
verdict_notes: I reproduced the grep with no --include filters (all file types, whole tree minus .git) and got exactly three hits: the declaration at /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/configuration/param_extraction.py:52, the smoke assertion at /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/configuration/test_param.py:36 (`assert cfg.max_fit_iterations > 0`), and the doc string in /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/config_descriptions.json:143. I then checked the dynamic-dispatch escape hatches the protocol warns about: no `asdict`/`vars`/`__dataclass_fields__` reflection anywhere under pipelines/processing/param_extraction/; the run metadata writer (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/processing/param_extraction/io.py:41-61) enumerates fit fields explicitly and does not include it; queue.py:62 builds `FitSettings(fit_config=fit_config)` leaving the default untouched; the actual iteration budget flows from `ExtractionConfig.adam_steps` -> pipeline.py:104 -> sigma/extractor.py:39,169,250 into the JAX Adam kernel. So the field is genuinely read by nothing but a test that asserts it is positive. The claim is factually correct.
correction: Two details in the claim are wrong and lower its weight. (1) "shipped to users as a knob" is not true. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/launch_layout.py:532-563 defines the extract_params launch form over `ExtractParamsEntryConfig`, which has no `max_fit_iterations` field at all — the exposed fit knobs are fit_threshold_factor, fit_truncation_index, fit_prominence_frac, fit_activity_threshold, adam_steps, adam_lr. The only place a user sees the field is the read-only Config documentation tab, which /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/config_registry.py builds by AST-walking every dataclass in configuration/ and requiring a description entry per field (_attach_descriptions indexes `field_descs[field["name"]]` with no .get). So the config_descriptions.json line is not an independent smell — it is a mandatory entry that exists only because the field exists, and its author honestly documented the field as unread rather than inventing a purpose. (2) Severity: this is an unused default on a config dataclass with zero behavioural consequence (no wrong results, no crash, no silent fallback), so it is minor housekeeping, not major. Note there is a sibling case in the same file that the audit should fold in rather than treat separately: `ExtractionConfig.pyrat_directory` (line 78) is documented at config_descriptions.json:149 as "carried on the config but not read by this extraction pipeline". Fix for both: delete the fields, drop their config_descriptions.json entries, and drop the `> 0` assertion at tests/configuration/test_param.py:36.

title: packages.find silently ships zero pipelines/ packages because pipelines/ has no __init__.py
description: `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` explicitly lists `"pipelines*"`, but `pipelines/` is the only top-level source directory without an `__init__.py` (configuration/, models/, tools/, tests/ all have one). setuptools' `find` (not `find_namespace`) stops at a directory that is not a regular package and never descends, so no `pipelines.*` subpackage is discovered either. Verified by running setuptools' find_packages with the exact include list: the result contains configuration.*, models.*, tools.* and nothing from pipelines. Every entry point in main/ imports `pipelines.…`, so an installed distribution would be import-broken while the declaration reads as if pipelines were covered. Either add `pipelines/__init__.py` or switch to `find_namespace`.
suggested_fix: Add an empty `pipelines/__init__.py` (matching the convention of the other four packages), or change the table to `[tool.setuptools.packages.find-namespace]`.
verdict_notes:
Mechanism independently reproduced from source. pipelines/ is the only top-level source dir in the include list without an __init__.py (configuration/, models/, tools/, tests/ all have one), while all 15 of its subdirectories DO have __init__.py. Running setuptools find_packages(where='.', include=["configuration*","models*","pipelines*","tools*"]) returns 33 packages whose top-level set is exactly ['configuration','models','tools'] — zero pipelines entries; find_namespace_packages with the identical include returns 44 pipelines.* entries. The cause is explicit in setuptools.discovery.PackageFinder._find_iter: a directory failing _looks_like_package hits `continue` BEFORE being appended back to `dirs`, so the walk never descends into pipelines/ and none of its valid subpackages are reachable. So the declaration on line 32 reads as if pipelines were covered while shipping nothing from it.

However the auditor's stated impact is hypothetical, not current. Nothing in the repo builds or installs the distribution: importlib.metadata.version('dlr-tomosar') raises PackageNotFoundError, no *.egg-info or dist-info exists, README.md lines 29-30 document only `pip install -r requirements.txt` plus extras (never `pip install .`/`-e .`), there is no CI directory, no build script in scripts/, and no test references pyproject or find_packages. All execution resolves imports from source instead: main/_bootstrap.py inserts _REPO_ROOT into sys.path, and pytest runs from the repo root with testpaths=["tests"]. Additionally main/ and webui/ are also absent from the include list, so even a correctly built wheel would carry no entry points — the wheel is not a usable deliverable regardless. This is a latent packaging-metadata defect worth fixing (the vault rule states each project is an installable package), but it breaks no path that runs today, so "major" overstates it.
correction: Two corrections. (1) Mechanism detail: the claim reads as though pipelines/ lacks package structure generally; in fact every one of its 15 subdirectories has an __init__.py. Only the top-level pipelines/ directory is missing one, and that alone is what aborts the walk (setuptools' _find_iter `continue`s past a non-package without appending it to `dirs`), hiding all 44 otherwise-valid pipelines.* subpackages. (2) Impact: "an installed distribution would be import-broken" describes a scenario that never occurs in this repo — the project is never pip-installed (no dist metadata, no CI, README installs only requirements.txt), and all imports resolve via main/_bootstrap.py's sys.path insertion and pytest's repo-root rootdir. Severity should be minor (latent packaging metadata), not major. The suggested fixes (add pipelines/__init__.py, or switch to find_namespace) are both correct; note that main/ and webui/ are also unpackaged, so an installable wheel would need more than this one-line fix to be functional.

title: pandas is a hard runtime dependency but is declared nowhere
description: `tools/benchmarking/sweep_report.py` imports pandas at module level. It is re-exported by `tools/benchmarking/__init__.py` and imported eagerly by `pipelines/dataloader_tuning/pipeline.py` (`from tools.benchmarking import LoaderSpec, GpuFeedBenchmark, DataLoaderSweep, SweepReport`), which is the whole body of `main/experiments/tune_dataloader.py`. pandas appears in neither `requirements.txt` nor `pyproject.toml` `dependencies` nor any optional extra. A fresh environment built exactly as README section 1 prescribes will therefore ImportError on the dataloader-tuning entry point. (`STEtools`, imported in tools/baselines/reading.py:27, is likewise undeclared, but it is a deferred import of an external DLR package that README section 5 at least half-documents alongside PyRAT.)
suggested_fix: Add `pandas` to `requirements.txt` and to `pyproject.toml` `dependencies` (or to a `benchmark` optional extra together with a deferred import), and mention STEtools next to PyRAT in README section 5.
verdict_notes: Independently reproduced. tools/benchmarking/sweep_report.py:6 imports pandas at module level, and a whole-repo grep for "pandas" (excluding runs/, results/, logs/) returns that single file — it is absent from requirements.txt, from pyproject.toml [project] dependencies, and from all three optional extras (processing, sigma, dev). README section 1 installs requirements.txt plus only h5py, jax, pytest, pyflakes, so a fresh Dune env has no pandas; the reference machine merely happens to have pandas 3.0.1 installed, which masks it. Blocking pandas via a sys.meta_path hook and importing from the repo root with the Dune interpreter yields "ImportError No module named 'pandas'" for pipelines.dataloader_tuning.pipeline, pipelines.shared.training.pretrain_preflight, and pipelines.backbone.training.launcher. This is not one of the known non-issues: it is not a deferred import in main/, it is an undeclared third-party module-level import inside tools/.
correction: The mechanism is correct but the blast radius is understated. The claim scopes the breakage to main/experiments/tune_dataloader.py via pipelines/dataloader_tuning/pipeline.py. There is a second, far more important path: tools/training/pretraining/loader_tuner.py:10 does `from tools.benchmarking import LoaderSpec, GpuFeedBenchmark, DataLoaderSweep, SweepReport`; loader_tuner is re-exported by tools/training/pretraining/__init__.py:3, which pipelines/shared/training/pretrain_preflight.py:9 imports wholesale, and that module is imported by pipelines/backbone/training/launcher.py:106, pipelines/unrolled/training/pipeline.py:18, and pipelines/shared/training/training_runner.py:6. So every training entry point fails at import in a README-built environment, not just the dataloader-tuning one. Additionally, tests/orchestration/test_dataloader_tuning.py:6 and tests/dataloader_tuning/test_pipeline.py:11 import SweepReport at module level, so `python -m pytest -q` (README section 2, described as "your proof the environment is correct") errors during collection on a clean clone. Fix: add pandas to requirements.txt and pyproject.toml dependencies, or drop the single pandas usage in SweepReport, which only wraps a small list of dicts in a DataFrame. Severity major stands.

title: All three tracked deck-figure scripts import a Logger from outside the repository
description:
`joint_error_heatmap.py:4`, `patch_sweep_heatmap.py:5` and `gen_dual_round2_tables.py:5` all walk up the parent chain looking for `

/code/tools/logger.py` and then `from tools.logger import Logger`. `tools/logger.py` does not exist in this repository — the refactor moved it to `tools/monitoring/logger.py`. On the author's machine the search escapes the repo and resolves to `/home/bard/Bard/code/tools/logger.py`, i.e. a different project's package (I confirmed the script runs and silently binds to that foreign module). On any fresh clone the generator expression finds nothing and raises `StopIteration` at import time. README section 6 tells users these decks are rebuildable from a fresh clone. `gen_dual_round2_tables.py` compounds this by hardcoding the author's vault layout in its entry point: `DualRound2Tables(_vault / "code" / "DLR-TomoSAR").run()`.
evidence: _vault = next(p for p in Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / "code" / "tools" / "logger.py").exists())
suggested_fix: Locate the repo root relative to `__file__` (`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`) and import `from tools.monitoring.logger import Logger`; drop the `_vault` search and the `code/DLR-TomoSAR` literal.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced directly.

Foreign bind on the author's machine: running the exact bootstrap from the deck directory with the Dune interpreter gives `vault= /home/bard/Bard` and `bound to /home/bard/Bard/code/tools/logger.py`. That path is outside the repository (`/home/bard/Bard/code/` contains Bomar, DLR-TomoSAR, DUNE-GNN, ..., and a shared `tools/`). The repository's own Logger is at `tools/monitoring/logger.py` — `ls` confirms there is no `tools/logger.py` in DLR-TomoSAR, so the search cannot ever stop inside the repo; escaping is structural, not incidental.

Fresh-clone failure: I copied the three scripts to a scratch path with no vault ancestor and ran `joint_error_heatmap.py`; it dies at line 4 with `StopIteration` inside the generator expression, at import time, before matplotlib or anything else. title: Both READMEs claim the webui backend is standard-library only; it imports numpy, matplotlib, scipy and torch at boot
description: webui/README.md:17 says "The backend is **standard-library only** (`http.server` + server-sent events), so it needs no extra installation" and README.md:111 repeats "The backend is standard library only, so nothing extra to install." `web_ui_server.py` eagerly imports `cube_explorer`, `fit_lab`, `model_probe`, `ab_autopsy` and `triage_board`, which import numpy and matplotlib at module level, plus `tools.*` which drags in torch and scipy. The claim misleads anyone trying to run the console on a machine without the training stack — exactly the scenario the sentence exists to cover.
evidence: The backend is **standard-library only** (`http.server` + server-sent events), so it
suggested_fix: Correct both sentences to say the HTTP layer uses only the stdlib but the console requires the project environment (numpy/matplotlib/torch), or make the heavy tabs lazily imported so the claim becomes true.
verdict_notes:

/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/serve.py:9 does `from web_ui_server import WebUIServer`, so this is the boot path, not a cold branch.

This is not one of the listed known non-issues: it is not a deferred import in `main/`, not a legacy-fallback question, and not dynamic dispatch. It is a straightforward documentation-versus-code contradiction.
