title: Multi-type launch pages expose config panels that the non-backbone pipelines silently ignore
description:
The `benchmark`, `cross_validate` and `tune` pages are `type_tab` pages whose `training_type` selects a completely different pipeline. Several sections are correctly gated with `when` (`size-match` on backbone, `ae-loss`, `jepa`, and tune's `loss`), but the following are NOT gated even though the selected pipeline never reads them:

- `benchmark` "Input channels" panel (line 890) -> `BenchmarkConfig.input` is only consumed by `TrainingWorker._run_backbone` (pipelines/benchmark/workers.py:157). For training_type in (jepa, profile_autoencoder) the dataset comes from `ConfigFactory.training_dataset_config()`, which hardcodes `InputConfig.full_stack()` (pipelines/shared/config/config_factory.py:30). A user who deselects interferograms for a JEPA benchmark silently trains on the full stack.
- `benchmark` "Loss" section (line 901) -> `BenchmarkConfig.loss` is only used for backbone (_apply_loss_component, SeedExpandedStage.unit_base); JEPA uses jepa.param_loss, profile-AE uses ae_loss.
- `benchmark` "Max-batch probe" panel (line 897) -> `BenchmarkConfig.runs_max_batch()` returns True only for backbone.
- `cross_validate` "Loss" section (line 968) -> cv.curriculum is applied only in FoldTrainingWorker._run_backbone; _jepa_entry_config/_ae_entry_config never pass it.
- `cross_validate` Normalization/Augmentation panels (lines 962-963) -> _ae_entry_config cannot pass them (ProfileAeEntryConfig has neither field).
- `tune` Normalization/Augmentation panels (lines 1068-1069) -> TuningWorker._ae_entry_template does not pass them for profile_autoencoder.

Because the fields exist on the entry dataclass, LaunchLayout._validate is satisfied and nothing errors; the values are just dropped. The unrolled pipeline handles the analogous case explicitly with _warn_inert_augmentation, which shows the intended behaviour is to warn, not to silently drop.
suggested_fix: Add `"when": {"field": "training_type", "in": [...]}` to the benchmark Input-channels / Loss / Max-batch panels and the cross_validate Loss / Normalization / Augmentation and tune Normalization / Augmentation panels, mirroring the gating already used for size-match and tune's loss. Alternatively emit a loud warning from the non-backbone workers when an inert field deviates from its default.
verdict_notes: Reproduced every sub-claim from source. (1) BenchmarkConfig.input is consumed only at pipelines/benchmark/workers.py:154 inside TrainingWorker._run_backbone; the JEPA path (pipelines/jepa/training/pipeline.py:79) builds its dataset from ConfigFactory.training_dataset_config(), whose input_config is the hardcoded InputConfig.full_stack() (pipelines/shared/config/config_factory.py:29-30,55), and JepaEntryConfig has no input field — the train_jepa layout correctly exposes no Input panel, confirming the intended per-type surface. (2) BenchmarkConfig.loss is referenced only in _apply_loss_component (workers.py:29), batch_probe.py:53 (a backbone-only stage), and SeedExpandedStage.unit_base (stages.py:44-49) under an explicit training_type == "backbone" branch; jepa naming uses jepa.param_loss and profile_ae uses the bare model name. (3) runs_max_batch() is `self.training_type == "backbone"` (configuration/benchmark/general.py:116) and is the sole gate at pipelines/benchmark/pipeline.py:99. (4) cv.curriculum is applied only at pipelines/cross_validation/workers.py:137 in _run_backbone; _jepa_entry_config and _ae_entry_config never pass it. (5) ProfileAeEntryConfig (configuration/training/profile_autoencoder.py:41-65) has no normalization or augmentation field — profile-AE uses its own ProfileNormalizer — so cross_validate/_ae_entry_config (workers.py:193) and TuningWorker._ae_entry_template (pipelines/tuning/workers.py:26) cannot pass them, while the sibling _image_ae_entry_template and _jepa_entry_template do. Mechanism verified: LaunchLayout._claims traverses all sections irrespective of `when`, so _validate's claim-every-leaf-exactly-once rule is satisfied by a gated section just as by an ungated one; gating costs nothing, and the JS supports only section-level `when` (launch_widgets.js:5065-5067), which the existing size-match/ae-loss/jepa sections already demonstrate. No test in tests/webui/test_launch_layout.py pins the current gating set, so it is not an encoded intent. The unrolled pipeline's _warn_inert_augmentation (pipelines/unrolled/training/pipeline.py:100-105, tested in tests/unrolled_training/test_pipeline_guards.py:132) confirms the project's intended handling is a loud warning, consistent with the no-silent-fallback policy. Not one of the listed known non-issues.
correction: Two refinements plus one aggravating fact. (a) Scope precision: the cross_validate and tune Normalization/Augmentation panels are inert only on the profile_autoencoder tab — the jepa (and tune's image_autoencoder) paths do forward both fields; the benchmark Input/Loss/Max-batch panels are inert on both non-backbone tabs. (b) The auditor's list is incomplete in the same direction: benchmark's own Normalization, Augmentation and Geometry panels are likewise dropped on the Profile AE tab, since BenchmarkWorker._ae_entry_config (pipelines/benchmark/workers.py:60-72) passes only run_name/seed/logdir/pixel_subsample/keep_empty_frac/ae_model_name/ae_loss/paths/training/overfit_check. (c) Severity stays major and is arguably understated: StagedPipeline.__init__ writes ConfigCli.save_resolved(config, pipeline/resolved_config.json) (pipelines/shared/orchestration/staged_pipeline.py:24), so the dropped values are not merely ignored at runtime — they are archived into the run record, leaving an artifact that claims e.g. input.use_interferograms=false for a JEPA benchmark that actually trained on the full stack. Fix: move the affected panels into their own `when`-gated sections (the pattern already used for size-match/ae-loss/jepa), or add a _warn_inert_* guard in the non-backbone worker paths.

title: LossScaleProbeConfig.enabled_losses can never be set from any entry point
description: `LossScaleProbe.__init__` validates and applies `probe_cfg.enabled_losses` per-term (pipelines/backbone/training/loss_probe.py:28-35), but the only two production constructors of `LossScaleProbeConfig` hardcode `enabled_losses = {}` (here and pipelines/shared/training/worker_base.py:20), and `BackboneEntryConfig`/`DualEntryConfig` expose only `probe_enabled`, `probe_n_batches`, `probe_reference`, `probe_exit_after` -- there is no `probe_enabled_losses` field for ConfigCli to override. The override machinery is only reachable from tests/backbone_training/test_loss_probe.py, so the documented ability to force individual probe terms on/off (webui/equation_library.py:950 describes it) is unreachable in practice.
suggested_fix: Either add a `probe_enabled_losses: dict` field to the entry configs and wire it through `_probe_config`, or delete the `enabled_losses` field and its handling in LossScaleProbe.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. LossScaleProbeConfig.enabled_losses (configuration/training/backbone.py:203) is really consumed by LossScaleProbe.__init__ (pipelines/backbone/training/loss_probe.py:27-39: unknown-key validation, then per-term use_flag override with DEFAULT_OFF fallback). But the only two production constructors of LossScaleProbeConfig are pipelines/backbone/training/launcher.py:79-86 and pipelines/shared/training/worker_base.py:14-21, both passing enabled_losses = {}. LossScaleProbeConfig is not nested inside BackboneEntryConfig/DualEntryConfig/BackboneTrainerConfig, and those entry configs expose only probe_enabled/probe_n_batches/probe_reference/probe_exit_after (configuration/training/backbone.py:243-246, configuration/training/dual.py:112-115). ConfigCli builds flags by walking dataclass leaves of the entry config only (tools/runtime/config_cli.py:39-48, 62-69), so no --...enabled_losses option is ever registered. webui/launch_layout.py:610 and :784 expose the same four probe fields and nothing more. A repo-wide grep for "enabled_losses" (tests/, webui JS, JSON registries included) returns only: the two hardcoded {} literals, the three consumer lines in loss_probe.py, the dataclass field, tests/backbone_training/test_loss_probe.py:46,60, and two user-facing docs that advertise the feature (webui/equation_library.py:950, webui/config_descriptions.json:1132). I also checked the dual path is not a separate constructor: DualSingleTrainRunner subclasses SingleTrainRunner and inherits _probe_config unchanged (pipelines/dual/training/launcher.py:22), so dual has the same gap; the dual probe_* fields themselves are consumed correctly. Conclusion: the per-term probe override is reachable only from unit tests, while being documented as a user-facing knob — a real, minor config-contract gap (tunable with no entry-point route), not a false positive from dynamic dispatch.
correction: Two details to adjust. (1) The hardcoded `enabled_losses = {}` at launcher.py:85 and worker_base.py:20 is identical to the dataclass default (field(default_factory=dict)), so it is redundant rather than the cause; the actual defect is the absence of a `probe_enabled_losses`-style field on BackboneEntryConfig/DualEntryConfig, i.e. the anchor is better placed at configuration/training/backbone.py:243-246. (2) The claim understates reach slightly: worker_base's constructor is shared by three worker pipelines (benchmark/workers.py:169, patch_sweep/workers.py:49, cross_validation/workers.py:152), all of which disable the probe entirely anyway, and the dual entry inherits the backbone launcher's _probe_config, so both backbone and dual entry points are affected. A fix is straightforward since ConfigCli's _SUPPORTED_TYPES already includes dict (tools/runtime/config_cli.py:14).

title: Package-level re-export shims in backbone/training and backbone/dataset are never used
description: `pipelines/backbone/training/__init__.py` defines a lazy `__getattr__` re-exporting Trainer, TrainingPipeline, TrainingRunMetadata and SingleTrainRunner, but a repo-wide grep (including tests/, main/, webui/ and webui/repomap_data.json) finds no `from pipelines.backbone.training import ...` anywhere -- every caller imports the submodule directly (`pipelines.backbone.training.trainer`, `.pipeline`, `.launcher`). The same holds for `pipelines/backbone/dataset/__init__.py`, whose 10 eager re-exports and 13-entry `__all__` are never consumed by name; worse, being eager they force `augmentation`, `datasets`, `normalizer`, `stats_computer`, `pipeline`, `metadata_writer` and `spatial` (plus shared `loaders`/`dataset_spatial`) to be imported whenever any single submodule is imported.
suggested_fix: Delete both re-export shims (or, if the package-level API is wanted, convert callers to use it) so there is one import path per symbol.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/training/__init__.py lines 1-22 is exactly the quoted lazy __getattr__ shim re-exporting Trainer, TrainingPipeline, TrainingRunMetadata, SingleTrainRunner. A repo-wide grep for "backbone.training import", "backbone import training", "backbone.dataset import", "backbone import dataset" across *.py, *.js, *.json and *.md (tests/, main/, webui/, webui/repomap_data.json included) returns zero hits. Every actual consumer imports the submodule directly: pipelines/dual/training/launcher.py:11 (from pipelines.backbone.training.launcher import SingleTrainRunner), pipelines/dual/training/pipeline.py:5, pipelines/patch_sweep/workers.py:25, pipelines/benchmark/batch_probe.py:15. TrainingRunMetadata is universally imported from pipelines.shared.config.run_metadata, never through the shim. Same result for all 10 eager re-exports in pipelines/backbone/dataset/__init__.py: I grepped each name (Cropper, Patcher, GridInfo, Normalizer, StatsComputer, MetadataWriter, SpatialAugmenter, MultiRegionDataset, PatchDataset, DatasetPipeline) and found zero package-level imports. Checked the dynamic-dispatch escape hatches the protocol demands: repomap_data.json only ever references concrete module file paths (pipelines/backbone/dataset/pipeline.py, spatial.py, datasets.py, augmentation.py, stats_computer.py, normalizer.py, metadata_writer.py), never the package name; no importlib.import_module call anywhere targets these packages (the only lazy-package pattern in the repo is tools/runtime/__init__.py, unrelated). No test references the package __init__ files. So the dead-code claim stands. I do not endorse the auditor's secondary "worse, being eager" framing: the forced submodule imports happen once at import time on a cold path, and pipelines/backbone/dataset/pipeline.py already imports every one of those modules itself, so there is no measurable waste and no severity bump. Severity remains minor: cosmetic dead code, no behavioural failure.
correction: Scope is understated. The dead re-export shim is a repo-wide pattern, not limited to the two cited files. Of the 11 non-empty __init__.py files under pipelines/, only two have real consumers: pipelines/backbone/inference/plots (used at pipelines/backbone/inference/animation.py:18) and pipelines/processing/param_extraction/sigma (used at pipelines/processing/param_extraction/pipeline.py:38). The other nine are equally unconsumed and should be part of the same cleanup: pipelines/backbone/training, pipelines/backbone/dataset, pipelines/jepa/training, pipelines/profile_autoencoder/training, pipelines/profile_autoencoder/dataset, pipelines/tuning, pipelines/dataloader_tuning, pipelines/processing/external_params, pipelines/processing/generation, pipelines/processing/param_extraction, pipelines/processing/param_extraction/plots. Two smaller detail fixes: the dataset __init__ also eagerly imports pipelines.backbone.dataset.stats (Stats), which the auditor's list omits; and the "worse, being eager they force ... imports" clause should be dropped, since it is a one-time cold-path import cost and pipelines/backbone/dataset/pipeline.py imports the same modules directly anyway. Supporting argument for deletion rather than retention: these are consumer-less convenience shims, which runs against the project's stated no-legacy-fallbacks / break-loudly policy.

title: Curriculum swap writes an un-decayed base LR when only the warmup is reset, then it is overwritten anyway
description: The immediate-LR fixup fires when `reset_lr OR reset_warmup`, but it always multiplies `lr_scheduler.base_lrs`. With `reset_lr=False, reset_warmup=True` the scheduler's `current_lrs` are the decayed values, so this sets the optimizer back to the *undecayed* base LR and logs "Optimizer LR set to warmup-adjusted value" -- a value the schedule never intended. It has no lasting effect only because `BaseTrainer.train_epoch` calls `_update_optimizer(self.lr_scheduler.effective_lrs())` on the very first batch of the same epoch (tools/training/trainer.py:241), which restores `current_lrs * warmup_factor`. The block is therefore both wrong in intent and dead in effect, and its log line is misleading.
evidence:
immediate_lrs = [lr * warmup_factor for lr in self.lr_scheduler.base_lrs]
            self.update_optimizer(immediate_lrs)
suggested_fix: Use `self.lr_scheduler.effective_lrs()` (or `current_lrs`) instead of `base_lrs`, or drop the block entirely since train_epoch re-applies the correct LR before the first step.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. pipelines/backbone/training/trainer.py:53-57 gates on `reset_lr or reset_warmup` but unconditionally derives the immediate LR from `lr_scheduler.base_lrs`. Scheduler.reset() (tools/training/scheduling.py:175-179) sets `current_lrs = base_lrs`, so with reset_lr=True the block equals `effective_lrs()` and is benign. With reset_lr=False and reset_warmup=True, `current_lrs` still holds the decayed values written by Scheduler.step() (scheduling.py:183), so the block pushes `base_lr * warmup_factor` into the optimizer -- for a cosine schedule swapping near mid-horizon that is roughly 2x the scheduled LR -- while logging "Optimizer LR set to warmup-adjusted value", a value the schedule never intended. The write is then discarded: `_before_epoch` -> `maybe_swap` runs immediately before `train_epoch`, whose first loop iteration calls `self._update_optimizer(self.lr_scheduler.effective_lrs())` at tools/training/trainer.py:241, before `_compute_loss` and before any `optimizer.step()` (line 269); the end-of-epoch block at lines 463-464 corrects it again. So no gradient step ever runs at the wrong LR, confirming both halves of the claim (wrong in intent, dead in effect). The combination is reachable: reset_lr and reset_warmup are independent bools defaulting to False in configuration/training/general/loss.py:93-94 and both exposed in webui/launch_layout.py:434. No test encodes this fixup's semantics (tests/backbone_training/test_trainer.py:266-299 covers only scheduler reset and loss-config swap), and the pattern occurs exactly once in the repo (unrolled trainer has no equivalent). Not one of the listed known non-issues.
correction: Two refinements. (1) The defect is exclusive to the reset_lr=False, reset_warmup=True combination; when reset_lr=True the block is numerically correct because Scheduler.reset() has just restored current_lrs to base_lrs. (2) The residue is not purely a log line: `BaseTrainer._update_optimizer` (tools/training/trainer.py:196-203) also emits an `optim/lr/<name>` TensorBoard scalar whenever the value changes, so the un-decayed LR is written into the scalar stream at the current global_step and is immediately followed by the correct value at that same step, producing a duplicated/misleading point in the LR curve. Severity minor is right -- no training dynamics are affected.

title: ParamSampler and SlotVitals freeze amp_zero_thr at the warmup stage and never follow the curriculum swap
description: Both diagnostics are constructed once from `self.initial_loss_cfg.amp_zero_thr` (the warmup stage when the curriculum is enabled) and that threshold is never refreshed by `CurriculumController.maybe_swap` or `_on_state_restored`. Everything else that consumes the same threshold reads it live: `Loss._param_term`/`_physical_errors`/`_occupancy` use `self.loss_cfg.amp_zero_thr`, and `ReconstructionFigures.capture_reference` builds its ExampleSelector from `criterion.loss_cfg.amp_zero_thr` (diagnostics.py:315). If `curriculum.complete.amp_zero_thr` differs from `curriculum.warmup.amp_zero_thr`, the slot_vitals active-fraction / usage-entropy scalars and the param histograms are computed against a stale threshold for the whole complete phase, silently disagreeing with the occupancy scalars logged from the same batch.
suggested_fix: Have ParamSampler/SlotVitals read the threshold from the criterion at begin() time, or push the new stage's amp_zero_thr into them from CurriculumController.maybe_swap and Trainer._on_state_restored.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. trainer.py:70 binds initial_loss_cfg to curriculum.warmup when the curriculum is enabled (configuration/training/general/loss.py:97-99), and lines 73-74 copy that stage's amp_zero_thr into ParamSampler.thr and SlotVitals.thr as plain attributes (diagnostics.py:17, :70). CurriculumController.maybe_swap (trainer.py:30) and _on_state_restored (trainer.py:153-156) only call Loss.set_curriculum, which rebinds Loss.loss_cfg (loss.py:73-84) and touches nothing else; a repo-wide grep shows no other write to those .thr attributes. Meanwhile Loss reads the threshold live in _param_term (loss.py:103), _physical_errors (:135), _match_params (:158) and _occupancy (:233). Concrete failure: post-swap, for the same pred_params_phys in one validation batch, _occupancy emits pred_active_frac / pred_active_slot{g} using complete.amp_zero_thr while SlotVitals.observe (diagnostics.py:89) emits slot_vitals/active_frac and usage_entropy using warmup.amp_zero_thr, and ParamSampler.observe (diagnostics.py:30) filters histogram samples with the same stale threshold — e.g. warmup 1e-4 vs complete 1e-3 makes the two families of scalars count different slots as active, silently, in the same TensorBoard run. Not one of the listed known non-issues; no test encodes the frozen behaviour as intended (tests/backbone_training/test_diagnostics.py only constructs the objects with a literal threshold, and the curriculum tests in test_trainer.py never touch amp_zero_thr). Severity stays minor because it is latent: CurriculumInheritance.apply (loss.py:112-134) copies complete-stage values into warmup for any field overridden only on complete, so the shipped presets (webui/launch_layout.py:130) keep both stages equal; divergence requires the user to explicitly set curriculum.warmup.amp_zero_thr (exposed by the webui "Loss stages" pair panel, launch_layout.py:617/:791 with amp_zero_thr in the loss template at :188) or set curriculum.inherit=False. It affects diagnostics only, never the gradient.
correction: Mechanism and line numbers are right (trainer.py:73-74). title: The crop always materialises primary + secondaries + interferograms regardless of input_config
description: `Cropper._stack_inputs` loads and copies all three artifacts into one contiguous in-RAM array with no reference to `input_config.use_primary/use_secondaries/use_interferograms`, and `PatchDataset.__getitem__` then calls `self.grid.extract(self.inputs, idx)` (datasets.py:128), copying every layer of that stack for every patch before `_build_input_tensor` discards the disabled ones. For the input-trial variants that deliberately disable channels while widening the track set -- e.g. `noamp-allsec-ifg` (`use_primary=False, use_secondaries=False, tracks=all`, configuration/training/backbone.py:_default_input_trials) -- this holds the whole unused secondaries stack in RAM (complex64 x n_secondaries x azimuth x range, several GB for the all-track crop) and doubles the per-sample memcpy in every dataloader worker.

inputs_split                      = np.empty((n_passes, az_size, rg_size), dtype=primary.dtype)
        inputs_split[0]                   = primary_view
        inputs_split[1:1 + n_secondaries] = secondaries_view
        inputs_split[1 + n_secondaries:]  = interferograms_view

1. `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/dataset/spatial.py:53-73` (`Cropper._stack_inputs`) opens primary/secondaries/interferograms with `mmap_mode="r"`, then allocates `np.empty((1 + n_secondaries + n_interferograms, az, rg), dtype=primary.dtype)` (complex64) and copies all three artifacts in. There is no `InputConfig` reference anywhere in `Cropper` — it has no access to one (`__init__` takes only layout, split_regions, logger, secondary_labels). So the whole stack is materialised in RAM per split, unconditionally.
2. `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/dataset/pipeline.py:103-127` passes `arrays["inputs"]` straight into `PatchDataset`, once per split region (train, val and test are all alive simultaneously by the end of `DatasetPipeline.run`).
3. `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/dataset/datasets.py:128` -> `Patcher.extract` (spatial.py:228-237) does `np.ascontiguousarray(array[..., v0c:v1c, h0c:h1c])` over the *full* layer axis, so every `__getitem__` in every dataloader worker copies the disabled layers too. Only afterwards does `_build_input_tensor` (datasets.py:72-101) slice out the sections and skip the ones whose `use_*` flag is False.
4. Nothing on the training path consumes the disabled layers: `StatsComputer._collect` (stats_computer.py:66-92) explicitly `continue`s on `if not enabled`, and the only other reader of `PatchDataset.inputs` in the repo is `datasets.py:128` itself (grep for `.inputs` over pipelines/tools/webui/main returns exactly those two sites).

Magnitude, on the real dataset rather than test_data: `test_data/data/dataset.json` lists 29 passes (1 primary + 28 secondaries), and `InputTrialPlanner._overrides` (pipelines/backbone/training/experiments.py:586-591) sets `paths.secondary_labels` to all 28 candidates when `tracks: "all"`. Default crop is azimuth 1000-16000, range 500-4000 (configuration/sar/processing_config.py:139-142) with train = azimuth 1000-13000 (configuration/training/general/run.py:75), i.e. 12000 x 3500 = 42e6 complex64 pixels = 336 MB per layer. For `noamp-allsec-ifg` (`use_primary=False, use_secondaries=False`) the 1 primary + 28 secondary layers held but never read are ~9.7 GB on the train split alone, plus ~1.2 GB more across val/test; the per-patch memcpy is 57 layers (934 KB at 64x32) instead of the 28 useful ones (459 KB). Two corrections to the auditor's framing.

(a) Scope is wider than the input-trial variants. So every standard backbone run — not just `noamp-allsec-ifg` — materialises and per-patch-copies 4 unused secondary layers out of 9 (~1.3 GB on the train crop, ~44% of every patch memcpy). The all-track `noamp-*` trials are just the worst case (~10-12 GB, 29 of 57 layers).

(b) The fix is not simply "honour input_config inside _stack_inputs". title: Slot-organization scalars are split across two unrelated §3 metric tables
description: The three emergent slot-organization scalars produced by `Metrics._slot_organization_stats` land in the wrong §3 sections. `slot_mu_rank_diag` starts with `slot_` and literally contains the substring `_mu_`, so the 3.9b matcher claims it and it is filed under "Per-slot parameter statistics by activity". `slot_usage_entropy` and `slot_gt_alignment` match no rule and fall through to the catch-all "3.2 Curve-level (GT)" (a behaviour a test even pins: `test_report_metric_taxonomy_routes_keys` asserts `slot_usage_entropy` → 3.2). The result is that the three metrics that §2.7 presents as one coherent group are scattered over a parameter-statistics table and a curve-level table in the full metric dump.

suggested_fix: Add an explicit taxonomy entry for slot organization (e.g. matching `slot_usage_entropy`, `slot_mu_rank_diag`, `slot_gt_alignment` by exact key) ahead of the 3.9b rule, and update the taxonomy test.

Every other member of that table is a genuine per-slot/per-activity parameter statistic (`slot_0_mu_active_pred_mean`, `slot_0_amp_inactive_gt_std`, ...), so a K-independent global diagonality scalar sitting in that table is genuinely mis-filed.
- `slot_usage_entropy` and `slot_gt_alignment` match no rule and land on the final `lambda k: True` catch-all, "3.2 Curve-level (GT)" — a table of curve-space errors, which they are not.

It does not make the routing correct; it only means fixing it requires updating that line.

Not one of the listed known non-issues. No numeric or computational error: the values themselves are correct and are shown correctly in the §2 headline table, so the impact is confined to grouping in the §3 full-dump. Minor is the right severity.

title: Unreachable "skipped" branches for full_curves and track metadata

title: _equal_indices can emit duplicate slice indices and never centres a single slice
description: `np.linspace(n_total * 0.1, n_total * 0.9, n_slices).round().astype(int)` is not deduplicated, so whenever `n_slices > 0.8 * n_total` the same index appears twice (e.g. `n_total=10, n_slices=10` → `[1,2,3,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]`). Each duplicate makes `FigureComposer._slice_set` render and overwrite the identical `{axis}_{index}` figure set, and the duplicate paths are appended twice to `figure_paths`, so the report embeds the same image twice. Separately, with `n_slices=1` linspace returns the 10 % position rather than the centre of the axis, which is unlikely to be the intended single representative slice.
suggested_fix: Apply `np.unique(...)` to the rounded result, and special-case `n_slices == 1` to the midpoint.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. `_equal_indices` (pipelines/backbone/inference/pipeline.py:99-101) clamps `n_slices` to at most `n_total` but then spreads those samples over only the 10-90% span, so the spacing is 0.8*n_total/(n_slices-1); as soon as n_slices-1 > 0.8*n_total the rounded integers collide, and since the clamp permits n_slices == n_total, every n_total > 5 in that configuration produces duplicates. Downstream the duplication is real: FigureComposer._slice_set (figures.py:332-371) keys the output filename on the index alone, so the duplicate index re-renders and overwrites the same PNG and appends the same Path twice to figure_paths[group]; ReportAssets.images (tools/reporting/reporting.py:35-42) emits one markdown image line per list element with no dedup, so the report embeds the identical figure twice (and twice the base64 payload when embed_images is on). _slice_set runs three times per inference (denorm, unit-area, reduced), multiplying the waste. No KeyError arises because SSIM metrics are computed over all_*_idx = arange(n). Severity stays minor: with the shipped defaults (5 slices per axis, configuration/inference/general.py:58-60) against realistic cube sizes there are no duplicates; the failure needs a user to set the slice count near the axis length via webui/launch_layout.py:367,390 or ConfigCli — which the min(n_slices, n_total) clamp actively invites. Not covered by any test (tests/backbone_inference/test_figures.py:79-80 hardcodes distinct indices), and not one of the known non-issues.
correction: Two details in the claim are off. (1) The worked example is wrong: n_total=10, n_slices=10 gives linspace(1.0, 9.0, 10) = 1, 1.889, 2.778, 3.667, 4.556, 5.444, 6.333, 7.222, 8.111, 9, which rounds to [1,2,3,4,5,5,6,7,8,9] — a single collision at index 5, not the [1,2,3,3,...] the auditor quotes. The duplication itself is real; the illustrative array is not. (2) The second half of the claim — that n_slices=1 returns the 10% position instead of the centre — should be dropped: webui/config_descriptions.json:1689-1691 documents these fields as "equally spaced across the 10-90 percent span", so np.linspace(a, b, 1) returning the span start is consistent with the documented contract, a design choice rather than a defect. Also worth noting beyond the claim: even without collisions the 10-90% window means the outer 20% of each axis is never sliced, so a request for n_total slices can never cover the axis. Fix is to dedupe (np.unique on the rounded values, or an integer-stride construction) and to widen the span when n_slices approaches n_total.

title: Occlusion baseline is zero, not the channel mean the report claims
description: `ChannelOcclusion.deltas` zeroes the normalized channel, while the generated report states the channel is set to "its mean". After `Normalizer._apply_normalization` (`(x - loc) * inv_scale`, with log1p compression on the heavy-tailed channels) zero corresponds to the channel's robust *location* — the median in the compressed domain — not its mean. For the log1p amplitude channels the two differ materially, so the reported "prediction shift when the channel is replaced by its mean" is not what is measured, and the occlusion ranking is biased toward channels whose distribution is most skewed around the robust location.
suggested_fix: Either occlude with the batch-empirical channel mean (`occluded[:, c] = images[:, c].mean()`) to match the documented semantics, or reword the report paragraph to say the channel is set to the normalized zero (its robust location).
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. `ChannelOcclusion.deltas` (pipelines/backbone/inference/input_attribution.py:135) sets `occluded[:, c] = 0.0` on the tensor coming out of `run.loader`, which is normalized: pipelines/backbone/dataset/datasets.py:108-143 calls `Normalizer.normalize_input`, and `Normalizer._apply_normalization` (normalizer.py:73 torch / :94 numpy) computes `(x - loc) * inv_scale` after optional log1p compression. Therefore normalized 0 corresponds exactly to the per-channel `loc`, never to the channel mean in general. With the default `input_strategy = "per_slot"` (configuration/normalization/general.py:167, _SLOT_STRATEGIES at :123-135) the input slots map as: `pass/mag` and `ifg/mag` -> ROBUST_IQR_LOG1P, whose `fit` returns `np.percentile(log1p(x), 50)` i.e. the MEDIAN of the compressed values (general.py:56-60); `ifg/phase` -> FIXED_DIV_PI, whose `fit` returns `loc = 0.0` (general.py:30-31), so occlusion sets the channel to zero phase, a fixed physical value with no relation to the data distribution; `pass/raw_re_im`, `pass/norm_re_im`, `dem/elevation` -> ZSCORE, the only case where 0 really is the mean. A user-selectable MIN_MAX_P999 preset makes `loc` the 0.1st percentile, i.e. a near-minimum. Meanwhile the generated report asserts the mean baseline: `_write_report` line 226 writes "Occlusion, when computed, is the mean shift of the predicted profile when one normalized channel is zeroed (its mean)." That parenthetical is false for the standard configuration. Concrete failure: a run with the default per-slot normalization produces input_attribution.md telling the reader the occlusion column measures the prediction shift when a channel is replaced by its mean, while for the amplitude channels it is replaced by the log-domain median and for the interferogram phase channels by exactly zero phase. Not a KNOWN NON-ISSUE (no legacy shim, no dynamic dispatch, no config-contract question). The tests (tests/backbone_inference/test_input_attribution.py) only assert that zeroing an unused channel yields no shift, so they do not encode a mean-replacement intent; the code itself is a defensible zero-baseline occlusion, which is why this is documentation-level, not a computation bug.
correction: The defect is the report prose, not the occlusion code. The offending line is input_attribution.py:226 (the `_write_report` paragraph "... zeroed (its mean)"), not line 135; line 135 implements a legitimate zero-baseline occlusion and the figure title at line 216 already describes it correctly as "zeroed". Mechanism correction: normalized zero maps to the per-channel `loc`, which is the median of log1p values for ROBUST_IQR_LOG1P slots (pass/mag, ifg/mag), exactly 0 phase for the FIXED_DIV_PI ifg/phase slot, and the 0.1st percentile for MIN_MAX_P999 -- only ZSCORE slots make the "mean" wording true. The auditor's added claim that the ranking is "biased toward channels whose distribution is most skewed around the robust location" is speculative and not the load-bearing part; for log1p-compressed amplitude the mean/median gap is modest, and the larger mismatch is the fixed loc = 0 phase channels. Fix is a one-sentence edit: drop "(its mean)" and say the baseline is the normalized zero, i.e. each channel's robust location (median in the log1p domain for the amplitude channels, zero phase for the interferogram phase channels).

title: features_at does not check the stored tensor's batch dimension against the input batch
description: `FeatureSampler.features_at` unpacks `_B, C, h, w = maps.shape` and then discards `_B`, indexing `maps[b, :, fi, fj]` with `b` derived from the *input* batch size B. Any 4-D activation whose leading dimension is not the input batch (a folded window/patch batch of shape `(B*n_windows, C, h, w)`, or a layer that internally reshapes) is silently sampled at the wrong entries, producing features that do not correspond to the targets in `counts_all`/`mus_all`. The `_B` name signals the author knew the dimension existed but chose not to validate it. Same code path is shared by representation_cka.py:175.
evidence:
maps        = stored.numpy()
        _B, C, h, w = maps.shape
suggested_fix: Take B as a parameter and raise when `maps.shape[0] != B`, so a folded-batch layer is dropped like the non-4-D ones instead of producing silently misaligned features.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source and by running the real code.

Mechanism, traced: `LayerProbeCore.collect` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/layer_probes.py:129-143) derives `B, _, H, W = images.shape`, samples `b, i, j = sampler.sample_coords(B, H, W)` (so `b` in [0, B)), then hands every stored activation with `ndim == 4` to `FeatureSampler.features_at`, which unpacks `_B, C, h, w = maps.shape` (line 78), discards `_B`, and indexes `maps[b, :, fi, fj]` (line 83). The only guard is `tensor.ndim != 4`. Because activation folding can only multiply the batch (`B*nW >= B`), `maps[b]` is always a legal index, so a wrong leading dimension can never raise — it is always silent.

Such layers exist in this repo's backbone zoo. `models/backbone/swin_unet.py` `WindowAttention.forward` folds windows into the batch (`windows.view(-1, ws*ws, C)` at swin_unet.py:170), and the leaf module `attention.attention_dropout` (the dropout applied to the attention matrix inside `scaled_dot_product`) emits a 4-D tensor `(batch_windows, num_heads, seq, seq)`. Running every registered backbone with an ActivationRecorder store hook (B=2, input 4x64x32) I got, for swin_unet only: `encoder_stages.0.blocks.0.attention.attention_dropout -> (12, 2, 49, 49)` with B=2, i.e. dim0 = 6*B. Feeding that tensor straight through `FeatureSampler.features_at(t, b, i, j, 64, 32)` returned a `(64, 2)` float array with no error — features taken from windows 0-1 of an attention matrix, aligned against `counts_all`/`mus_all` targets for pixels of samples 0-1. Exactly the claimed silent mis-sampling.

Reachability: `_select_layers` linspace-subsamples leaves, so whether a folded layer lands in the selection depends on config. With `LayerProbeConfig.max_layers = 24` and standard patches it happened to miss; with `max_layers = 20` (a legal ConfigCli override) `encoder_stages.1.blocks.0.attention.attention_dropout (8, 5, 49, 49)` with B=4 is selected, and with `CkaConfig.max_layers = 16` on 128x64 patches `encoder_stages.2.blocks.5.attention.attention_dropout (8, 10, 49, 49)` with B=4 is selected in representation_cka.py:175. So the defect is real but conditional for the batch-dimension case.

Tests (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/backbone_inference/test_layer_probes.py) only exercise a two-Identity NCHW toy net; nothing encodes an intent that 4-D means NCHW-with-batch-first, and there is no coverage of folded or channels-last activations. Not any of the listed known non-issues.
correction: The claim's mechanism is correct but understates the defect. The missing validation is not only about the batch dimension: `features_at` assumes any 4-D activation is NCHW spatial, and the repo has a second, unconditional violation of that on the DEFAULT path. `ChannelLayerNorm`/`ConvNeXtBlock` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/models/blocks.py:242-280) run their `norm`, `fc1`, `activation`, `fc2` leaves on channels-LAST tensors, so for convnext_unet with default `max_layers = 24` the selected layer list I obtained contains e.g. `encoder_stages.0.blocks.0.fc1 -> (4, 64, 32, 192)`, `encoder_stages.3.blocks.0.activation -> (4, 8, 4, 1536)`, `decoder_stages.2.blocks.1.norm -> (4, 32, 16, 96)`. Here dim0 is correctly B, but C/h/w are read as (H, W, C): the report writes `n_channels = 64` for a 192-channel layer, and the "features" are spatial rows sampled at clipped, meaningless coordinates. No configuration override is needed — every convnext_unet layer-probe and CKA run already produces silently wrong R²/CKA numbers, which then drive the "K most decodable at '<layer>'" claim in layer_probes.md and the CKA heatmaps. Correct anchor for the fix is line 78 (`_B, C, h, w = maps.shape`), which should assert `_B == B` and reject/route non-NCHW 4-D activations rather than treating every rank-4 tensor as a feature map.

title: LayerProbeCore seed parameter is threaded but never set, and the config exposes no seed
description: `LayerProbeCore.__init__` accepts `seed: int = 0` and forwards it to `FeatureSampler`, but `LayerProbeRun.run` never passes it and `LayerProbeConfig` (configuration/diagnostics.py) has no seed field. `RidgeProbe` is likewise constructed with only two of its three arguments, so its train/test split seed is also pinned to 0. Every sibling analysis config exposes its randomness knob (`CkaConfig.sample_seed`, `LossLandscapeConfig.direction_seed`, `RobustnessConfig.seed`), making this an oversight rather than a deliberate choice: the probe R² cannot be checked for sampling sensitivity.
evidence: def __init__(self, model, layers: list[str], ppg: int, amp_thr: float, samples_per_batch: int, probe: RidgeProbe, seed: int = 0) -> None:
suggested_fix: Add `sample_seed: int = 0` to `LayerProbeConfig`, thread it into both `LayerProbeCore(..., seed=self.config.sample_seed)` and `RidgeProbe(..., seed=self.config.sample_seed)`, and claim the field in webui/launch_layout.py.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. pipelines/backbone/inference/layer_probes.py L94 declares `LayerProbeCore.__init__(..., seed: int = 0)` and forwards it to `FeatureSampler` (L100), but the only production caller, `LayerProbeRun.run` (L256-263), omits `seed=` and builds `RidgeProbe(self.config.ridge_lambda, self.config.test_fraction)` without its third `seed` argument, so both the pixel-sampling RNG (L68) and the probe train/test permutation (L37) are permanently seeded 0. configuration/diagnostics.py L278-293 confirms `LayerProbeConfig` has no seed field, while every sibling analysis config does and actually threads it: `CkaConfig.sample_seed` L311 -> representation_cka.py:151, `LossLandscapeConfig.direction_seed` L331 -> loss_landscape.py:166-167, `RobustnessConfig.seed` L351 -> robustness.py:134, and figures.py:93 passing `cfg.profile_seed` into `Metrics.select_pixels`. A repo-wide grep for LayerProbeCore/RidgeProbe/FeatureSampler across all file types hits only layer_probes.py, representation_cka.py (FeatureSampler only) and tests/backbone_inference/test_layer_probes.py, and the tests also never pass `seed`, so no caller sets it. The dynamic-dispatch registries are consistent with the gap rather than hiding it: webui/config_descriptions.json L2476 and webui/launch_layout.py L1379 ("probe_layers") both enumerate exactly the seedless field set, and main/analysis/probe_layers.py only wraps the dataclass in ConfigCli, which cannot introduce a field that does not exist. No KNOWN NON-ISSUE covers this. Severity minor is right: the pinned seed is deterministic, not incorrect; the cost is only that probe R2 cannot be re-run under a different pixel sample or split.
correction: Two details to sharpen. (1) Category: "dead-code" is imprecise — the `seed` parameter is live inside LayerProbeCore (it reaches FeatureSampler's RNG); what is actually missing is any caller able to set it, i.e. an unreachable config knob / config-coverage gap. (2) Mechanism completeness: the RidgeProbe omission is not merely "likewise" — it is the more consequential of the two, since it fixes the held-out split used for every reported R2 (layer_probes.py L37), and it also applies in the tests, which construct RidgeProbe with only ridge_lambda. The fix is one field, `seed: int = 0`, added to LayerProbeConfig (configuration/diagnostics.py L278-293) plus a claim in webui/config_descriptions.json and webui/launch_layout.py "probe_layers" (unclaimed fields fail tests), then threaded into both LayerProbeCore(seed=...) and RidgeProbe(..., seed=...) at layer_probes.py L256-263.

title: Track-dropout sweep repeats identical evaluations at full drop and reports a meaningless zero std
description: `drop_curve` runs `draws_per_count` random subsets for every `n_dropped`, but at `n_dropped == n_tracks` `rng.choice(n_tracks, size=n_tracks, replace=False)` is deterministic — the same all-tracks set every draw. The sweep therefore performs `draws_per_count` identical full passes over all batches (each pass being `n_dropped`-channel occlusion + forward + render) and records `mse_std = 0.0`, which the report presents in the "± across draws" column as if it were a measured spread. The same degeneracy applies at `n_dropped == n_tracks - 1` once `draws_per_count` exceeds the number of distinct subsets.
suggested_fix: Cap the draw count at `min(draws, comb(n_tracks, n_dropped))` and emit `mse_std = None` (rendered as "—") when only one distinct subset exists.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source. In `/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/robustness.py`, `RobustnessCore.drop_curve` loops `for n_dropped in range(n_tracks + 1)` and, for every n_dropped >= 1, runs `draws` independent `self.rng.choice(n_tracks, size=n_dropped, replace=False)` draws (line 61), each followed by a full `self._mse(batches, transform)` pass (line 69) i.e. clone + channel zeroing + forward + curve render over every cached batch.

At `n_dropped == n_tracks` the draw is degenerate: I verified with numpy in the project env that `default_rng(0).choice(4, size=4, replace=False)` returns a permutation of `[0,1,2,3]` on every call. Since line 62 flattens `chosen` into a channel index list and line 66 does `occluded[:, list(channels)] = 0.0`, permutation order is irrelevant — the occluded tensor, and hence the MSE, is bit-identical across all `draws`. So the last row costs `draws` identical evaluations and records `mse_std = float(np.std(values)) == 0.0` exactly, which line 162 prints under the "± across draws" header. `n_tracks` here is `run.n_secondaries` (TrackChannels.build, input_attribution.py:59), typically 4 for this dataset, with `draws_per_count` default 3 (configuration/diagnostics.py:349, webui slider up to 16).

Tests (tests/backbone_inference/test_robustness.py:48) exercise `drop_curve([[1],[2]], draws=2)` — the same degeneracy is present there (both draws at n_dropped=2 are identical) but nothing asserts on `mse_std`, so no intended behavior is encoded that contradicts the claim. This is not one of the listed known non-issues.
correction: Two framing corrections. (1) The "inefficiency" half is real but negligible in practice: this is a cold diagnostics path (RobustnessBatch runs once per run dir) with defaults max_batches=2, batch_size=4, so the waste is `draws-1` = 2 redundant forwards out of `n_tracks*draws + 1` = 13 total, on tiny batches. It is not on a training step, per-epoch loop, or request handler. The substantive defect is the reporting artifact, not compute. (2) The n_dropped == n_tracks-1 claim is weaker than stated: with draws > C(n_tracks, n_tracks-1) = n_tracks duplicates are guaranteed by pigeonhole, and duplicates can occur by chance even below that, but the draws are not deterministic there, so `mse_std` is generally nonzero — only the full-drop row is strictly degenerate. Also note the "± across draws" column already prints 0.0 for the dropped=0 row via `row.get("mse_std", 0.0)` (line 162), where a zero is legitimate; the misleading value is specifically the full-drop row, whose 0.0 is arithmetically true but reflects a single realizable subset rather than a measured spread. A minimal fix is to cap the draw count at `math.comb(n_tracks, n_dropped)` (or draw distinct subsets) and omit `mse_std` when only one distinct subset exists.

title: 2-D contour crashes when the sampled landscape is flat
description: `contour_2d` builds its levels with `np.logspace(log10(max(losses.min(), 1e-12)), log10(losses.max()), 20)`. When the landscape is flat over the sampled span (a degenerate model, a tiny `span`, or a loss that saturates), `losses.min() == losses.max()` and all 20 levels collapse to the same value; `contourf` then raises "Filled contours require at least 2 levels", killing the run after the full n_points_2d^2 grid of forward passes has already been paid for.
suggested_fix: Guard with an explicit check — if `losses.max() <= losses.min() * (1 + 1e-12)`, raise a clear ValueError naming the flat landscape (project style is to break loudly), or widen the range to `[min, min*1.01]` before building levels.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. `LossLandscapePlots.contour_2d` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/backbone/inference/loss_landscape.py:95) builds `levels = np.logspace(np.log10(max(losses.min(), 1e-12)), np.log10(losses.max()), 20)`. When the sampled grid is exactly flat, `losses.min() == losses.max()`, logspace returns 20 identical values, and `ax.contourf(..., levels=levels, ...)` raises. I confirmed with the project env (matplotlib 3.10.8 / numpy 2.4.3): a constant 11x11 loss grid raises `ValueError: Contour levels must be increasing` (both for a normal value 0.37 and for the 1e-12 clamp branch). Nothing catches it: `LossLandscapeRun.run` calls `contour_2d` at line 182 with no try, `PlotBase._save` has no guard, and `LossLandscapeBatch.run` (line 234) loops over runs without try/except, so one degenerate run aborts the whole batch, not just that run. The cost is already sunk: the n_points_2d^2 grid of forward passes runs at line 176 before plotting, and both 1-D cuts are plotted first (they survive flatness — `cut_1d` only sets a log yscale). Reachability: `span` is a user-settable float with no lower bound, exposed as a bare `"span"` field in webui/launch_layout.py:1345 (no min/max widget spec, unlike batch_size/max_batches/n_points_*) and overridable via ConfigCli in main/analysis/map_loss_landscape.py, so `span=0` (or a span so small that `origin + alpha*dir` rounds to the same float32 params) yields a bit-exactly constant grid. Tests (tests/backbone_inference/test_loss_landscape.py) only cover FilterNormalizedDirection and LandscapeEvaluator; contour_2d is untested, so no test encodes an intended behavior here. This is not one of the listed known non-issues (it is a plain unguarded plotting edge case, not a legacy-fallback or dispatch matter). Severity minor is right: the default config (span 0.5, a trained model) will not produce a bit-exactly flat grid, so this only bites degenerate/misconfigured invocations.
correction: Two details in the claim are off. (1) The exception text is wrong: on the repo's matplotlib 3.10.8 the failure is `ValueError: Contour levels must be increasing`, not "Filled contours require at least 2 levels" (that message belongs to older/different level-handling paths). (2) The trigger list should be tightened — float rounding means "a loss that saturates" rarely gives bit-exact equality across all n_points_2d^2 nodes; the concrete reachable triggers are `span=0` (unbounded in webui/launch_layout.py:1345 and via ConfigCli) or a span small enough that the float32 parameter update is a no-op. Worth adding that the same flat case also breaks the `LogNorm` vmin==vmax, and that the failure aborts the entire `LossLandscapeBatch` loop, not only the offending run. Fix: fall back to a linear/degenerate-safe level set (e.g. widen by a small factor or use `np.linspace` with a nudged max) when `losses.max() <= losses.min()`.

title: Fit-metric plots crash instead of skipping when a metric field has no finite values
description: Several plot helpers guard the all-NaN case in one statement and then immediately use an unguarded reduction on the same empty array. In `_plot_r2_distribution`, `pvals` is guarded with `if valid.size > 0` on line 31 but line 37/38 call `np.percentile(valid, 0.5)`/`(valid, 99.5)` unconditionally, which raises on an empty array. The same pattern appears in `plots/metrics.py:36` (`min(v for v in pvals if np.isfinite(v))` raises `ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence` when every R2 percentile is NaN) and in `_plot_snr_vs_r2`/`_plot_snr_vs_ambiguity` (plots/metrics.py:147, 186) which call `PlotBase._binned_median`, whose `x.min()` raises on an empty selection. The sibling `SpatialMapPlotter._plot_spatial_maps` (plots/spatial.py:67) shows the intended behaviour: warn and skip. A tomogram with NaNs (or an empty active mask) turns a plotting nicety into a hard failure of the whole `ParamRunInferencePipeline`.
evidence:
pvals = np.percentile(valid, qs) if valid.size > 0 else [float("nan")] * 5
...
        lo = float(np.percentile(valid, 0.5))
        hi = float(np.percentile(valid, 99.5))
suggested_fix: Return early with a `logger.warning` when `valid.size == 0` (and when the paired subsample is empty in the SNR plots), mirroring `_plot_spatial_maps`.
verdict_notes:
I reproduced the failures directly against the repo code with the project env (numpy 2.4.3, /home/bard/miniconda3/envs/Dune/bin/python), calling the helpers with degenerate inputs:

- `DistributionPlotter._plot_r2_distribution` with an all-NaN r2_map -> `IndexError: index -1 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0`. The guard on distributions.py:31 (`np.percentile(valid, qs) if valid.size > 0 else [nan]*5`) proves the author anticipated the empty case, yet lines 37-38 call `np.percentile(valid, 0.5/99.5)` unguarded. Confirmed as claimed.
- `MetricsBarPlotter._plot_global_metrics_summary` with all-NaN `r2_p*` -> `ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence` at metrics.py:36. Confirmed as claimed. Note this is the SAME trigger condition as the first: `FittingMetricsCalculator._compute_global_summary` (metrics.py:212-226) sets every `r2_p*`/`r2_mean` to NaN exactly when `r2_valid.size == 0`.
- `_plot_snr_vs_r2` / `_plot_snr_vs_ambiguity` with an all-NaN second map -> also crash (`ValueError: Invalid vmin or vmax`), but the failure happens EARLIER than the auditor states: `ax.hexbin` on the empty paired-subsample raises before `PlotBase._binned_median` (tools/reporting/plotting.py:229 `x.min()`) is ever reached. So the crash is real, the cited mechanism/line for those two is wrong.

No caller guards this: `ParamRunInferencePipeline._plots` -> `FittingResultPlotter.run` has no try/except, so the exception aborts the run (the metrics summary JSON is written first, at inference.py:80, so that artifact survives). Sibling helpers in the same package do warn-and-skip on the same class of degenerate input: spatial.py:67-69, distributions.py:144-146 ("no active components"), distributions.py:179-181 ("K-selection ambiguity plots skipped: no data"). The inconsistency is genuine, not a deliberate loud-failure design (the project's "no legacy fallback" rule is about schemas/old artifacts, not about plot helpers half-guarding the same array).

Reachability, traced from source: `R2.pixel_map` (tools/metrics/scoring.py:57-63) divides by `ss_tot + 1e-12` and `GaussianMixture.evaluate_slice` floors sigma and clips the exponent, so an all-non-finite r2_map needs NaN/inf in the loaded tomogram or in parameters.npy — plausible but not the common case. The auditor's "empty active mask" cause is wrong for the R2 path (zero active Gaussians gives pred=0 and a finite, negative R2). It IS correct for the ambiguity path: `KSelectionDiagnostics._compute_margin_maps` (metrics.py:77-78) NaNs `k_relative_margin_map` wherever `best_k_map == 0`, and `best_k_map` is initialised to zeros (sigma/extractor.py:474) and only filled for pixels that pass fitting, so a scene where nothing is fitted yields an all-NaN margin map with a finite snr map -> `_plot_snr_vs_ambiguity` crashes, while `_plot_k_ambiguity_distribution` on the same map correctly warns and skips.

Tests: tests/processing/test_param_extraction.py only smoke-tests the plotters on real data with active pixels (`test_fitting_result_plotter_smoke`, `test_param_run_inference_pipeline_smoke`); no degenerate-input test encodes crash-as-intended behaviour.
correction: Two details are off. (1) The exception types/locations: distributions.py:37 raises IndexError ("index -1 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0"), metrics.py:36 raises ValueError as claimed, but metrics.py:147/186 do NOT fail in `PlotBase._binned_median` — `ax.hexbin` on the empty paired subsample raises `ValueError: Invalid vmin or vmax` first (metrics.py:144 and 183), so `_binned_median`'s `x.min()` is a latent second failure, not the trigger. (2) The stated cause is only half right: an empty active mask does not make r2_map all-NaN (pred=0 still yields a finite R2), so it does not trigger the distributions.py:37 / metrics.py:36 crashes; those need NaN/inf in the tomogram or in parameters.npy. An empty active mask (best_k_map all zeros) instead NaNs `k_relative_margin_map` and takes down `_plot_snr_vs_ambiguity`. Severity "minor" is right: cold plotting path on degenerate data, and the metrics summary JSON is already written before plots run — but the exception does abort `ParamRunInferencePipeline` rather than skipping the figure.

title: Penalty legend claims an amplitude-weighted penalty that the selector does not implement
description: The penalised-score decomposition plot labels the red bars as `mean penalty $\lambda_K K \bar{A}_{\mathrm{norm}}$`, i.e. lambda times K times a mean normalised amplitude. The implemented penalty in `BestKSelector.select` is `penalised_all = mse_all + lambda_k * np.arange(1, k_max + 1)` — plain `lambda * K`, with no amplitude factor; `tests/processing/test_param_extraction.py::test_k1_penalty_equals_lambda` pins that behaviour. The published figure therefore documents a model-order criterion that the code does not use.
evidence: ax.bar(k_vals, pty_means, bottom=mse_means, color="#d62728", alpha=0.78, edgecolor="white", lw=0.5, label=r"mean penalty $\lambda_K K \bar{A}_{\mathrm{norm}}$")
suggested_fix: Change the legend to `$\lambda_K K$` (or implement the amplitude weighting in `BestKSelector.select` if that was the intent).
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source.

1. Implemented criterion — /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/processing/param_extraction/sigma/selection.py:41: `penalised_all = mse_all + lambda_k * np.arange(1, self.k_max + 1, dtype=np.float64)[None, :]`. The penalty is a pure `lambda_k * K` term, broadcast identically over every pixel. `scale_all` (the per-pixel profile maximum) is used only at line 52 to rescale output amplitudes (`amps_out = amps_norm * scale_all[:, None]`), after `best_K_idx` has already been chosen at line 42; it never enters the score.

2. What the plotted bars actually are — /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/processing/param_extraction/metrics.py:97,109: `penalty_k = pen_k - mse_k`, then `summary[f"k{k}_penalty_mean"] = float(pty_v.mean())`. Since `pen - mse == lambda_k*K` exactly, `k{k}_penalty_mean` is the constant `lambda_k*K`, with no amplitude weighting whatsoever. plots/metrics.py:105 reads exactly that key into `pty_means` and line 108 labels those bars `mean penalty $\lambda_K K \bar{A}_{\mathrm{norm}}$`.

3. Tests pin the plain form — tests/processing/test_param_extraction.py:345 `test_k1_penalty_equals_lambda` asserts `np.nanmax(pen[0]-mse[0]) == approx(LAMBDA_K)`; :356 `test_best_k_is_argmin_of_penalised`; webui test tests/webui/test_fit_lab.py:169 asserts `row["penalised"] == row["mse"] + lambda_k*row["k"]`, matching webui/fit_lab.py:292.

4. The project's own equation catalog agrees with the code, not the label — webui/equation_library.py:358 gives `pen_K = MSE_K + \lambda_K \cdot K` and the note explicitly says "the lambda_k*K penalty is applied per lambda value in BestKSelector.select".

5. A repo-wide grep for `\bar{A}` / `A_{\mathrm{norm}}` returns exactly one hit: this label. So it is an isolated stray factor, not a convention defined elsewhere.

Concrete failure: with k_max=5, lambda_k=1e-2, the red bar for K=3 has height exactly 0.03 regardless of any amplitude statistic, while the legend tells the reader it is 0.03 times a mean normalised amplitude. Any reader of the published figure `penalised_score_decomposition.png` who reconstructs the model-order criterion from the legend gets an amplitude-weighted MDL-style penalty that the pipeline does not implement, and would mis-predict K* for pixels whose normalised amplitude mean differs from 1.

Impact is limited to a figure legend (no numerical effect on extraction), so minor severity is right. Line 108 is the correct anchor.
correction: Mechanism is slightly broader than stated: the mislabelled bars come from `k{k}_penalty_mean` in pipelines/processing/param_extraction/metrics.py:97-109, computed as `penalised_per_k - mse_per_k`, which is the constant `lambda_k*K`. The repo's own equation catalog (webui/equation_library.py:358) and the webui fit-lab path (webui/fit_lab.py:292, pinned by tests/webui/test_fit_lab.py:169) both document/implement the plain `MSE_K + lambda_K*K` form, so the figure legend is the single outlier — the fix is to change the label to `$\lambda_K K$`.

title: param_extraction_meta.json omits fit-affecting knobs it is supposed to be the record of
description: `param_extraction_meta.json` is the strict provenance/reproducibility contract for a parameter run — `ParamRunInferencePipeline._metrics` reads `k_max`, `threshold_factor`, `truncation_index` and `activity_threshold` back out of it, and the project treats it as the authority for how a run was fitted. The payload records the fit flags, lambda, k_max and sigma_init_divisor but silently drops `prominence_frac` (which changes the peak initialisation and therefore the fitted parameters) and the whole Adam block (`adam_steps`, `adam_lr`, `adam_b1`, `adam_b2`), all of which are live config fields on `ExtractionConfig`/`ExtractParamsEntryConfig`. Two runs fitted with different `prominence_frac` or `adam_steps` produce identical metadata and identical auto-encoded output suffixes (`output_suffix_value` also ignores them), so they collide in the same directory name and are indistinguishable after the fact.
suggested_fix: Add `prominence_frac`, `adam_steps`, `adam_lr`, `adam_b1`, `adam_b2` (and ideally `range_batch_size`/`gpu_pixel_batch_size` for provenance) to the payload written by `save_run_metadata`.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source.

1. The payload (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/processing/param_extraction/io.py lines 41-61) writes every scalar of `FitConfig` except one: `threshold_factor`, `truncation_index`, `k_max`, `lambda_k`, `sigma_init_divisor`, `activity_threshold` and the three fit flags are all there; `prominence_frac` (configuration/param_extraction.py:16) is the only `FitConfig` field dropped. None of `ExtractionConfig.adam_steps / adam_lr / adam_b1 / adam_b2` (configuration/param_extraction.py:87-90) is recorded either.

2. Those knobs do change the fitted numbers. `prominence_frac` flows pipeline.py:100 -> extractor.py:309 -> `PeakInitialiser.run` -> `find_peaks(raw, prominence=pmax * prominence_frac, ...)` (sigma/initialiser.py:30), i.e. it decides which peaks seed amps/mus/sigmas. The Adam knobs flow pipeline.py:104-107 -> extractor.py:250-253 -> `SigmaScan.adam_scan`, which is a fixed-length `jax.lax.scan` over `n_steps` with no convergence criterion (sigma/kernels.py:86) — steps/lr/betas directly determine where the local optimisation stops.

3. The directory name does not disambiguate them: `output_suffix_value` = `k{k_max}_lam{lambda}_sig{sigma_init_divisor}_{free_params}` (configuration/param_extraction.py:102-111), asserted by tests/configuration/test_param.py:143-149. So two extractions on the same dataset with the same k/lambda/mode but e.g. `adam_steps=3000` vs `500`, or `fit_prominence_frac=0.05` vs `0.2`, both resolve to `<dataset>/params/params_k5_lam0.01_sig4_sigma`, the second overwrites parameters.npy/fit_diagnostics.npz, and the two `param_extraction_meta.json` files are identical apart from `timestamp`. Nothing else in the run directory records them: `config_state.json` is written by the dataset generation pipeline (pipelines/processing/generation/artifacts.py:101), not by extraction, and the only other trace is a free-text log line in the shared `params/logs` logger (sigma/extractor.py:99-100), which logs adam_steps/adam_lr but not prominence_frac and is not per-run.

4. The file is genuinely treated as the run's authority: `ParamRunInferencePipeline._metrics` reads `k_max`, `threshold_factor`, `truncation_index`, `activity_threshold` back out of it (pipelines/processing/param_extraction/inference.py:37-44), `ParamExtractionComparison` loads it per trial (pipelines/comparison/param_extraction_comparison.py:125), and `configuration/sar/gaussian_config.py:21-24` refuses to proceed without it ("the parameter run must be self-describing"). No test pins the payload's key set, so nothing encodes the omission as intended. This is a provenance gap, not a legacy-fallback or other listed non-issue.
correction: Two details in the claim need adjusting. (a) `adam_b1`/`adam_b2` are fields on `ExtractionConfig` only — `ExtractParamsEntryConfig` (configuration/param_extraction.py:154-179) exposes just `adam_steps` and `adam_lr`, and `ExtractionPlanResolver._build_plan` (queue.py:66-67) forwards only those two, so b1/b2 are always the defaults 0.95/0.999 from the entry path and cannot in practice diverge between runs. The knobs actually reachable-and-unrecorded are `fit_prominence_frac`, `adam_steps`, `adam_lr`. (b) The cited "line 41" is just the start of the payload dict; the defect is the payload's key set as a whole (io.py:41-61). Severity minor is right: no run produces wrong numbers, the loss is after-the-fact identifiability plus silent overwrite of a prior run's outputs in the colliding directory. Fix is to add `prominence_frac` and the Adam block to the payload (and, if collisions matter, fold non-default values into `output_suffix_value`).

title: `spurious_peaks_median` counts the dominant peak itself, inflating every value by one
description: `_chunk_maps` marks a height bin as a peak when it is a local maximum above `SPURIOUS_FRACTION * peak`, where `peak` is that pixel's global maximum amplitude returned by `ContrastEstimator.contrast_from_amplitude`. The dominant peak trivially satisfies `middle > 0.3 * peak`, so it is always counted. The metric is published as `spurious_peaks_median` and labelled "Spurious peaks per profile" / "Competing peaks vs window" with a lower-is-better orientation (WindowComparisonReport.ORIENTATION line 216, WindowComparisonPlots.PANELS line 167). A clean single-scatterer profile therefore scores 1 spurious peak, not 0. The bias is a constant +1 so the window ranking survives, but the absolute numbers in the report table and the bar plot are wrong.
suggested_fix: Exclude the argmax bin from the count (subtract 1, or mask `amp.argmax(axis=0)`), or rename the metric to `peaks_per_profile` and update the report wording accordingly.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source. In /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/comparison/preprocessing_comparison.py, `WindowMetrics._chunk_maps` (line 111-115) gets `peak` from `ContrastEstimator.contrast_from_amplitude` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/processing/param_extraction/metrics.py line 26: `peak = amp.max(axis=0)`), i.e. the per-pixel global maximum over the height axis. Line 113 then counts every interior bin that is a strict local max (`middle > amp[:-2] & middle >= amp[2:]`) and exceeds `0.3 * peak`. The dominant bin satisfies `peak > 0.3 * peak` for any peak > 0 and is a local max, so it is always included; there is no exclusion of the global maximum and no `-1` anywhere downstream (`is_peak.sum(axis=0)` goes straight into `spurious_map`, then `np.median(spurious_map[valid])` at line 125).

Numeric check (Dune env, numpy): a clean single-Gaussian profile (H=32, peak at bin 16) yields count 1; the same profile plus one competing scatterer at 0.5 amplitude yields 2. So the published `spurious_peaks_median` is the total number of significant peaks, not the number of competing/spurious ones.

The value is surfaced as "Spurious peaks per profile" / "Competing peaks vs window" in WindowComparisonPlots.PANELS (line 167), as column "Spurious" with lower-is-better orientation in WindowComparisonReport.METRIC_COLUMNS/ORIENTATION (lines 207, 215), and the narrative paragraph at line 237 talks about "spurious competing peaks per profile". Only consumer is main/analysis/compare_preprocessing_trials.py; no test encodes the counting semantics (tests/entrypoints/test_main_entrypoints.py only checks the entry point wiring), so nothing contradicts the claim. It is not one of the listed known non-issues.

Impact is exactly as the auditor scoped it: descriptive report/plot numbers are inflated, window ranking is preserved because the offset is +1 for essentially every valid pixel. Minor.
correction: Two details to tighten. (1) The offset is +1 for virtually all valid pixels but not literally constant: a pixel whose global maximum sits at height bin 0 or H-1 is excluded from `middle = amp[1:-1]` and so gets no self-count (such a profile can even report 0 while containing a peak). Since the metric is a median over pixels, the practical effect is still a uniform +1 shift, and the ranking across windows is unaffected. (2) The bias is on top of `_summarise` line 125 (`spurious_peaks_median`), not only line 113; the minimal fix is to subtract the self-count (e.g. count peaks and subtract 1 where the argmax falls in the interior, or exclude the argmax bin) — or, alternatively, relabel the metric as "significant peaks per profile", which would leave the numbers correct and only change the wording at lines 167, 207 and 237.

title: Size-match reference skip never fires for non-`conv` heads, so the reference is width-bisected against itself
description: `SizeMatchStage.run` skips the reference with `if model_name == reference`. `self.models` holds keys from `ModelBuilder.model_key(name, head)`, which returns the bare name only for head `conv` and `f"{name}-{head}"` otherwise (pipelines/shared/model/model_builder.py:13-14). With the default `size_match.reference_model = 'unet'` and `heads = ['mlp']`, models are `['unet-mlp', ...]` and the guard never triggers: `unet-mlp` is bisected against a target computed for `unet` with head `conv` (`SizeMatcher.reference_count` uses `split_key('unet')`, sizing.py:176-182). The records dict then gains a phantom `'unet'` entry (scale 1.0, empty overrides) that no worker reads — `BenchmarkWorker._size_overrides` looks up the full model key — and the reference backbone is trained with rounded bisected widths instead of its declared defaults, since `_round` only has to land inside the 5 % tolerance. The phantom row is also rendered into size_match_report.md.
suggested_fix: Normalise the reference to the same model-key form as `self.models` per swept head before comparing (or compare on `ModelBuilder.split_key(...)[0]`), and store the reference record under the key the workers actually look up.
verdict_notes:
Mechanism reproduced from source, though the auditor's trigger example is wrong.

What holds:
- /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/benchmark/stages.py:266 is `if model_name == reference: continue`, and `reference` is the raw string `config.size_match.reference_model` (default `"unet"`, configuration/benchmark/general.py:27).
- `self.models` comes from BenchmarkPipeline._model_keys (pipelines/benchmark/pipeline.py:29) = `ModelBuilder.model_key(name, head)`, which is the bare name only for head `conv` and `f"{name}-{head}"` otherwise (pipelines/shared/model/model_builder.py:13-14).
- `SizeMatcher.reference_count` (sizing.py:176-182) splits the reference with `ModelBuilder.split_key`, so `"unet"` is counted with head `conv` and at DEFAULT widths (it calls `_count`, not `_count_at`).
- So whenever `heads` contains anything other than `conv`, no model key equals the reference, the guard never fires, and the reference backbone is bisected against a target computed for a different head.

What the auditor got wrong: `heads` defaults to `["conv"]` (configuration/benchmark/general.py:102), not `["mlp"]`, so the DEFAULT benchmark configuration is unaffected — the guard works. And `mlp` is not a valid head at all: BACKBONE_HEADS = ("conv", "multihead", "per_gaussian", "set_pred") (models/backbone/__init__.py:70), and pipeline._validate_sweep would `SystemExit` on `heads=['mlp']` before the stage ever runs. The real trigger is any non-conv head, e.g. `heads=["set_pred"]`, which is the project's standard head, and `heads` is a first-class multi-select in the webui launch form (webui/launch_layout.py:879).

Concrete reproduction (ran the real WidthScaler/get_backbone in the Dune env, in_channels=9, out_channels=15 for K=5):
- unet+conv = 31,041,999 params; unet+set_pred = 31,054,169 (a 0.04% difference).
- With reference `unet` and models `['unet-set_pred', ...]`, the target is 31,041,999 and `matcher.match('unet-set_pred', target)` bisects: scales 0.6325, 2.2494, 1.1927, 0.8685, then 1.0178 → 32,107,241 params, deviation +3.43%, inside the 5% tolerance so it stops there. Overrides written: `{'features': [64, 128, 264, 520]}` instead of the declared defaults `[64, 128, 256, 512]`.
- BenchmarkWorker._run_backbone (pipelines/benchmark/workers.py:145) applies those overrides for key `unet-set_pred`, so the reference backbone trains at +3.4% capacity with rounded bisected widths.
- `records` also gains a phantom `'unet'` entry (scale 1.0, empty overrides, deviation 0.0) that no worker ever reads (`_size_overrides` looks up the full key, workers.py:31-41) and that `_load_cached` ignores (it only checks `all(m in records for m in self.models)`), yet `_write_report` iterates `sorted(records.keys())` so the phantom row is rendered into size_match_report.md, and the header line claims "Reference model `unet` at 31,041,999 parameters" for a model absent from the sweep.
- Same leak downstream: ComparisonStage is handed `config.size_match.reference_model` (pipeline.py:75) and comparison_report.py:193 prints "Reference model: `unet`" while every collected trial is `unet-set_pred`.

Severity stays minor: every model in the sweep, reference included, is still matched to one common target inside the 5% tolerance, so the capacity-fairness invariant is not broken. The damage is a reference that silently drifts off its declared defaults plus phantom/incorrect rows in two reports. No test covers the non-conv-head path — tests/benchmark/test_stages.py only exercises bare names (`["unet"]`, `["unet", "resunet"]`), which is exactly why this went unnoticed.
correction: Trigger condition is wrong in the claim. `heads` defaults to `["conv"]`, and `"mlp"` is not a valid head (BACKBONE_HEADS = conv/multihead/per_gaussian/set_pred), so `heads=['mlp']` would SystemExit in BenchmarkPipeline._validate_sweep, never reaching stages.py:266. The bug fires for any non-conv head — in practice `heads=["set_pred"]`, the project standard. Measured effect with that config: target 31,041,999 (unet+conv defaults), `unet-set_pred` converges at scale 1.0178 → features [64,128,264,520] (+3.43%) instead of its declared [64,128,256,512]. Also add two consequences the claim missed: `SizeMatcher.reference_count` counts the reference at default widths via `_count`, so the anchor is a model that is never trained; and ComparisonStage/ComparisonReport inherit the same bare `reference_model` string, printing "Reference model: `unet`" in the benchmark comparison report even though every trial is `unet-set_pred`. Severity minor is correct — all models including the reference still land within the 5% tolerance of a single common target, so the capacity comparison itself remains valid. A fix is to compare `ModelBuilder.split_key(model_name)[0] == ModelBuilder.split_key(reference)[0]` only when heads match, or better, to validate at _validate_sweep time that `reference_model` is one of `self.models` and require it to carry the head.

title: VRAM probe writes its work directory outside the benchmark run, keyed only by model name
description: `MaxBatchProbe.work_dir` is `log_base_dir / 'max_batch_probe' / model_name`, independent of the benchmark run_tag, while everything else in the stage lives under `run_dir` (`MaxBatchStage.stage_dir = run_dir / 'max_batch'`, stages.py:74). The probe passes this directory to `ConfigFactory.training_trainer_config(logdir=...)`, `DatasetPipeline(training_run_directory=...)` and `Trainer(run_dir=...)`, so dataset metadata, normalization stats and trainer logs are all written there. Two benchmark runs with different run tags probing the same backbone — normal given the project runs concurrent experiments — write to the same directory and interleave logs and dataset metadata, and the artifacts survive outside the run with no association to the run that produced them.
suggested_fix: Root the probe work directory in the run: `Path(config.paths.log_base_dir) / run_tag / "max_batch" / model_name / "probe"`, passing the run tag (or the stage's run_dir) into MaxBatchProbe.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. pipelines/benchmark/batch_probe.py:39 sets work_dir = log_base_dir/"max_batch_probe"/model_name with no run_tag, while pipelines/benchmark/stages.py:74 keeps every other stage artifact under run_dir = log_base_dir/run_tag (tools/orchestration/stages.py:21), and pipelines/benchmark/workers.py:110-116 already has self.run_dir and writes max_batch_result.json under it. The probe writes into work_dir: Logger(log_dir=work_dir/"logs", name="max_batch") which opens <log_dir>/max_batch.log with mode "w" (tools/monitoring/logger.py:164, truncating), and DatasetPipeline(training_run_directory=work_dir) which saves normalization stats to work_dir/"meta" (pipelines/backbone/dataset/pipeline.py:159) plus dataset-config, crop and patch metadata (lines 181-192). Concrete failure: two benchmark runs with different run tags (same default log_base_dir) probing the same model name share that directory; the later run truncates the earlier probe log, concurrent runs interleave into a truncated file, and the meta/ files are replaced by whichever wrote last, with no association to any run. Nothing in the repo reads max_batch_probe/ (single grep hit repo-wide), so no cross-run stale reuse. Not one of the listed known non-issues; no test pins the location (tests/benchmark/test_batch_probe.py builds work_dir by hand), and the 2026-07-03 benchmark audit note already listed this same item as an unfixed minor note.
correction: The mechanism is narrower than described: no trainer logs, TensorBoard events or checkpoints are written there. IOConfig.writer is None (configuration/training/general/runtime.py:9), emit_docs=False, and trainer.train() is never called (only TrainStepMemoryProbe forward/backward steps), so Trainer(run_dir=work_dir) writes nothing to disk during the probe. The real collateral is the probe log file (opened with mode="w", so a second run truncates the first's log and concurrent runs interleave) and the dataset meta/ files (normalization stats, dataset config, crop and patch metadata) being overwritten. Because DatasetPipeline always recomputes and nothing reads that directory back, the measured batch size and downstream training are unaffected — the damage is limited to orphaned, run-unattributable and mutually clobbering artifacts. Severity minor is correct; the cited line 39 is correct for the current file.

title: `_worker_counts()` re-evaluated per batch size and `_main_specs()`/`SweepReport` built twice
description: `_main_specs` calls `self._worker_counts()` inside the inner comprehension, so it runs once per batch size (5 times with the default `batch_sizes`) and each call re-emits `self.logger.subsection(f"Skipping worker counts above {cores} cores: ...")`, duplicating that warning in the log. `run()` then calls `_main_specs()` again only to report `n_specs` in the meta event (line 158), doubling it again. Separately `SweepReport(main_results, ...)` is constructed at line 164 and rebuilt from the same records inside `_write` (line 121), re-deriving the dataframe and recommendation. Cheap relative to the sweep, but the duplicated warning is actively misleading when reading the tuning log.
evidence:
for batch_size in self.config.batch_sizes
            for workers in self._worker_counts()
suggested_fix: Hoist `workers = self._worker_counts()` above the comprehension, memoise `_main_specs()` (or pass the list into `run`), and pass the already-built SweepReport into `_write`.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source.
