This is not a dynamic-dispatch false positive: ProjectPaths is a concrete object accessed by attribute, not by string key, and it appears in no script_catalog/launch_layout/config_descriptions/repomap registry. It also matches no KNOWN NON-ISSUE. Severity minor is right — it is inert wiring, not a defect, and the fix is a signature cleanup with no behavioural change.
correction: Two details are off. (1) Wrong file for the wiring: the five objects are NOT constructed in request_router.py. They are built in webui/web_ui_server.py lines 98-106 (`CubeExplorer(self.paths, self.logger)`, `FitLab(...)`, `ModelProbe(...)`, `TriageBoard(...)`, `AbAutopsy(...)`) and then handed to RequestRouter as already-constructed objects. RequestRouter's own `self.paths` (request_router.py:57) is genuinely used — request_router.py:482, 495, 563, 574, 839-856, 962-963 — so describing it as "threaded through the router wiring in request_router.py" mislabels a live dependency as part of the dead one. (2) Slight imprecision on TriageBoard: the claim says it "actually consumes the argument", which is true, but the dead thing there is specifically the redundant `self.paths` attribute at triage_board.py:58; the parameter itself must stay because line 60 needs `paths.logs_dir`. Fix scope: drop the parameter and attribute entirely from FitLab, AbAutopsy, ModelProbe and CubeExplorer (updating the four call sites in web_ui_server.py:98-106 and the tests that pass ProjectPaths() in test_fit_lab.py and test_model_probe.py); in TriageBoard drop only line 58 and keep the parameter.

title: Unused json import in results_browser
description: `import json` at the top of results_browser.py is never used; the only occurrences of the string 'json' elsewhere in the file are the `.json` suffix literals in `CONFIG_SUFFIXES` and `STAGE_MARKERS`. Config files are returned as raw text via `_read_text`, never parsed.
suggested_fix: Remove the import.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/results_browser.py line 3 is `import json`, and an AST walk of the module finds no Name node with id 'json' and no Attribute access on a name 'json' — so there is genuinely no use, not merely no grep hit. The only textual 'json' occurrences are the '.json' suffix literal in CONFIG_SUFFIXES (line 15) and the marker paths 'pipeline/resolved_config.json' / 'docs/trainer_config.json' in STAGE_MARKERS (lines 26, 29), both used only for suffix-set membership and Path.exists() checks, never parsed. Config files are shipped to the frontend as raw decoded text by _read_text (call site line 80, definition line 243), which read_bytes + decode + truncates; no deserialization anywhere. Checked the dynamic-dispatch escape hatch the protocol requires: repo-wide the module is referenced only by tests/webui/test_results_browser_logs.py:12, webui/request_router.py:35, and webui/web_ui_server.py:32, and all three import only ResultsBrowser. No test monkeypatches a `json` attribute on the module, no `results_browser.json` attribute access exists, and there is no style/lint/import test in tests/ that would intentionally retain the import. This is not one of the listed known non-issues (it is not a late import in main/, not a registry-driven symbol, not a config-descriptions claim). Claim details (file, line, mechanism, severity) are all accurate; no correction needed.

title: Gaussian-count truncation in _match_params is unreachable for the default matching strategy
description: `_match_params` supports a prediction/GT Gaussian-count mismatch by truncating both sides to `min(num_gaussians, gt_gaussians)` after matching. But the truncation is applied *after* `ParamMatcher.match`, and the hungarian path raises `ParamMatcher.match requires equal pred/gt gaussian counts` (tools/loss/param_loss.py:30-31) before it can run. Since `param_matching` defaults to HUNGARIAN (`AblationCatalog.PARAM_MATCH_FULL`), the mismatch handling only ever executes under `sorted_gt`, where it silently drops the extra slots instead of failing loudly. The code reads as if mismatched counts are a supported configuration when they are half-supported.
suggested_fix: Either validate the counts up front and fail loudly for both strategies (consistent with the no-legacy-fallbacks policy), or move the truncation before ParamMatcher.match so both strategies behave the same.
verdict_notes: Verified in source: pipelines/backbone/training/loss.py:158-165 truncates to min(num_gaussians, gt_gaussians) AFTER ParamMatcher.match, and tools/loss/param_loss.py:30-31 raises on unequal counts in the hungarian path (the default, PARAM_MATCH_FULL). So the truncation is unreachable under the default and, under sorted_gt, silently drops the extra Gaussian slots from the loss instead of failing. That is exactly the kind of silent tolerance the project's no-legacy-fallback / break-loudly policy forbids, and the code misleadingly reads as if mismatched counts are a supported configuration. Fix is small and clarifying: assert equality (or fail loudly) and delete the dead truncation.

title: Active-Gaussian threshold uses > in metrics.py but >= in the matching/organization helpers
description: `Metrics._active_count_stats` (lines 291-293), `_param_population_stats` (line 335), `_matched_gaussian_metrics` (lines 366-367) and `Predictor._finalize_results` (predictor.py:314) all test `amp > ParamMatcher.ACTIVE_AMP_THR`, while `GaussianMatcher` (gaussian_matching.py:30-31, 58) and every `SlotOrganization` helper (slot_organization.py:13, 32, 56-57) test `amp >= amp_threshold`. The two conventions are mixed inside a single metric — e.g. `_matched_gaussian_metrics` builds `act_pred`/`act_gt` with `>` but consumes an assignment computed with `>=` — so a slot whose amplitude lands exactly on 1e-3 is simultaneously active and inactive depending on which line reads it.
suggested_fix: Route every activity test through a single helper (e.g. `ParamMatcher.is_active(amp)`) so the comparison operator is defined in one place.
verdict_notes: Confirmed by reading the code: tools/metrics/gaussian_matching.py (lines 29-31, 57) and tools/metrics/slot_organization.py (13, 32, 56-57) compare amplitude with >= against ParamMatcher.ACTIVE_AMP_THR, while every other consumer of that same named constant uses strict > (metrics.py 291-293/335/366-367, predictor.py 237/314, failure_modes.py 41-42, stratified.py 24, normalization_audit.py 70, plots/*, webui/model_probe.py 160), and webui/equation_library.py:1487 documents the constant as 'strict >'. Metrics._matched_gaussian_metrics genuinely mixes the two inside one metric: act_pred/act_gt use > while the assignment they index was computed with >=. Numerical impact is tiny (exact-equality boundary), so this is minor rather than a bug, but a single shared threshold constant having two competing comparison conventions across modules is a real consistency defect a reviewer would flag, and the fix is a trivial, clearly-improving normalization to one operator.

title: Seed report reimplements Report's metric grouping through four private members
description: `SeedComparisonReport._report_keys` and `_grouped_keys` reach into `Report._is_per_slice_ssim`, `Report._METRIC_SKIP_KEYS`, `Report._METRIC_TAXONOMY` and `Report._section_order` to reproduce the filtering-and-grouping loop that already exists verbatim inside `Report._build_full_metrics` (report.py:631-644). Any change to the taxonomy or skip rules has to be mirrored by hand in two places, and the seed report is coupled to a 900-line module's private surface just to bucket metric keys.
evidence: return [key for key in means if not Report._is_per_slice_ssim(key) and "_raw" not in key and key not in Report._METRIC_SKIP_KEYS]
suggested_fix: Extract the filter + taxonomy grouping into a small public helper (e.g. `MetricTaxonomy.group(keys)` in tools/reporting) and call it from both `Report._build_full_metrics` and `SeedComparisonReport`.
verdict_notes: Confirmed real duplication: SeedComparisonReport._report_keys/_grouped_keys (seed_comparison.py:108-118) reproduce the identical filter-and-bucket loop from Report._build_full_metrics (report.py:627-644) while reaching into four private members of Report (_is_per_slice_ssim, _METRIC_SKIP_KEYS, _METRIC_TAXONOMY, _section_order). Any taxonomy or skip-rule change must be mirrored by hand in two modules, and there is no test-enforced link between them. The fix -- lift the grouping into one shared classmethod on Report -- is small and clearly better.

title: TrialCollector subclass replaces the base constructor, leaving most inherited helpers unusable
description: `TrialCollector.__init__` establishes `run_dir`, `training_dir` and `pipeline_dir`, on which `_aggregate_sources`, `_run_dirs`, `_seed_dirs`, `_parse_parameters` and `collect` all depend. The subclass `pipelines/comparison/trial_collector.py:28` overrides `__init__` without calling super and sets a completely different attribute set (`runs_dir`, `run_tags`, `seed_dispersion`), then overrides `collect` too — it inherits only `_read_checkpoint` and `_attach_inference`. Any future call into a base method on that subclass fails with `AttributeError` rather than anything meaningful, and the two `collect` implementations have already diverged (the subclass builds no `size_match`, `trainer_config`, `run_summary`, `parameters` or `training_result`). The shared piece here is two small helpers, not a class hierarchy. Related: `collect()` calls `_aggregate_sources()` (which loads `pipeline/training_results.json` unguarded) before the `training_dir.is_dir()` guard, so the friendly "no training directory" path is only reachable when the pipeline directory happens to exist.
suggested_fix: Extract `_read_checkpoint`/`_attach_inference` into a small mixin (or module-level functions) that both collectors use, and let the comparison collector stand on its own instead of subclassing a class whose invariants it does not satisfy.
verdict_notes: Verified against source. pipelines/comparison/trial_collector.py:28 TrialCollector.__init__ does not call super() and sets a disjoint attribute set (runs_dir/run_tags/seed_dispersion), so the inherited run_dir/training_dir/pipeline_dir never exist on the subclass. Every base method except _read_checkpoint, _attach_inference and the _attach_figures hook (_aggregate_sources, _run_dirs, _seed_dirs, _parse_parameters, _optional_json, base collect) would AttributeError if ever called on it — a real latent trap, not taste. The subclass does use the template-method hook _attach_figures legitimately, so the hierarchy is not entirely gratuitous, but the broken constructor contract is a genuine, easily-fixed fragility. The secondary claim also checks out: trial_collection.py:194 calls _aggregate_sources() (which does an unguarded FileIO.load_json of pipeline/training_results.json) before the training_dir.is_dir() guard at line 196, so the friendly 'No training directory found' error path is only reachable when the pipeline directory already exists — otherwise it raises instead. Material enough to raise in review.

title: UnrolledTrainer re-implements the shared BaseTrainer loop instead of subclassing it
description:
`UnrolledTrainer` is a standalone 220-line training loop that duplicates almost everything `tools/training/trainer.py::BaseTrainer` already provides: optimizer construction, batch-size LR scaling, `Warmup`/`Scheduler` wiring, `WeightEma`, `VramReservation`, checkpointing, early stopping and completion marking. Every other model family (backbone, dual, image AE, profile AE, JEPA) goes through `BaseTrainer`.

The fork has already drifted: the unrolled loop has no `use_amp`/autocast, no `gradient_accumulation_steps`, no `abort_on_nonfinite_loss` guard, no `Tracker`/resource monitoring, no `TrainerState` resume, no `snapshot_every_n_epochs`, no `GradientClipper` telemetry and no cache clearing — all of which are config-driven elsewhere. It also returns a dict instead of `BaseTrainer`'s `(train_losses, val_losses, best_val_loss)`, which is why `OverfitGateTrainer` (pipelines/unrolled/training/pipeline.py:27-35) exists purely as a shape adapter for the shared `OverfitCheck`.
suggested_fix: Port `UnrolledTrainer` onto `BaseTrainer` (implementing `_build_param_groups`, `_build_criterion`, `_compute_loss`) and give `UnrolledEntryConfig` a trainer-config view, which also removes the `OverfitGateTrainer` shim.
verdict_notes: Confirmed by reading both files. pipelines/unrolled/training/trainer.py is a 220-line standalone loop that re-implements optimizer construction, batch-size LR scaling, Warmup/Scheduler wiring, WeightEma, VramReservation, checkpointing, early stopping and CompletionMarker stamping, all already provided by tools/training/trainer.py::BaseTrainer (499 lines), which every other family uses. The drift is real and verifiable: UnrolledTrainer hardcodes self.use_amp = False and never autocasts, has no gradient_accumulation_steps, no torch.isfinite/abort_on_nonfinite_loss guard, no Tracker/ResourceMonitor, no TrainerState resume, no _maybe_snapshot, no GradientClipper (raw clip_grad_norm_ instead), no cache clearing and no validation_frequency. It builds throwaway WarmupConfig/SchedulerConfig objects (lines 53-56) just to satisfy the shared Warmup/Scheduler, and returns a dict instead of BaseTrainer's (train_losses, val_losses, best_val_loss), which is why the OverfitGateTrainer shape adapter exists at pipelines/unrolled/training/pipeline.py:27-35. This is a fork of the project's core training runtime that silently drops config-driven safety and telemetry; the missing-TensorBoard quirk covers only one facet. Note the fix also spans configuration/training/unrolled.py, since UnrolledEntryConfig lacks the optimizer/memory/resources/early_stopping sub-configs BaseTrainer reads.

title: Autoencoder/unrolled loaders inherit RunLoader but break its contract
description:
`ImageAeRunLoader._build_model(self, device)` and `UnrolledRunLoader` (which defines `_build_unrolled_model` and never implements `_build_model` at all) subclass `RunLoader`, whose abstract-by-convention hook is `_build_model(self, backbone_name, in_channels, out_channels, patch_size)` and whose `load(*, split, batch_size, num_workers, device, checkpoint_name)` is the entry point. Both subclasses replace `load` with an incompatible keyword-only signature (`load(*, config, device)`), so the inherited `load` is unreachable and would crash if ever called — which is exactly what `InferenceComponentsResolver` would do if either run type were routed through it.

Meanwhile `ProfileAeRunLoader` (pipelines/profile_autoencoder/inference/loader.py:40) solves the same problem by not inheriting at all and copy-pasting `_read_run_summary` / `_load_checkpoint`. Three loaders, three different relationships to the same base class, and the inheritance that does exist is only used to borrow `_read_json`, `_build_dataset_config` and `_load_checkpoint`.
suggested_fix: Extract the genuinely shared helpers (`_read_json`, `_build_dataset_config`, `_load_checkpoint`) into a small `RunArtifactReader` mixin that all four loaders use, and stop subclassing `RunLoader` where the `load` contract is not honoured.
verdict_notes: Verified. ImageAeRunLoader (pipelines/image_autoencoder/inference/loader.py:35) and UnrolledRunLoader (pipelines/unrolled/inference/loader.py:46) both subclass RunLoader (pipelines/backbone/inference/loader.py:52), which is not a mixin but a fully concrete backbone loader: its load(*, split, batch_size, num_workers, device, checkpoint_name) returns a backbone Run and its _build_model(backbone_name, in_channels, out_channels, patch_size) calls get_backbone. Both subclasses replace load with an incompatible load(*, config, device), so the inherited entry point is unreachable; ImageAeRunLoader overrides _build_model(self, device) with a different arity, and UnrolledRunLoader inherits the backbone _build_model unchanged while defining _build_unrolled_model beside it, an inherited method that would build the wrong model if ever called. ProfileAeRunLoader (pipelines/profile_autoencoder/inference/loader.py:40) does not inherit at all and re-implements _read_run_summary and a near-identical _load_checkpoint, exactly the cross-module copy the project's own rules forbid. Three loaders, three different relationships to one base, where the only thing actually borrowed is _read_json/_build_dataset_config/_load_checkpoint. The fix is concrete: extract those helpers into a small shared base and let each family compose instead of claiming to be a backbone loader. Minor severity but a real design defect, not taste.

title: LinkNet's `current_skip` and its conditional are redundant
description: After the encoder loop `x` already equals `encoder_outputs[-1]`, so at `stage_index == 0` `current_skip` is the same tensor as `x`, and for every later stage `current_skip` is computed and then discarded. The whole line and the ternary reduce to `decoded = decoder_stage(x)`. As written the code reads as if a skip connection feeds each decoder stage's input, which it does not — the skips only enter through the `decoded + target_skip` addition below.
evidence:
current_skip  = encoder_outputs[-(stage_index + 1)]
            decoder_input = current_skip if stage_index == 0 else x
suggested_fix: Replace both lines with `decoded = decoder_stage(x)` and keep only the `target_skip` addition.
verdict_notes: Verified against models/backbone/link_net.py:184-199. After the encoder loop `x` is exactly `encoder_outputs[-1]`, so at stage_index==0 `current_skip` is the same tensor as `x`, and for every later stage `current_skip` is computed and thrown away. The two lines collapse to `decoded = decoder_stage(x)`. This is not just redundancy: in a backbone forward the ternary implies each decoder stage is fed a skip tensor, which is false (skips only enter via the `decoded + target_skip` addition), so it actively misreads the architecture's wiring. Small, exact, behavior-preserving fix in a comprehension-critical spot.

title: The conv+norm+activation unit is re-implemented in four backbone modules instead of living in blocks.py
description: `ConvNormAct` (deeplab_v3_plus.py:12) and `RSUConv` (models/backbone/u2net_lite.py:11) are the same component — a dilation-aware Conv2d followed by `build_norm2d` and `build_activation` — with RSUConv just fixing kernel_size to 3. The same triple is built inline again as the `conv()` closure in `MultiResBlock` (models/backbone/multires_unet.py:18-23) and as raw `nn.Sequential` literals in `HRNetLite.BranchFusion` (models/backbone/hrnet_lite.py:32-34, 42-45) and `HRNetLite.__init__` (hrnet_lite.py:97-101, 121-125). The project rule in CLAUDE.md is explicit that a component needed in a second place moves to `models/blocks.py` and is imported from both; `models/blocks.py` already hosts the shared `ConvBlock`/`ResidualConvBlock`/`ConvNeXtBlock` family, so this one is simply missing from it.
evidence:
class ConvNormAct(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_channels:  int,
        output_channels: int,
        kernel_size:     int = 3,
        dilation:        int = 1,
suggested_fix: Move `ConvNormAct` into `models/blocks.py` and import it from deeplab_v3_plus, u2net_lite (replacing `RSUConv`), multires_unet and hrnet_lite.
verdict_notes: Confirmed on all cited sites: deeplab_v3_plus.py:12 ConvNormAct and u2net_lite.py:11 RSUConv are the same dilation-aware Conv2d + build_norm2d + build_activation unit (RSUConv just fixes kernel_size=3), multires_unet.py:18-23 rebuilds it as a local `conv()` closure, and hrnet_lite.py:32-45/97-101/121-125 inlines the same triple as raw nn.Sequential literals. models/blocks.py does NOT already provide it: ConvBlock (blocks.py:140) is a double-conv unit, and ResidualConvBlock/ConvNeXtBlock are heavier composites, so the single conv-norm-act primitive is genuinely missing. The repo rule is explicit that a component needed in a second place moves to models/blocks.py and is imported from both, and blocks.py is already the established home for exactly this family. Cross-module duplication of a shared primitive across four backbones is material.

title: Tuning entry hardcodes an --n-trials default that contradicts TuningConfig
description: `main/experiments/tune.py` declares `--n-trials` with `default=8` while the configuration dataclass sets `TuningConfig.n_trials = 100` (configuration/tuning/general.py:26). This is a tunable living in `main/`, which the project's config contract forbids. In practice the scheduler always passes `--n-trials` explicitly (pipelines/tuning/pipeline.py:72), so the 8 only bites someone invoking the worker by hand, silently running an eighth of the intended budget. The same function also silently falls back to a pristine `TuningEntryConfig()` when `--run-dir` is absent (line 47-49), discarding every scheduler-side override instead of failing loudly the way `ConfigCli.load_worker_config` does for the other experiment entries.
suggested_fix: Drop the argparse default (require the flag, or read it from `TuningConfig`), and make the worker path require `--run-dir` and error out when the resolved config is missing.
verdict_notes: Confirmed at main/experiments/tune.py:20-22 and 46-49. Two real deviations from the project's own config contract: a tunable default (--n-trials=8) lives in main/ while TuningConfig.n_trials=100, and the worker silently proceeds with a pristine TuningEntryConfig() when --run-dir is absent, discarding all scheduler-side overrides. Sibling workers (benchmark.py:32, cross_validate.py:36, sweep_patches.py:36) use ConfigCli.load_worker_config, which raises FileNotFoundError instead. The silent fallback is exactly the pattern the no-legacy-fallback policy forbids, and the fix is small and obvious.

title: embedding_dim is declared inside tunable_lr_params() on both autoencoder base configs
description: `ImageAutoencoderBaseConfig.tunable_lr_params()` (line 37) and `ProfileAutoencoderBaseConfig.tunable_lr_params()` (configuration/architectures/profile_autoencoder.py:31) both include `embedding_dim`, an architecture parameter, in the dict whose name and every other entry are learning rates and weight decays. It works only because the autoencoder tuner merges both dicts (`pipelines/tuning/tuners.py:174`); the JEPA tuner at tuners.py:230 uses `tunable_arch_params()` alone, so the same misplacement in a config consumed by that path would silently drop the parameter from the search space.
suggested_fix: Move `embedding_dim` into `tunable_arch_params()` on both base configs (subclasses override that method, so add it to each override or have them merge a base arch dict).
verdict_notes: Confirmed: embedding_dim, an architecture parameter, sits in tunable_lr_params() in both configuration/architectures/image_autoencoder.py:37 and profile_autoencoder.py:31, while both classes' tunable_arch_params() return an empty dict. It only reaches the search space because the AE tuner merges both maps (pipelines/tuning/tuners.py:174); the JEPA tuner at tuners.py:230 uses tunable_arch_params() alone, so the categorisation is load-bearing and currently wrong. One-line move with a clear correctness rationale.

title: Three divergent Gaussian evaluators; JEPA reconstructs GT curves differently at train and inference time
description:
The same mixture-of-Gaussians evaluation is implemented three times with three different numerical guards:
- `GaussianMixture` (lines 21-71): sigma clamped to `SIGMA_FLOOR=1e-6`, exponent clamped to [-100, 0], no amplitude clamp.
- `GaussianCurve.reconstruct` (lines 104-129, torch): same sigma floor and exponent clamp, no amplitude clamp.
- `GaussianReconstructor._single` (line 77, numpy): **no** sigma floor (uses `2.0*sig*sig + 1e-8`), **no** exponent clamp, and `reconstruct_batch` additionally clamps amplitude with `np.maximum(gauss[:, :, 0:1], 0.0)` while `components` (line 97) does not.

This is not just duplication — it changes results across the train/eval boundary. JEPA reconstructs its ground-truth curves with `GaussianCurve.reconstruct` during training (pipelines/jepa/training/loss.py:48) but with `GaussianReconstructor.reconstruct_batch` during inference (pipelines/jepa/inference/embedding.py:29). The backbone has the same split: training loss uses `GaussianCurve` (pipelines/backbone/training/loss.py:91), inference probes use `GaussianReconstructor` (pipelines/backbone/inference/probes.py:65). So the reference the model is scored against at inference is produced by a different function, with a different sigma guard and a silent negative-amplitude clamp, from the one it was optimised against.
suggested_fix: Collapse to one numpy implementation and one torch implementation that share the same constants (`SIGMA_FLOOR`, `EXPON_FLOOR`, `EXPON_CEIL`) and the same amplitude policy, then have `GaussianReconstructor`/`GaussianMixture` be thin shape-adapters over it. In particular decide once whether negative amplitudes are clamped and apply that decision on both sides of the train/eval boundary.
verdict_notes: Verified in tools/data/gaussians.py: GaussianMixture and GaussianCurve both clamp sigma to SIGMA_FLOOR=1e-6 and the exponent to [-100,0], while GaussianReconstructor._single (line 77) uses only an epsilon in the denominator with no exponent clamp, and reconstruct_batch silently clamps amplitude to >=0 while components does not. The train/eval split is confirmed by grep: JEPA loss (pipelines/jepa/training/loss.py:48) and backbone loss (pipelines/backbone/training/loss.py:91) use GaussianCurve, while inference (pipelines/jepa/inference/embedding.py:29, predictor.py:35, pipelines/backbone/inference/probes.py:65, predictor.py:246-247) uses GaussianReconstructor. Three implementations of the same math with divergent numerical guards, on opposite sides of the train/eval boundary, is a real correctness/consistency hazard (a near-zero sigma overflows in the numpy path but not the torch path) and the silent amplitude clamp is exactly the kind of hidden fallback the project bans. Consolidating to one evaluator is a clear improvement.

title: Importing the Logger drags in matplotlib through tools.reporting, only to serve a dead method
description: `tools/monitoring/logger.py` imports `tools.reporting.markdown`, which executes `tools/reporting/__init__.py`, which imports `.plotting` and therefore `matplotlib` (confirmed by the import traceback when running `from tools.reporting.markdown import MarkdownTable`). Every entry script, worker, and test that merely wants logging pays that import. The only use of `MarkdownDoc`/`MarkdownTable` inside logger.py is `Logger.save_profiler_results`, which nothing in the repository calls — grep over *.py, *.js and the JSON registries finds the single definition site and no caller and no test.
suggested_fix: Delete `Logger.save_profiler_results` and the markdown import (a profiler-report writer belongs in tools/reporting anyway); the monitoring package then no longer depends on the plotting stack.
verdict_notes: Verified end to end. tools/monitoring/logger.py:28 does a module-level `from tools.reporting.markdown import MarkdownDoc, MarkdownTable`; tools/reporting/__init__.py eagerly imports .plotting, which imports matplotlib and calls matplotlib.use("Agg"). So any process that imports the Logger (every entry script, worker, and test) pays a matplotlib import. The only consumer of those symbols is Logger.save_profiler_results (logger.py:369), and a repo-wide grep for both 'save_profiler_results' and 'profiler' returns exactly one hit -- the definition itself -- with no caller and no test. This is real, material, and the fix is trivial (delete the dead method, or move the import into it). Not covered by any known non-issue: it is a genuine unnecessary heavy-dependency coupling in a core infra module, not a dynamic-dispatch false positive.

title: `tune` is missing from TRAINING_LOGDIRS although the tuning pipeline writes TensorBoard events
description: `TRAINING_LOGDIRS` maps `benchmark`, `cross_validate` and `sweep_patches` to `paths.log_base_dir`, but omits `tune`, whose config also carries `paths.log_base_dir` (`configuration/tuning/general.py:44`) and whose pipeline writes per-trial event files under `<log_base_dir>/<tag>/trials/trial_XXXX` (`pipelines/tuning/tuners.py:121,185,246`, via `RunMetadata`'s `SummaryWriter`). As a result the Optuna search is the only experiment entry that gets neither TensorBoard autostart nor a `/api/tensorboard/start` default logdir, unlike its three siblings. (`train_unrolled`'s absence is deliberate — it emits no TB scalars — but `tune` does.)
suggested_fix: Add `"tune": ("paths.log_base_dir",)` to `TRAINING_LOGDIRS`.
verdict_notes: Verified: TuningEntryConfig (configuration/tuning/general.py) carries paths.log_base_dir and pipelines/tuning/tuners.py writes real TensorBoard event files under <log_dir>/trials/..., yet webui/tensorboard_manager.py TRAINING_LOGDIRS omits "tune" while including its three orchestration siblings (benchmark, cross_validate, sweep_patches). This is a concrete functional gap, not taste: Optuna searches get no TB autostart and no default logdir in /api/tensorboard/start, and the fix is a one-line map entry.

title: /proc/meminfo, /proc/stat and the /proc pid walk are each reimplemented in three separate monitors
description: Three byte-for-byte equivalent /proc/meminfo parsers exist: system_monitor.py:224 (`_memory`), contention_monitor.py:181 (`_read_memory`) and resource_watchdog.py:139 (`_ram_percent`). Two copies of the /proc/stat busy/total CPU-percent computation exist: system_monitor.py:40-53 (`_cpu_counters`) and resource_watchdog.py:121-134 (`_cpu_percent`). Three near-identical full /proc pid walks with the same fragile `stat[stat.rindex(")") + 2:].split()` field indexing exist: system_monitor.py:82-121 (`_procs`), system_monitor.py:444-467 (`ActiveUsers._scan`) and contention_monitor.py:252-285 (`ContentionMonitor._scan`). The project rule is explicit that a component needed in a second place is moved to a shared module rather than copied, and this duplication is also what lets the per-pid CPU-delta bug exist in one copy and not the others.
suggested_fix: Move the /proc readers (meminfo, stat CPU counters, pid stat field extraction) into a single shared ProcStats-style module that all three monitors import, and have the three scanners share one walk.
verdict_notes: Verified in source. /proc/meminfo is parsed three times (system_monitor.py:_memory, contention_monitor.py:_read_memory, resource_watchdog.py:_ram_percent) with identical partition/int-parse logic; the /proc/stat busy = sum(vals[1:9]) - vals[3] - vals[4] computation appears in both system_monitor._cpu_counters and resource_watchdog._cpu_percent; and three full /proc pid walks repeat the same fragile stat[stat.rindex(')') + 2:].split() with magic field indices 11/12/17/21 (system_monitor._procs, ActiveUsers._scan, ContentionMonitor._scan). This is low-level OS parsing, exactly the kind of thing that belongs in one shared helper: the magic offsets are easy to get wrong, a kernel/format assumption change must be fixed in three places, and the known per-caller CPU-delta bug lives in one copy only because the walk was copied rather than shared. Material and fixable with a small webui-level /proc reader module.

title: Large field lists in LAUNCH layouts are duplicated verbatim across pages
description: The `experiment_builder` field list is copied verbatim (about 20 lines, 40+ paths) between `train_backbone` (lines 623-634) and `train_dual` (797-810), the latter adding only `routing_trials.*` and `ratio_trials.*`. The JEPA "Autoencoder runs" group with its three `checkpointOnly` dataset pickers is copied verbatim three times — `benchmark` (911-923), `cross_validate` (980-992) and `tune` (1088-1100). The five `INFER_*_LAYOUT` dicts (463-516) differ only in section key, title and template. The existing tests catch drift only when a config field is added or removed; a widget or picker tweak applied to one copy and not the others is invisible to them.
suggested_fix: Hoist the shared experiment-builder list and the JEPA autoencoder group into module-level constants (like TRAIN_ESSENTIALS / INFER_ESSENTIALS already are) and build the five inference layouts from one helper parameterised by key/title/template.
verdict_notes: Confirmed by reading the layout dicts. The ~20-line, 40+ path experiment_builder field list is byte-identical between train_backbone (623-634) and train_dual (797-810) apart from two added trial groups, and the JEPA 'Autoencoder runs' group with its three checkpointOnly dataset pickers is repeated verbatim in benchmark, cross_validate and tune. The file already establishes the fix as its own convention (INFER_ESSENTIALS, CH_AE_MODE, GPU_MANY, named templates are hoisted constants), so this is inconsistency with the module's own style rather than a taste preference. The drift risk is concrete: layout is declarative data no test compares across pages, so a widget/picker tweak applied to one copy silently diverges, and only field add/remove is caught. The INFER_*_LAYOUT sub-claim is the weakest part (nine short lines each, a factory may not be clearer), but the two big duplications alone justify the finding.

title: note()/_strip_operational()/_notes_dir() and the OPERATIONAL_* regexes are copy-pasted verbatim across four model libraries
description: `OPERATIONAL_PAREN`, `OPERATIONAL_MARKERS`, `OPERATIONAL_HEADING`, `note()`, `_strip_operational()` and `_notes_dir()` are byte-for-byte identical in webui/backbone_model_library.py (lines 10-12, 74-121), webui/jepa_model_library.py (lines 9-11, 19-66), webui/image_autoencoder_model_library.py (lines 10-12, 33-80) and webui/profile_autoencoder_model_library.py (lines 10-12, 37-84). The `collect()`/`_resolve_defaults()` pair is also duplicated three times with only the config-module import and the attribute name (`normalization` vs `embedding_norm`) differing. This directly violates the project rule against copying a function between modules: a change to the note-sanitising rules now has to be made in four places, and any missed copy silently serves differently-sanitised markdown for one model family.
suggested_fix: Extract a `ModelNoteLibrary` base class (note sanitising, notes dir, defaults resolution) into a shared module and have the four libraries subclass it, supplying only NOTE_FILES, CONFIG_CLASSES, the config module and the normalization attribute name.
verdict_notes: Verified by reading all four files: OPERATIONAL_PAREN/OPERATIONAL_MARKERS/OPERATIONAL_HEADING plus note(), _strip_operational() (~26 lines) and _notes_dir() are byte-for-byte identical in webui/backbone_model_library.py (10-12, 74-121), webui/jepa_model_library.py (9-11, 19-66), webui/profile_autoencoder_model_library.py (10-12, 37-84) and webui/image_autoencoder_model_library.py. collect()/_resolve_defaults()/_import_*_config() are duplicated near-verbatim too, differing only in the imported config module and the attribute name (normalization vs embedding_norm). ~50 lines of copy-paste across four modules, directly violating the standing project rule 'Never copy a class or function between modules'; the sanitising regexes are behaviour-bearing, so a rule change edited in three of four places silently serves differently-sanitised markdown for one model family. Fix (shared note-library base/module) is obvious and clearly improves the code.

title: The dual model family has no flow and no repo-map diagram, and unrolled inference has no repo-map diagram
description: `models/dual/`, `pipelines/dual/` (training pipeline, launcher, experiments, inference loader and pipeline), `main/training/train_dual.py` and `main/inference/infer_dual.py` are a first-class model family with its own registry (`DUAL_CONFIG_REGISTRY`), its own trials mode, and a dedicated webui toggle. `FlowLibrary.collect()` returns 15 flows covering backbone, profile-AE, image-AE, JEPA and unrolled but nothing for dual, and repomap_data.json contains 13 folders / 30 diagrams with no dual folder at all. repomap_data.json also has `unrolled-training` but no `unrolled-inference`, while every other family has both. Running RepoMapDeriver.drift over the curated map shows all five pipelines/dual modules and all six pipelines/unrolled/inference modules as uncovered. The Flows and Repo Map tabs therefore silently present an incomplete picture of the codebase.
evidence:
return [
            self._processing(),
            self._param_extraction(),
            self._dataset(),
            self._training(),
            self._profile_ae_train(),
            self._image_ae_train(),
            self._jepa_train(),

suggested_fix: Add a `_dual_train` (and ideally `_dual_infer`) flow plus `dual-training` / `dual-inference` and `unrolled-inference` repomap diagrams, or state in the tab blurb which families the curated content deliberately omits.
verdict_notes: Verified: models/dual/, pipelines/dual/{training,inference} exist as a first-class family with DUAL_CONFIG_REGISTRY, dedicated main/ entries and a webui toggle, yet FlowLibrary.collect() (webui/flow_library.py:2075) lists 15 flows with no dual entry, and repomap_data.json's folder list (preprocessing, param_extraction, backbone, profile_autoencoder, image_autoencoder, jepa, unrolled, shared, cross_validation, benchmarking, tune, comparison, weights_xray) contains no dual folder and no unrolled-inference counterpart. The webui's documentation tabs are curated project artifacts with a drift checker, so an entire uncovered model family is a real, material gap with a clear fix.

title: resolveChromium() copied verbatim into all four visual-harness scripts
description: The identical 12-line `resolveChromium()` (PW_CHROMIUM env override, scan `~/.cache/ms-playwright` for `chromium*`, try `chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell` then `chrome-linux/chrome`, throw otherwise) is duplicated in snap_ui.js:34, dump_frames.js:16, render_diagram.js:35 and snap_repomap.js:33. Any change to the Playwright cache layout has to be made in four places.
suggested_fix: Extract a `chromium.js` module in webui/tools/visual/ exporting one `ChromiumResolver` class and require it from the four entry scripts.
verdict_notes: Confirmed: resolveChromium() is byte-equivalent in all four scripts under webui/tools/visual/ (snap_ui.js:34, dump_frames.js:16, render_diagram.js:35, snap_repomap.js:33), same env override, same cache scan, same two relative exe paths, same error text. The four files sit in one directory with a package.json, so a shared chromium.js module is a trivial, obviously-correct extraction, and today any Playwright cache-layout change must be applied four times.

title: Triage re-render fabricates a partial payload and duplicates the server's AUX_LAYERS list
description: `_annotate()` re-renders with a hand-built stand-in for the API payload — `this._renderCases({ has_modes: ..., aux: this._auxKeys() })` — instead of the real response, and `_auxKeys()` hardcodes `["label_r2", "seed_std_profile", "flip_consistency"]`, a verbatim copy of `TriageBoard.AUX_LAYERS` (webui/triage_board.py:55). The server also sorts and filters that list by which maps actually loaded, so the two derivations can disagree, and adding a fourth aux layer server-side silently fails to appear after any annotation. The full re-render also wipes any note text the user typed but has not committed in the other cards.
suggested_fix: Keep the last `/api/triage/cases` payload on `this` and re-render from it after annotating; patch the single affected card instead of rebuilding the grid.
verdict_notes: Confirmed by reading triage.js:144-170 and triage_board.py:55. _annotate() re-renders with a fabricated payload {has_modes: this.cases.some(...), aux: this._auxKeys()} rather than the real API response, and _auxKeys() hardcodes the same three names as TriageBoard.AUX_LAYERS. The server filters/orders that list by which .npy maps actually loaded, so the two derivations can diverge and a new server-side aux layer silently stops appearing after an annotation. Fix is a one-liner (cache the load payload and re-render from it), so the cost/benefit clearly favors raising it.

title: ExperimentBuilder is ~2.8 kloc of fifteen near-identical mode panels
description: `ExperimentBuilder` (lines 399-3163) implements each of its 15 fan-out modes with the same hand-copied quadruple: `_<mode>Panel()` builds a header + note + chip container, `_<mode>Trials()/_<mode>Weights()` parse the leaf through `PythonLiteral` in an identical try/catch, `_emit<Mode>()` renders back and `_paint<Mode>()`/`_repaint<Mode>()` rebuild the chips. `_physicsWeightChip` (1132) and `_pairWeightChip` (1394) are byte-for-byte the same but for a title string; `_togglePhysicsComponent` (1120), `_togglePairCandidate` (1382) and `_toggleHeadOption` (2157) are the same catalog-ordered toggle; `_togglePresenceCell` (1555) and `_toggleAugCell` (2005) are the same dict-cell toggle. `refreshFromView()` and `_paintMode()` then have to enumerate all fifteen by hand, so every new mode touches six places.
suggested_fix: Describe each mode declaratively (leaf names, chip renderer, summary formula, name pattern) in one table and drive one generic list/dict panel class from it, splitting the file so launch_widgets.js is not a 5 kloc grab bag.
verdict_notes: Confirmed at scale: launch_widgets.js is 5224 lines and ExperimentBuilder occupies roughly 399-3163 of them. Spot checks match the claim - _togglePhysicsComponent (1120) and _togglePairCandidate (1382) are the same catalog-ordered toggle, and _physicsWeightChip (1132) vs _pairWeightChip (1394) differ only in the input title string. With fifteen modes each requiring panel/trials/weights/emit/paint plus manual enumeration in refreshFromView() and _paintMode(), this is a material organization problem: every new fan-out mode edits six places. A table-driven mode descriptor is the obvious fix.

title: Four gauge classes each re-implement the same easing/peak-tracking state machine
description: `DialGauge`, `LinearMeter`, `TankGauge` and `SegMeter` all repeat the same `_raf`/`_tick` easing loop (`this.v += (this.t - this.v) * 0.14`, settle threshold, redraw), the same `set()` with `REDUCED_MOTION` short-circuit, the same `onResize()` guard and (in the first two) the same 60 s peak-decay logic — roughly 40 duplicated lines per class. A per-project rule forbids copying a component between modules; here it is copied four times inside one.
suggested_fix: Introduce an `AnimatedGauge extends CanvasBase` holding `set`/`_tick`/`onResize`/peak state, and let the four gauges implement only `_draw()`.
verdict_notes: Confirmed: DialGauge (3), LinearMeter (159), TankGauge (299) and SegMeter (395) each repeat the same _raf/_tick easing loop (`+= (t - v) * 0.14`, settle threshold, redraw, re-schedule), the same REDUCED_MOTION short-circuit in set(), and the same `onResize() { if (this._ready) this._draw(); }`. The finding's 40-lines-per-class figure is inflated (closer to 15-20), and the classes use different field names (v/t vs f/t), but all four already extend a shared CanvasBase, so hoisting the animation state machine there is a natural and low-risk consolidation rather than a speculative abstraction.

title: _SilentLogger and the force-CPU fixture are copy-pasted across a dozen test modules instead of living in conftest
description: Ten modules in this scope each define their own `_SilentLogger` (tests/backbone_inference/test_data_consistency.py:15, test_figures.py:25, test_flip_consistency.py:15, test_paper_figures.py:13, test_pipeline_e2e.py:22, test_predictor.py:25, test_reduced.py:23, test_seed_comparison.py:13, test_seed_disagreement.py:18, test_training_evolution.py:14, plus tests/benchmark/test_results.py:17, test_sizing.py:12, test_stages.py:21 and tests/dataloader_tuning/test_adapters.py:26 — 17 copies repo-wide). Two incompatible variants exist: an explicit `section/subsection/kv_table` stub that raises AttributeError when production code starts calling a new logger method, and a catch-all `__getattr__` stub that silently swallows everything. Which one a test gets is accidental. The same applies to the CUDA-disabling fixture, duplicated as `force_cpu`/`_force_cpu` in tests/backbone_training/test_pipeline.py:16, test_trainer.py:17, test_new_backbone_runtime.py:25, tests/ae_training/test_image_ae_pipeline.py:29, test_image_ae_trainer.py:23, test_profile_ae_pipeline.py:31, test_profile_ae_trainer.py:22, tests/ae_inference/test_pipeline_e2e.py:25 and tests/dual_inference/test_pipeline_e2e.py:31.
evidence:
class _SilentLogger:
    def section(self, *a, **k):    pass
    def subsection(self, *a, **k): pass
    def kv_table(self, *a, **k):   pass
suggested_fix: Move one silent-logger stub (preferably the strict, explicit-method variant) and one `force_cpu` fixture into tests/conftest.py and import/consume them everywhere.
verdict_notes: Verified: 17 modules define their own _SilentLogger, and the two variants are genuinely incompatible — the explicit section/subsection/kv_table stub (tests/backbone_inference/*, e.g. test_figures.py:25, test_reduced.py:23) raises AttributeError when production code calls a new logger method, while the catch-all __getattr__ stub (tests/benchmark/test_stages.py:21, tests/dataloader_tuning/test_adapters.py:26) silently swallows it. tests/conftest.py exists (130 lines) and holds neither the stub nor the CUDA-disabling fixture, so the consolidation target is already there. Not a pure style nit: which failure mode a test gets is accidental, and the silent variant hides real regressions.

title: tests/dual_training and tests/dual_inference are the only test directories without __init__.py
description: Every other directory under tests/ (backbone_training, backbone_inference, ae_training, ae_inference, benchmark, comparison, configuration, cross_validation, data_layer, dataloader_tuning, diagnostics, entrypoints, inference_dispatch, ...) ships an __init__.py, which is what makes cross-package imports like `from tests.backbone_training._helpers import geometry_config` work and what keeps module names fully qualified. tests/dual_training/ and tests/dual_inference/ (and tests/models_dual/, outside this scope) lack it, so under pytest's default prepend import mode their modules are imported as bare top-level names (`test_loader`, `test_experiments`, `test_pipeline_e2e`) with their directory injected into sys.path. Those basenames already exist as fully-qualified modules in backbone_inference/backbone_training; the moment a second __init__-less directory gains a file with the same basename, pytest fails with 'import file mismatch'. tests/dual_inference/test_pipeline_e2e.py also imports `tests.backbone_training._helpers`, so it depends on the package layout it does not itself participate in.
suggested_fix: Add empty __init__.py files to tests/dual_training/ and tests/dual_inference/ (and tests/models_dual/) to match every sibling package.
verdict_notes: Confirmed by directory scan: tests/dual_inference, tests/dual_training and tests/models_dual are the only package dirs under tests/ without __init__.py (tests/__init__.py itself exists, so every other dir imports fully qualified). Under pytest prepend mode those modules become bare top-level names whose basenames (test_pipeline_e2e, test_experiments, test_loader) already exist as qualified modules elsewhere, and tests/dual_inference/test_pipeline_e2e.py imports tests.backbone_training._helpers, so it depends on the package layout it opts out of. Latent 'import file mismatch' breakage with a one-file fix — worth raising.

title: tests/webui has no conftest.py, so every fixture and stub is copy-pasted across 33 files
description: There is no `tests/webui/conftest.py`. As a result the 8-line `REPO_ROOT/WEBUI_ROOT` sys.path bootstrap is repeated verbatim in 33 test modules; `class StubPaths` is redefined in 12 modules with 6 different, silently divergent attribute sets (`repo_root`/`main_dir`/`logs_dir`/`gpu_pools_dir`/`saved_runs_dir`/`gpu_guard_dir`); `class StubDescriber` in 5; and the `_make_cube_run` + `_loaded_explorer` pair (including a 30-second `load_status()` polling loop) is duplicated in `test_cube_explorer_metrics.py`, `test_cube_explorer_params.py`, `test_cube_explorer_save.py`, and near-duplicated again in `test_cube_explorer_attach.py` and `test_slice_collector.py`. When `ProcessManager` or `CubeExplorer` grows a new path or artifact, each copy has to be found and updated independently.
suggested_fix: Add `tests/webui/conftest.py` holding the sys.path bootstrap, one parameterised `StubPaths`, `StubDescriber`, and a `loaded_cube_explorer` fixture with the shared wait-for-ready helper; delete the per-file copies.
verdict_notes: Verified: tests/webui/conftest.py genuinely does not exist while tests/ has a top-level conftest.py, so the pattern is established elsewhere. 33 of 35 webui test modules repeat the REPO_ROOT/WEBUI_ROOT sys.path bootstrap verbatim, `class StubPaths` is redefined in 12 modules with divergent attribute sets, and the _make_cube_run/_loaded_explorer pair is duplicated across three cube_explorer test modules (with a third variant taking extra kwargs). This is real, material duplication with an obvious fix (a package conftest with shared fixtures/stubs), and it directly causes drift when ProcessManager or CubeExplorer grows a new path.

title: tests/models_dual is missing __init__.py, unlike every sibling test package
description: Every other test directory in scope (`tests/models_backbone`, `tests/models_autoencoders`, `tests/models_baseline`, `tests/models_unrolled`, ...) ships an `__init__.py`; `tests/models_dual/` does not (nor do `tests/dual_inference/` and `tests/dual_training/`). Under pytest's default prepend import mode this silently changes the module name from `tests.models_dual.test_dual_resunet` to a top-level `test_dual_resunet` and prepends the directory to `sys.path`. It also blocks the `from tests.<pkg>._helpers import ...` reuse pattern the unrolled tests rely on, and makes basename collisions with other non-package test dirs a latent collection error.
evidence:
from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
import torch

from models.dual             import DUAL_MODEL_REGISTRY, get_dual
suggested_fix: Add empty `tests/models_dual/__init__.py` (and the same for tests/dual_inference and tests/dual_training) to match the rest of the suite.
verdict_notes: Verified: tests/models_dual/, tests/dual_inference/, and tests/dual_training/ are the only non-__pycache__ test dirs lacking __init__.py; all siblings (models_backbone, backbone_inference, jepa, configuration, ...) have one. The consequences claimed are accurate: basenames collide with package siblings (test_loader.py, test_pipeline_e2e.py, test_experiments.py) so rootdir-relative module naming is inconsistent, and the widely used `from tests.<pkg>._helpers import ...` pattern (18+ call sites, including dual_inference importing from tests.backbone_training._helpers) cannot be applied in reverse to these dirs. Minor severity but a real, one-line consistency fix.

title: Eleven live webui modules (~5700 lines) have no test coverage at all
description: Grepping the whole tests/ tree for each module name returns zero hits for: `contention_monitor.py` (472 lines), `equation_library.py` (1695), `flow_library.py` (2092), `physics_loss_library.py` (368), `pipeline_library.py` (113), `profile_autoencoder_model_library.py` (164), `image_autoencoder_model_library.py` (150), `jepa_model_library.py` (94), `resource_watchdog.py` (149), `tensorboard_manager.py` (231), `web_ui_server.py` (181). All are instantiated in `webui/web_ui_server.py:92-96` and injected into `RequestRouter.__init__`, so they are live production paths, not dead code. The asymmetry is stark: `tests/webui/test_backbone_model_library.py` asserts that `BackboneModelLibrary.CONFIG_CLASSES`/`NOTE_FILES` cover `BACKBONE_MODEL_REGISTRY` exactly and that every model resolves a note — the three sibling model libraries (profile-AE, image-AE, JEPA) have no equivalent guard, so a new autoencoder in the registry would ship with a missing note and nothing would fail.
evidence:
from resource_watchdog                 import ResourceWatchdog
from contention_monitor                import ContentionMonitor
from tensorboard_manager               import TensorboardManager
suggested_fix: At minimum add registry-coverage tests for the three sibling model libraries mirroring test_backbone_model_library.py, plus schema tests for equation_library/flow_library/physics_loss_library/pipeline_library like tests/webui/test_repomap_library.py already does for RepoMapLibrary.
verdict_notes: Verified by grepping the whole tests/ tree: zero references to any of the eleven module names or their classes (ContentionMonitor, ResourceWatchdog, TensorboardManager, EquationLibrary, FlowLibrary, PipelineLibrary, PhysicsLossLibrary, the three AE/JEPA model libraries, web_ui_server), covering ~5700 live lines wired into web_ui_server and RequestRouter. The asymmetry is concrete and actionable: tests/webui/test_backbone_model_library.py asserts CONFIG_CLASSES and NOTE_FILES cover BACKBONE_MODEL_REGISTRY exactly, but the three sibling model libraries have no equivalent registry-coverage guard, so a newly registered autoencoder/JEPA model would ship with a missing note silently. Worth raising.

title: tools/__init__.py is an unused facade that forces matplotlib, torch, tensorboard and the pyrat stack to load on any tools import
description: The 61-line aggregate re-export in tools/__init__.py is imported by nothing in production: `grep -rn 'from tools import' --include=*.py .` returns 0 hits, and only three test helpers touch it via `import tools` (tests/backbone_training/_helpers.py:104, test_loss.py:463, test_loss_probe.py:32) and use just `NullLogger`/`NullTracker` out of the ~50 names in `__all__`. Everything else imports submodules directly (`from tools.monitoring.logger import Logger`). Because Python executes the package `__init__` before any submodule, this facade makes every `import tools.<anything>` eagerly pull matplotlib (via .reporting -> plotting), torch (via .training), the tensorboard EventAccumulator (via .diagnostics -> tensorboard_export), and the pyrat env/launchers (via .sar). Demonstrated concretely: `python3 -c 'import tools.data.io'` fails with `No module named 'matplotlib'` even though tools/data/io.py imports only json/os/pathlib. That inflates startup cost for every entry script and worker process and couples unrelated subsystems.
evidence:
from .monitoring    import Logger, NullLogger, NullTracker, ResourceMonitor, Tracker
from .reporting     import MarkdownDoc, MarkdownTable, MetricSectionGrouper, PlotBase, ReportAssets
...
from .diagnostics   import IssueDetector, LayerReport, StateDictResolver, WeightAnalyzer, WeightXray, XraySummarizer
from .training      import BaseTrainer, Checkpoint, EarlyStopping, GradientClipper, MetricAggregator, Scheduler, Warmup
from .sar           import InterferogramLauncher, TomogramLauncher
suggested_fix: Empty tools/__init__.py (keep at most NullLogger/NullTracker if the test helpers should stay as-is) and let callers keep importing submodules directly.
verdict_notes: Verified end to end. `grep -rn 'from tools import'` returns zero hits; only three test helpers do `import tools` (tests/backbone_training/_helpers.py:6, test_loss.py:15, test_loss_probe.py:15) and _helpers.py uses only tools.NullLogger / tools.NullTracker. Meanwhile 629 call sites import submodules directly (`from tools.<sub>...`). The coupling claim reproduces exactly: `python3 -c 'import tools.data.io'` fails with ModuleNotFoundError: matplotlib, traced to tools/reporting/plotting.py:6, because Python runs tools/__init__.py first and line 2 pulls .reporting -> plotting -> matplotlib (and line 6 pulls torch via .training, line 5 the tensorboard EventAccumulator, line 9 the pyrat launchers). So a module that imports only json/os/pathlib cannot be imported without the entire plotting/torch/tensorboard/pyrat stack. This is a real architectural defect, not taste: a facade with no production consumers imposes eager cross-subsystem imports and startup cost on every entry script and worker process, and it is not on the known-non-issues list (it is not dynamic dispatch, not a main/ bootstrap ordering, not a legacy shim). The fix is small and unambiguous - delete the aggregate re-export and have the three test helpers import tools.monitoring directly - and it clearly improves the codebase.

title: webui/README.md has drifted badly from the code it documents
description: Concrete, verifiable mismatches: line 4 and line 31 say "the nine entry-point scripts" / "The nine `main/*.py` entry points" — `ScriptCatalog.META` has 39 entries and main/ holds 41 non-underscore entry scripts. Line 29 says "Ten backbones across three families" — `BACKBONE_MODEL_REGISTRY` and `BackboneModelLibrary._families()` both hold 20. Lines 18, 27 and 83 say KaTeX — the frontend uses MathJax (`grep -c katex webui/static/index.html` returns 0; index.html:1111 loads `mathjax@3.2.2`), and it also pulls xterm, which the list omits. Line 84 documents `model_library.py ModelLibrary`, a file that does not exist (it is four files: backbone/, profile_autoencoder/, image_autoencoder/, jepa_model_library.py). Line 53 names `tools/config_cli.py`; the real path is `tools/runtime/config_cli.py` (`script_config_resolver.py:122` watches the correct one). The backend architecture block lists 11 modules out of 39, and the frontend block lists 9 JS files out of 34.
evidence: project's signal-model equations, lets you browse and configure the nine entry-point
suggested_fix: Regenerate the counts and file lists from the code (a test asserting the counts against ScriptCatalog.META and BACKBONE_MODEL_REGISTRY would keep them honest), and replace every KaTeX mention with MathJax.
verdict_notes: Verified in the repo: README says "nine entry-point scripts" while main/ holds 41 non-underscore entries and ScriptCatalog covers far more; index.html has zero katex hits and loads mathjax@3.2.2; webui/model_library.py does not exist (four *_model_library.py files do); tools/config_cli.py does not exist (tools/runtime/config_cli.py does); static/js has 34 files vs the 9 listed. Documentation this wrong actively misleads anyone onboarding to the console, and the fix is mechanical.

title: The run-selection cascade and the whole *Batch wrapper are copy-pasted across 13 modules
description: The identical four-line cascade `if run_filter: return selector.filter(...); if sys.stdin.isatty(): return selector.select(); return selector.all()` appears verbatim in 13 modules: pipelines/backbone/inference/{activation_xray:135, attention_capture:274, input_attribution:278, layer_probes:291, loss_landscape:225, receptive_field:199, robustness:183, representation_cka:108, training_evolution:146, paper_figures:23}, tools/diagnostics/{weight_xray:103, tensorboard_export:327} and tools/reporting/report_collector:111. In nine of them the entire enclosing `*Batch` class is a template — `__init__(config, logger)`, `_select_runs`, and a `run()` that logs a section and loops calling `<X>Run(run_dir, config, logger).run()` — differing only by the RunSelector `action=` string, the section title and the Run class. A matching `_load_run` body is duplicated eight times across the same package (identical in six: layer_probes:198, robustness:105, loss_landscape:120, activation_xray:31, attention_capture:176, input_attribution:176). `RunSelector` already exposes `select`/`filter`/`all` but not the cascade, which is the natural home for it.
suggested_fix: Add `RunSelector.resolve(run_filter)` holding the cascade, and introduce a `RunBatchBase` (config, logger, section title, Run class) that the nine template batches subclass.
verdict_notes: Confirmed: the same four-line run_filter/isatty/all cascade is verbatim in 13 modules, and the surrounding *Batch class is a near-identical template (compared activation_xray.py:135 and weight_xray.py:103 directly - identical except the config attribute name, action string and Run class). RunSelector already owns select/filter/all and is the obvious home for the cascade. Real, concrete duplication with a cheap, low-risk fix.

title: pipelines/backbone/inference conflates the inference pipeline with eleven standalone analysis tools
description: The package holds 30 modules. Only about half participate in `pipeline.py` (loader, predictor, model_wrapper, metrics, figures, report, plots/, reduced, stratified, failure_modes, flip_consistency, data_consistency, normalization_audit, presence_calibration, probes, run_metadata_paths). Eleven modules are never imported by anything inside the inference pipeline and are only reachable from a main/analysis entry: activation_xray, attention_capture, loss_landscape, receptive_field, robustness, representation_cka, training_evolution, paper_figures, layer_probes, input_attribution, seed_comparison (I traced every intra-package import; the only inbound edges for these are between themselves). They are post-hoc model diagnostics, not the sliding-window inference pipeline, and their siblings of identical shape live under tools/diagnostics and tools/reporting — so the same concept is currently spread across three packages.
suggested_fix: Split the eleven post-hoc tools into `pipelines/backbone/analysis/` (or `pipelines/diagnostics/`) and move the tools/ batches there too, leaving `pipelines/backbone/inference/` as just the inference pipeline.
verdict_notes: Verified: pipelines/backbone/inference holds 30 modules, and activation_xray, attention_capture, loss_landscape, receptive_field, robustness, representation_cka, training_evolution, paper_figures, layer_probes, input_attribution and seed_comparison are not referenced by pipeline.py at all - they are post-hoc diagnostics reachable only from main/analysis entries. Half a package that has nothing to do with the sliding-window inference pipeline is a real discoverability problem, and the same concept also lives under tools/diagnostics and tools/reporting.

title: RequestRouter is a 1000-line god object: 35 constructor collaborators and a 464-line if/elif dispatch
description: `__init__` takes 35 injected collaborators on a single source line (line 56). `_route_get` (line 94) runs 464 lines to line 557 as a flat `if path == ... : ...; return` chain, and `_route_post` another 195 lines; together they contain 103 path comparisons. `parse_qs(urlparse(handler.path).query)` is re-written 40 times inside those two methods, and the `self._send_json(handler, result, 200 if result.get("ok") else 404)` idiom is repeated dozens of times. The file has 19 methods total, so ~66% of it is the two dispatch methods. Any new tab requires editing the same two functions and the 35-argument signature.
evidence:
def _route_get(self, handler, path: str) -> None:
        if path == "/" or path == "":
suggested_fix: Replace the if-chain with a route table mapping (method, path) -> handler callable, parse the query string once per request in `route()`, and group the 35 collaborators into a few service objects (results/cubes/datasets; system/watchdogs; libraries; process control).
verdict_notes: Verified against the file: 1001 lines, a single-line __init__ taking 35 collaborators (line 56), _route_get spanning lines 94-557 and _route_post 558-752 as flat if-path-equals chains, 88 path comparisons and 41 parse_qs(urlparse(...)) repetitions, with only 19 methods total. This is a textbook god object where every new endpoint edits the same two functions and the 35-argument signature - a strong senior would raise it.

title: shape_logger_types is a diagnostics detail stored in 20 config dataclasses and special-cased out of persistence three times
description: `shape_logger_types: tuple = field(default_factory=lambda: (nn.Conv2d, nn.ConvTranspose2d, ...))` is repeated verbatim in all 20 backbone config dataclasses in this 1360-line file. It holds nn module *classes*, so it is not serializable and every persistence path has to exclude it: `pipelines/shared/config/config_persistence.py` declares `EXCLUDED = {"shape_logger_types"}` three separate times (lines 82, 125, 140), and two tests exist purely to assert it is excluded. Its only real consumer is `pipelines/backbone/training/docs.py:188`. A config field that no persistence layer may touch and that every class must repeat is a misplaced responsibility.
suggested_fix: Move the tuple to a module-level constant in `pipelines/backbone/training/docs.py` (or a small shared base dataclass), delete the 20 field declarations and the three EXCLUDED sets.
verdict_notes: Confirmed: shape_logger_types appears 20 times in configuration/architectures/backbone.py plus dual.py and unrolled.py, holds nn module classes so it cannot be serialized, and config_persistence.py has to declare EXCLUDED = {"shape_logger_types"} three separate times with tests asserting the exclusion. Its only consumer is pipelines/backbone/training/docs.py:188. A field every config must repeat and no persistence path may touch belongs in the diagnostics module, not the config dataclasses.

title: _catalog_root path validation is copy-pasted across three webui modules
description: The identical 13-line `_catalog_root(raw)` staticmethod — strip, empty check, `expanduser`, absolute check, `resolve`, is_dir check, returning `(Path|None, message)` — appears verbatim in webui/run_leaderboard.py:398, webui/training_curves.py:121 and webui/cube_explorer.py (same error strings at lines 845/849). webui/results_browser.py has two further partial copies (lines 40 and 157) using the same "an absolute path is required" message in a different return shape.
suggested_fix: Move it to `webui/project_paths.py` as `ProjectPaths.catalog_root(raw)` and have all five call sites use it.
verdict_notes: Verified byte-identical bodies at run_leaderboard.py:398, training_curves.py:121 and cube_explorer.py:842, with the same error strings reused in results_browser.py at lines 40 and 157 in a different return shape. This is path validation (absolute-path check plus resolve) duplicated across the webui surface, where divergence between copies has real consequences; a shared helper is the obvious fix.

title: figure_style is free text on the nine diagnostics pages but a choice widget on the inference pages
description: figure_style accepts exactly two values (report, paper) and the layout already declares CH_FIGSTYLE = {"kind": "choice", "options": ["report", "paper"]}, applied in the inference_full, profile_inference, image_inference and unrolled_inference templates (lines 369, 398, 405, 412). Every diagnostics page instead lists the bare string: xray_activations (1254), measure_receptive_field (1277), animate_training (1300), stress_inputs (1325), map_loss_landscape (1350), compare_representations (1374), probe_layers (1399), capture_attention (1419), attribute_inputs (1448). Those forms render a free-text box for a two-valued enum, so a typo is only caught (if at all) inside the plotting code after the job starts.
suggested_fix: Replace the bare "figure_style" entries on all nine diagnostics layouts with {"path": "figure_style", "widget": CH_FIGSTYLE}.
verdict_notes: Verified: CH_FIGSTYLE = {kind: choice, options: [report, paper]} exists and is applied in inference_full/profile_inference/image_inference/unrolled_inference (lines ~369-412), while all nine diagnostics pages list the bare string "figure_style" and therefore render a free-text box. The config dataclasses declare figure_style as a plain str with no validation (configuration/diagnostics.py x9, configuration/inference/*), so a typo in the webui form is only caught later inside plotting code. Same field, same two-valued enum, inconsistent widget in the same file; the fix is one token per site and reuses an existing constant.

title: _validate builds the claimed-path set as a side effect of the duplicate-detection comprehension
description: `duplicates` is computed with a set comprehension whose filter mutates `seen` (`path in seen or seen.add(path)`), and the next-but-one line then relies on `seen` having been fully populated by that comprehension to compute `unclaimed`. The dependency is invisible: reordering the two statements, or rewriting duplicates with a Counter, silently turns unclaimed into "every field" and the validator would reject every layout. This is the single guard that keeps the four config layers in sync, so it is worth making explicit.
evidence: duplicates = sorted({path for path in claimed if path in seen or seen.add(path)})
suggested_fix: Compute seen = set(claimed) explicitly, then derive duplicates from a collections.Counter(claimed); the two facts stop sharing hidden state.
verdict_notes: Confirmed at webui/launch_layout.py:1608: `duplicates = sorted({path for path in claimed if path in seen or seen.add(path)})` populates `seen` as a side effect, and `unclaimed = [path for path in paths if path not in seen]` two lines below depends on that mutation having happened. This is exactly the kind of implicit ordering dependency a senior reviewer flags: any innocuous refactor of the duplicates line (Counter, set(claimed)) silently makes `unclaimed` report every field, and this validator is the single guard keeping layout, config dataclasses and descriptions in sync. Cheap explicit fix (populate seen in a loop, or compute claimed_set separately).

title: Inference entry resolves runner classes through two dicts bridged by a throwaway string
description: InferenceEntry.RUNNERS maps RunType -> "ClassName" (lines 13-19) and _worker then builds a second local dict mapping the same "ClassName" strings back to the imported classes, so the lookup reads `runners[self.RUNNERS[self.run_type]]`. The intermediate string layer carries no information — the deferred import is already inside _worker, so the local dict could be keyed directly on RunType and RUNNERS deleted. The class attribute RUNNERS also has to be kept manually in sync with the local dict for the indirection to work. Related: __init__ annotates `run_type: str` (line 37) although every caller passes a RunType enum member.
suggested_fix: Key the local dict on RunType inside _worker, drop the RUNNERS string table, and fix the annotation to run_type: RunType.
verdict_notes: Confirmed: RUNNERS maps RunType -> class-name string, and _worker builds a second dict keyed on the same strings back to classes it has already imported directly, giving `runners[self.RUNNERS[self.run_type]]`. Unlike CONFIGS (which legitimately needs strings for getattr on the module), the string hop here carries no information and creates two tables that must be kept in sync by hand for lookups to work at all. The `run_type: str` annotation is also wrong; callers pass RunType members and RUNNERS/CONFIGS/DESCRIPTIONS are all keyed by the enum. Small, but a real needless-indirection cleanup with no behavioural risk.

title: Comparison/CV reports read checkpoint keys that best_model.pt never contains, so "epochs run" is always 0
description: `Checkpoint.save` writes `trainer.capture_state(epoch)` plus `best_val_loss`/`best_epoch`; `Trainer.capture_state` (tools/training/trainer.py:211-216) emits exactly `{epoch, params, x_axis}`. `train_losses`, `val_losses` and `global_step` only exist in the separate `last.pt` TrainerState blob (tools/training/checkpoint.py:151-165). `TrialCollector._read_checkpoint` opens `best_model.pt` and derives `n_train_epochs`/`n_val_epochs` from `train_losses`/`val_losses`, which are always absent, so both are always 0, and `global_step` is always None (dropped by the None filter at line 135, making it a dead entry in `_CHECKPOINT_KEYS`). The 0 propagates to every consumer: pipelines/shared/comparison/comparison_report.py:244, pipelines/cross_validation/cv_report.py:174 ("Epochs run" column) and pipelines/comparison/comparison_report.py:104, and it is averaged across seeds via `SeedRunAggregator.CHECKPOINT_KEYS` (line 44) and `FoldCollector.CHECKPOINT_KEYS` (pipelines/cross_validation/workers.py:19). The unit test that covers this (tests/benchmark/test_results.py:84-100) fabricates a checkpoint dict containing `train_losses`/`val_losses`/`global_step`, a schema no writer in the repo produces, which is why the drift was never caught.
evidence:
info["n_train_epochs"] = len(checkpoint.get("train_losses") or [])
        info["n_val_epochs"]   = len(checkpoint.get("val_losses") or [])
suggested_fix: Either read epoch counts from `last.pt` (TrainerState) / the tensorboard scalars, or add `train_losses`/`val_losses` lengths to `Trainer.capture_state`. Drop `global_step` from `_CHECKPOINT_KEYS`. Fix the test fixture to use the real `capture_state` payload.
verdict_notes:
I reproduced the claim from source and at runtime.

Writer side: `Checkpoint.save` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tools/training/checkpoint.py:42-50) writes `trainer.capture_state(epoch)` plus `best_val_loss` and `best_epoch`. `BaseTrainer.capture_state` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tools/training/trainer.py:211-216) returns exactly `{"epoch", "params", "x_axis"}`. `grep -rn "def capture_state"` over the whole repo returns only that one definition plus two test stubs — no trainer subclass (backbone, jepa, autoencoder_common, image/profile AE, tuning trials) overrides it, and nothing rewrites `best_model.pt` afterwards (`torch.save` sites: checkpoint.py:50/169 and trainer.py:372, the epoch snapshot, which writes only `{epoch, params}`). So `best_model.pt` on disk has exactly the keys `epoch, params, x_axis, best_val_loss, best_epoch`. `train_losses`/`val_losses`/`global_step` live only in the `last.pt` `TrainerState` blob (checkpoint.py:150-165).

Reader side: `TrialCollector._read_checkpoint` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/shared/comparison/trial_collection.py:121-135) opens `best_model.pt` and computes `n_train_epochs`/`n_val_epochs` from `checkpoint.get("train_losses"/"val_losses") or []`.

Runtime reproduction: I wrote a `best_model.pt` with exactly the real writer's key set into a fake run tree and ran `TrialCollector(...).collect()` in the Dune env. Result: `{'best_val_loss': 0.123, 'best_epoch': 7, 'epoch': 9, 'n_train_epochs': 0, 'n_val_epochs': 0}` — the two epoch counts are 0 and `global_step` is absent (dropped by the `is not None` filter at line 135, so that entry of `_CHECKPOINT_KEYS` at line 19 is indeed dead).

Propagation is as claimed: the always-0 `n_train_epochs` is rendered in /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/shared/comparison/comparison_report.py:244, /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/cross_validation/cv_report.py:174 and /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/comparison/comparison_report.py:104, and is averaged over seeds/folds via `SeedRunAggregator.CHECKPOINT_KEYS` (trial_collection.py:44) and `FoldCollector.CHECKPOINT_KEYS` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/cross_validation/workers.py:19) — averaging zeros yields zero.

The covering test /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tests/benchmark/test_results.py:84-99 fabricates a checkpoint dict containing `train_losses`/`val_losses`/`global_step`, a schema no writer in this repo produces, which is exactly why the drift went unnoticed. Note `pipelines/patch_sweep/report.py:66-79` reads the same file but only for `best_val_loss`/`best_epoch`, i.e. only keys that actually exist — consistent with the drift being local to `_read_checkpoint`.

This is not one of the listed known non-issues: it is a silent wrong value (0) rather than a loud break, which the project's no-legacy-fallback policy explicitly disfavours.
correction: All specifics in the claim check out (file, line 129, key sets, consumers, test). Two refinements: (1) the epoch count is recoverable without touching `last.pt` — `CompletionMarker.stamp` (tools/training/trainer.py:486-493) already records `epochs_completed`/`epochs_total` in the run's completion marker, and `record.run_summary` is already loaded by the collector, so the fix does not require reading `last.pt`. (2) Blast radius is confined to the report tables: `best_val_loss`, `best_epoch` and `epoch` are real values from the file, so model selection, training, inference and the leaderboard metrics are unaffected — only the "Epochs run"/"Epochs" column (and its seed/fold averages) is wrong. That argues for minor rather than major.

title: RunLoader recomputes n_gaussians from out_channels and ignores the persisted n_gaussians key
description: `save_run_summary` (pipelines/shared/config/run_metadata.py:87-100) persists an authoritative `n_gaussians` field, written correctly by the backbone pipeline (pipelines/backbone/training/pipeline.py:212) and by JEPA (pipelines/jepa/training/pipeline.py:259). No reader in the repo ever consumes it: the only loader that needs K derives it as `out_channels // 3` instead, and never cross-checks the two. That is exactly what turns the JEPA `out_channels = embedding_dim` write into a silent wrong result — for a JEPA run with a profile autoencoder of embedding_dim=16 the loader silently produces n_gaussians=5 / out_channels=15 while the correct K sits unread in the same JSON file — and it means any future divergence between the head width and K is undetectable. The `//3` also hard-codes params_per_gaussian, duplicating the constant already hard-coded at loader.py:128 and model_probe.py:154-159.
suggested_fix: Read `n_gaussians` from run_summary.json and raise loudly if `out_channels != params_per_gaussian * n_gaussians`; that single check converts the JEPA mismatch from a silent wrong result into a clear failure.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source.

1) The persisted key is genuinely unread. `save_run_summary` (pipelines/shared/config/run_metadata.py:87-101) writes `n_gaussians`, and it is written correctly by pipelines/backbone/training/pipeline.py:207-214 and pipelines/jepa/training/pipeline.py:259 (`gaussian_cfg.n_default_gaussians`). Grepping every reader of `run_summary.json` (pipelines/backbone/inference/loader.py:203-214, pipelines/{profile,image}_autoencoder/inference/loader.py, pipelines/unrolled/inference/loader.py, pipelines/shared/comparison/trial_collection.py:206, webui/run_leaderboard.py:94, scripts/rename_runs.py:147) shows nobody consumes the `n_gaussians` field. The hits at pipelines/backbone/inference/report.py:293/336/374/414 read `self.run_summary["n_gaussians"]` from the in-memory dict built by ReportPayloadBuilder.run_summary (report.py:15-33) out of `run.n_gaussians`, i.e. from the derived value, not from the JSON. scripts/rename_runs.py:180 uses `trainer["gaussian"]["n_default_gaussians"]` instead. tests/backbone_inference/test_pipeline_e2e.py:103 even writes a run_summary.json with no `n_gaussians` key at all and the loader is fine with it — proof the key is not on the read path.

2) The derivation is inconsistent with the rest of the repo and with data already in hand. `RunLoader.load` parses `dataset_creation_config.json` into a DatasetConfig that already carries the authoritative `n_gaussians` (loader.py:98, written by pipelines/backbone/dataset/pipeline.py:211 `dataset_config.n_gaussians = gaussian_cfg.n_default_gaussians`), then ignores it in favour of `out_channels // 3` (loader.py:214). The unrolled loader does the opposite and correct thing: pipelines/unrolled/inference/loader.py:153 uses `dataset_config.n_gaussians`. So the backbone loader has two authoritative sources of K in scope and cross-checks neither.
