3) The JEPA failure is real and on a live path. `InferenceComponentsResolver.for_run` (pipelines/shared/inference/inference_components.py) routes any run with a profile-AE config plus a backbone config to JEPA_INFERENCE_COMPONENTS -> JepaRunLoader, reached from main/inference/infer_backbone.py via BackboneInferenceRunner. JepaRunLoader overrides `_build_model` (jepa/inference/loader.py:39-53) so the network is built correctly from `ae_cfg.embedding_dim`, but it does NOT override `load`, so `run.n_gaussians = embedding_dim // 3`. That value is then used as the real K in pipelines/jepa/inference/predictor.py:14 (`gt_params_b[:, :n_K*3]` reshaped to `(B, n_K, 3, H, W)` and reconstructed into the GT curves that every metric is scored against) and in pipelines/jepa/inference/embedding.py:22 (same for the embedding/cosine/decode/chain metrics), and it is also passed to PatchDataset at loader.py:228-234.

Concrete inputs: profile AE `embedding_dim=12`, dataset extracted with k_max=5 (so training used K=5, GT stack has 15 channels). Loader computes n_gaussians = 12//3 = 4. PatchDataset's guard (pipelines/backbone/dataset/datasets.py:66-70) only fires when the derived K exceeds what the dataset provides, so 4 <= 5 passes silently. Every JEPA GT reference curve is then reconstructed from only the first 4 of the 5 Gaussians, so pixel MSE/MAE/R2/cosine, SSIM, elevation metrics and all embedding metrics are computed against a truncated ground truth — a silently wrong result, with `n_gaussians: 5` sitting unread in the same meta directory (both in run_summary.json and dataset_creation_config.json).

4) The `//3` also hard-codes params_per_gaussian, which exists as a real config field (configuration/sar/gaussian_config.py:13) and is duplicated as the literal 3 at loader.py:128 and webui/model_probe.py:151-159.

Tests: tests/jepa/test_inference.py never exercises `JepaRunLoader.load` — it builds fake runs with `n_gaussians` injected by hand (build_fake_run, line 176-209), so nothing pins the derivation. No test asserts the persisted `n_gaussians` is read back.
correction:
The mechanism is right but the "silent" characterisation is only half the story, and the example numbers are off for the project defaults. Two regimes, split by the profile AE embedding width vs. the extraction k_max:
- embedding_dim//3 < k_max (e.g. embedding_dim=12, k_max=5 -> K=4): silent, as the auditor describes — truncated GT reference, wrong metrics, no error.
- embedding_dim//3 > k_max (this is the DEFAULT case: ProfileAutoencoderConfig.embedding_dim = 24 in configuration/architectures/profile_autoencoder.py:12, k_max typically 5 -> K=8): PatchDataset (pipelines/backbone/dataset/datasets.py:66-70) raises loudly, "Configured n_gaussians=8 indexes ground-truth parameter channel 23 but the dataset provides only 15 (5 Gaussians). Set n_gaussians to match the parameter extraction used for this dataset." That message is actively misleading, since at inference K is not user-settable — it is derived from a width that has nothing to do with K.
The auditor's example (embedding_dim=16 -> K=5) happens to be the one case where the derived value coincides with the usual k_max=5 and no harm occurs.
Also worth noting in the fix: JepaParamRunLoader (image-AE-only JEPA) is unaffected because its run_summary out_channels is 3*K, and the plain backbone/dual loaders are unaffected for the same reason; only the profile-AE JEPA branch breaks. The fix is to read `run_summary["n_gaussians"]` (or `dataset_config.n_gaussians`) as authoritative and assert `out_channels == params_per_gaussian * n_gaussians` only on the param-space loaders.
Line reference is correct (pipelines/backbone/inference/loader.py:214).

title: Leaderboard config diff silently omits the architecture for dual, unrolled and autoencoder runs
description: `CONFIG_FILES` hard-codes `meta/model_config.json`, the backbone-only artifact name. The dual family writes `meta/dual_model_config.json` (pipelines/dual/training/pipeline.py:53 overriding `MODEL_CONFIG_IO`), unrolled writes `meta/unrolled_model_config.json` (pipelines/unrolled/training/pipeline.py:189), and the autoencoders write `profile_autoencoder_config.json` / `image_autoencoder_config.json` — all enumerated in `RunArtifacts` (pipelines/shared/inference/run_classifier.py:14-19). `_run_config` then does a bare `continue` on the missing file, so comparing two dual runs in the webui diff panel yields identical, architecture-free config sets: exactly the axis (`params_backbone` / `existence_backbone` / feature widths) the user selected the runs to compare. Unrolled runs additionally have no `run_summary.json` at all (their pipeline never calls `TrainingRunMetadata`), so the `summary.*` half disappears too, again silently.
suggested_fix: Iterate over all names in `RunArtifacts` (labelling each) instead of the single backbone filename, and surface a per-run note when none of the model-config artifacts is present rather than silently skipping.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source, but only for the dual family; the unrolled/autoencoder half of the claim does not hold.

CONFIRMED mechanism (dual):
- /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/webui/run_leaderboard.py:93-97 hard-codes CONFIG_FILES = (summary -> meta/run_summary.json, trainer -> docs/trainer_config.json, model -> meta/model_config.json).
- /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/pipelines/dual/training/pipeline.py:53 sets MODEL_CONFIG_IO = DualModelConfigIO; config_persistence.py:136-137 gives it FILENAME = RunArtifacts.DUAL_CONFIG = "dual_model_config.json". backbone/training/pipeline.py:205 saves through that IO into run/meta, so a dual run has meta/dual_model_config.json and NO meta/model_config.json — tests/dual_inference/test_pipeline_e2e.py:106 asserts exactly that (`assert not (run_directory / "meta" / "model_config.json").exists()`).
- _run_config (run_leaderboard.py:353-365) does a bare `continue` when the file is absent, so the whole `model.*` half of the diff vanishes with no error and no note. webui/static/js/leaderboard.js:788-800 renders only what the backend returned ("Config differences N of M"), so the omission is invisible in the UI.
- Concrete failure: two dual runs that differ only in params_backbone / existence_backbone / params_features / existence_features / trunk channel routing produce config sets containing only trainer.* and summary.* keys. Everything architectural is gone; the only differing rows are per-run path noise (run_metadata.py:41 sets trainer_config.io.logdir to the run directory, and save_run_summary writes run_directory/git_commit), so the panel shows a couple of meaningless path diffs and zero architecture rows — precisely the axis the user selected the two dual runs to compare.

REFUTED sub-claims:
- Unrolled and autoencoder runs never reach the leaderboard at all. Their inference output lives at run/inference/<family>/<stamp>/ (pipelines/shared/inference/metadata.py:13, SUBDIR="unrolled"/"profile_ae"/"image_ae"), while the leaderboard scans root.rglob("inference/*/metrics.json") (run_leaderboard.py:114) and the unit path globs "seed*/inference/*/metrics.json" (line 321). I verified with a filesystem repro that inference/unrolled/<stamp>/metrics.json is not matched. So the "unrolled also loses run_summary.json" consequence is unreachable through this panel (an unrolled dir passed to _side would fall into _unit_side and error out with "no seeded inference results").
- Dual inference does use the flat backbone layout (pipelines/dual/inference/pipeline.py reuses backbone InferenceComponents; backbone/inference/run_metadata_paths.py:15 base = run/inference), which is why dual runs do appear and are the real victim.
- "Identical config sets" is slightly too strong: io.logdir / summary.run_directory always differ, so the panel will not print "The resolved configs are identical"; it prints a diff made purely of paths and possibly git_commit.

Mitigating context (not enough to refute): dual run names carry the trunk tag dual_<params>.<existence> (run_naming.py:39-43) and the diff column headers are the run tags, so the two backbone choices remain visible by name. What is silently lost is feature widths, channel counts, input-group routing and every other DualResUNetConfig field.

Not a KNOWN NON-ISSUE: this is a silent skip of a missing artifact, which project policy explicitly counts as a finding rather than an accepted design.
correction: Scope is dual runs only. Unrolled and autoencoder runs are never listed or diffable by the leaderboard in the first place (their inference results sit one directory deeper, under inference/<family>/<stamp>/, which neither run_leaderboard.py:114 nor :321 matches), so the "unrolled also loses run_summary.json" part is unreachable. Also, the diff is not literally "identical": trainer.io.logdir (set to the run directory in pipelines/shared/config/run_metadata.py:41) and summary.run_directory/git_commit always differ, so the user sees a config diff made entirely of path noise with no architecture rows. Fix is to make CONFIG_FILES resolve the model config via RunClassifier/RunArtifacts (pipelines/shared/inference/run_classifier.py:14-19) instead of hard-coding the backbone filename, and to surface a skipped/missing-artifact note instead of `continue`.

title: Missing-training-directory guard is unreachable because the sources are loaded first
description: `collect()` calls `_aggregate_sources()` before checking `self.training_dir.is_dir()`. `_aggregate_sources` unconditionally does `FileIO.load_json(self.pipeline_dir / "training_results.json")` (line 163), which raises `FileNotFoundError` in exactly the situation the guard two lines below is meant to report gracefully (a run root with no training stage). The friendly `"No training directory found at: ..."` branch at lines 197-198 is therefore dead for the common case, and the user gets a raw traceback instead.
suggested_fix: Move the `training_dir.is_dir()` check (and ideally an explicit check for `pipeline/training_results.json`) above the `_aggregate_sources()` call.
verdict_notes: The ordering defect is real and I reproduced it by execution. In pipelines/shared/comparison/trial_collection.py, collect() (line 194) calls _aggregate_sources() before the training_dir guard (lines 196-198). _aggregate_sources (line 163) unconditionally does FileIO.load_json(pipeline_dir/"training_results.json"), and FileIO.load_json (tools/data/io.py:34-36) is a bare open(), so a missing file raises FileNotFoundError. Running TrialCollector(run_dir=<dir with only pipeline/>).collect() in the Dune env raised "FileNotFoundError [Errno 2] ... /pipeline/training_results.json" instead of logging "No training directory found at: ..." and returning []. The reachable user-facing path is main/analysis/compare_runs.py with an explicit --run-tag (its auto-resolution filters on (d/"training").is_dir(), so only the explicit tag exposes it); BenchmarkSeedCollector (pipelines/benchmark/results.py:9) and FoldCollector (pipelines/cross_validation/workers.py:18) inherit the same ordering. However the auditor overstates the impact: the guard is NOT dead. tests/benchmark/test_results.py:40 (test_collector_returns_empty_without_training_dir) writes pipeline/training_results.json=[] with no training/ dir and asserts collect()==[], and that state occurs for real when QueuedTrainingStage.run has an empty item list (tools/orchestration/stages.py writes the results file unconditionally, while training/ is only created when a job runs). Additionally the raw FileNotFoundError names the missing path and matches the project's break-loudly policy, which sister code relies on deliberately (pipelines/patch_sweep/report.py:52 with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError, match="training_results.json") at tests/patch_sweep/test_report.py:78). Net: a genuine but cosmetic cold-path inconsistency, not a dead branch.
correction: The guard is not dead code: it is covered by tests/benchmark/test_results.py:40 and is reached whenever pipeline/training_results.json exists but training/ does not (e.g. a training stage with an empty item list, which writes the results file without ever creating training/). What is actually true is narrower: when the results file itself is also absent (a run root with no pipeline stage at all, reachable via `main/analysis/compare_runs.py --run-tag <tag>`), the user gets a FileNotFoundError traceback naming .../pipeline/training_results.json rather than the friendly logged message. The same ordering exists in FoldCollector._aggregate_sources (pipelines/cross_validation/workers.py:28). Impact is UX-only on a cold path, and the raw error is itself loud and path-naming, consistent with the project's no-silent-fallback policy; the fix is simply to move the is_dir() guard above line 194.

title: Persisted configs silently fall back to today's dataclass defaults for keys absent from the file
description: `load_resolved` raises loudly on unknown keys (line 244) but silently skips keys that the stored file does not contain, leaving the freshly-constructed dataclass default in place. `ConfigIO.load` in pipelines/shared/config/config_persistence.py:63-73 is asymmetric in the same way: it rejects persisted fields the dataclass no longer has, but any dataclass field missing from the payload keeps the current default. Concretely, `pipelines/unrolled/inference/loader.py:50` rebuilds `UnrolledEntryConfig()` from `resolved_entry_config.json` and then uses `entry.geometry.height_axis_convention` at line 124 to pick the kz sign convention and `entry.curve_loss` / `entry.power_floor` at lines 156-157; a run persisted before any of those fields existed is scored under today's defaults with no warning, which contradicts the project's break-loudly policy for old artifacts.
suggested_fix: Make the missing-key branch loud (or at least logged): raise unless the field is on an explicit optional/back-compat allowlist, mirroring the unknown-key check.
verdict_notes:
Mechanism reproduced from source. `ConfigCli.load_resolved` (/home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/tools/runtime/config_cli.py:234-262) raises `KeyError` for any persisted key the dataclass no longer has (line 242-244), but the restore loop at line 246-248 does `if leaf not in mapping: continue`, so every dataclass leaf absent from the stored JSON silently keeps the freshly-constructed default. `ConfigIO.load` (pipelines/shared/config/config_persistence.py:65-73) is asymmetric in exactly the same way: it iterates `payload["config"]` and raises on unknown fields, so fields the payload lacks keep the registry default.

I checked the two defences that would refute this. (1) Serialization is not lossy: `to_mapping` (config_cli.py:208-219) drops leaves of unsupported types, which would make a strict "all leaves present" check impossible — but I instantiated every constructible dataclass under configuration/ and compared `_leaves` against `to_mapping`; zero leaves are dropped for any of them (UnrolledEntryConfig: 87 leaves, 87 keys). So the skip is never needed for a same-version round trip. (2) No caller needs partial payloads: every `load_resolved`/`load_worker_config` caller (main/experiments/tune.py:49,73, main/inference/_inference_entry.py:60, main/experiments/{benchmark,cross_validate,sweep_patches}.py) reads a file written by the same config type, normally by the same process generation. The only cross-version reader is the unrolled inference loader. No run-artifact version guard exists in RunLoader either.

Reachability is real, but not via the fields the auditor names — see correction. The tolerant load is what CLAUDE.md forbids ("no tolerant `.get(...)` loads", break loudly and regenerate), and the opposite direction in the very same function already raises, so the asymmetry reads as an oversight rather than a stance. Tests (tests/training_runtime/test_config_cli.py:177-218) cover round trip, type restoration, missing file and unknown key — nothing encodes intent for the missing-key case either way.
correction:
The mechanism is confirmed, but the concrete example is not reachable. `docs/resolved_entry_config.json` for unrolled runs was first written by commit 6f2af85 (2026-07-06, "Add gamma_net unrolled physics network..."), the same commit that introduced `curve_loss`, `power_floor` and `measurement_noise_std` in configuration/training/unrolled.py; `geometry.height_axis_convention` predates it (2026-07-03). No unrolled resolved_entry_config.json can therefore lack any of the three keys read at pipelines/unrolled/inference/loader.py:124,156-157, so "a run persisted before any of those fields existed" cannot exist.

Reachable instances instead: `overfit_check.*` joined UnrolledEntryConfig in 4ee2a19 (2026-07-14) and `pretrain.*` in 73b4798 (2026-07-20), so any unrolled run trained between 07-06 and those dates has a resolved_entry_config.json missing those leaves, and `load_resolved` fills today's defaults with no warning. The behaviourally sharper instance is `main/experiments/tune.py:73` (`--resume`): resuming a study started before a `TuningEntryConfig` field was added silently continues under the new default rather than the value the run was launched with. The `ConfigIO.load` half is the higher-risk one long-term: a backbone/unrolled/dual config field added after a checkpoint was trained keeps its new default, and if it does not change parameter shapes the state_dict still loads cleanly, so the model is rebuilt with different behaviour and no error.

Suggested fix is symmetric: after the unknown-key check, also collect `known - mapping.keys()` and raise, pointing at retraining/backfill (same treatment as ProfileDatasetConfigIO.load, which already directs old runs to scripts/backfill_profile_dataset_config.py).

title: Rename and JSON patch are two non-atomic phases; a partial apply can never be repaired by re-running
description: `_rename_runs` performs `source.rename(target)` and only then patches the run's own `meta/run_summary.json`, `docs/trainer_config.json` and `docs/resolved_entry_config.json`; the cross-run `batch_train_logs/train_scheduler_results.json` and `pipeline/{training,inference}_results.json` are patched later still, in `_process_runs` (lines 127-131), after the whole rename loop. Any interruption between the two phases — a Ctrl-C, a `FileExistsError` raised at line 302 for run N after runs 1..N-1 were already renamed, or a `ValueError` from `RunNaming.loss_tag` on a legacy trainer_config whose loss flags no longer map — leaves the directory renamed and the JSON un-patched. Re-running the script does not fix it: `_plan_run` recognises the already-renamed directory (line 186 `if name == new_tag ...`) and returns None, so the run drops out of the mapping, `_process_runs` hits `if not mapping: ... return` at line 118-120 and returns before ever reaching `_patch_file`. Concretely, for `runs/context/<dual_local_cnn-...>_ctx-cnn29/`, `meta/run_summary.json` keeps `"run_directory": ".../<dual_resunet-...>_ctx-cnn29"` forever, and `runs/context/batch_train_logs/train_scheduler_results.json` keeps the old `name` entries for every run renamed before the abort — even though `tests/dual_training/test_rename_runs.py:62-64` asserts that this patch is part of the contract. There is no --repair path and no backup.
suggested_fix: Do not gate the JSON patch on the run being renamed in this invocation. Plan the mapping, then patch metadata that still contains a stale name regardless of whether the directory move happened in this run (i.e. detect old names inside run_summary/trainer_config/scheduler results and repair them), and patch the scheduler/result files per-parent before, not after, the rename loop so an aborted loop leaves a repairable state.
verdict_notes: The core defect reproduces from source. scripts/rename_runs.py:_process_runs runs two non-atomic phases: _rename_runs (line 297) does source.rename(target) at 308 and patches only the run-internal PATCH_FILES at 309-311, while the cross-run batch_train_logs/train_scheduler_results.json and pipeline/{training,inference}_results.json are patched only after the entire loop, at lines 127-131. A Ctrl-C, an OS error, or the FileExistsError raised at line 302 for run N after runs 1..N-1 were already renamed leaves the directories renamed and those cross-run JSONs holding old names. Re-running provably cannot repair it: _plan_run line 186 skips an already-renamed directory ("already in the new naming") and returns None, so it never re-enters mapping; with every run already renamed, mapping is empty and line 118-120 returns before either _patch_file call. There is no --repair path, no backup, and _patch_file (319-327) is itself a bare read_text/write_text with no temp-and-rename. Grepping tests/ for SCHEDULER_FILE, RESULT_FILES, _patch_file and batch_train_logs shows the cross-run patch has zero test coverage. However several of the auditor's supporting details are wrong, and the severity is badly inflated (see correction).
correction: Three mechanism errors and a severity error. (1) The claimed "ValueError from RunNaming.loss_tag" trigger is impossible: line 117 completes _plan for every run in the parent group before the first rename at line 308, so a naming failure (run_naming.py:19, "Cannot name a run from a loss config with no enabled loss terms") always aborts strictly pre-rename; likewise _process_root finishes each parent group completely before the next. Only Ctrl-C/OS-error/FileExistsError inside the loop can produce partial state. (2) The concrete example is wrong for the FileExistsError trigger: run N is never renamed (target.exists() is checked before rename), and runs 1..N-1 had their in-run meta/run_summary.json patched in the same loop iteration. That file goes permanently stale only if the process dies in the narrow window between lines 308 and 311. The durable unrepairable damage is confined to the cross-run files. (3) tests/dual_training/test_rename_runs.py:62-64 does not encode the cross-run contract cited — it asserts the in-run PATCH_FILES patch applied inside the rename loop; the cross-run patch is untested. (4) Severity: scripts/rename_runs.py is a manual one-shot migration utility, dry-run by default, operating on gitignored run artifacts — a cold path. train_scheduler_results.json is written by pipelines/backbone/training/launcher.py:146 and read by no code in the repo. pipeline/training_results.json is read by pipelines/shared/comparison/trial_collection.py:163 and pipelines/cross_validation/workers.py:28 through a tolerant lookup (trial_collection.py:207: training_results[name] if name in training_results else {}), so a stale key yields an empty training_result field in a report, not a crash or a wrong metric. Repair is a hand-edit of one JSON. Minor, not critical.

title: The plan is never checked for two runs mapping to the same new name; the dry run reports both as fine and the apply aborts mid-loop
description: `_plan` accumulates `mapping[run_dir.name] = new_name` with no check that two different source directories produced the same `new_name`. Collisions are reachable because the new naming drops information the legacy names carried: `LegacyNaming.presence_letters` (line 48) emits an `F` letter for `amp_focal_gamma > 0` that the live `RunNaming.presence_tag` no longer emits, and `LegacyNaming.underscore_stem`/`run_prefix` carry no K, no augmentation and no weights at all — so a flagless-era run and a presence-era run of the same configuration sitting in the same `runs/trials/` parent both reconstruct to one `new_tag`. The only guard is `if target.exists()` inside the rename loop (line 301), which is evaluated lazily: in dry run neither target exists yet, so `--apply`-less output shows both renames as clean; under `--apply` the first `source.rename(target)` succeeds and the second raises `FileExistsError`, dropping the tree into exactly the unrepairable half-migrated state described in the previous finding.
evidence:
if new_name is not None:
                mapping[run_dir.name] = new_name
suggested_fix: After building the mapping, assert that `len(set(mapping.values())) == len(mapping)` and that no target already exists on disk, raising with both source names before any rename is attempted, so the dry run surfaces the collision.
verdict_notes:
I reproduced the failure from source rather than trusting the claim.

Mechanism, verified in /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/scripts/rename_runs.py:
- `_plan` (line 136-143) builds `mapping[run_dir.name] = new_name` with no uniqueness check on the values. Old names are unique by construction (they are directory names in one parent), so the dict never collapses; two entries can carry the same value.
- `_plan_run` reconstructs `new_tag = RunNaming.tag(...)` purely from persisted metadata, and it accepts four different legacy name generations (`flagless_tag`, `presence_tag`, `underscore_tag`, `run_prefix`, line 199). Those generations encode different subsets of the config, so two directories of the *same* configuration recorded in different naming eras have different names on disk but reconstruct to one identical `new_tag`.
- The only guard is `if target.exists()` in `_rename_runs` (line 301), evaluated lazily inside the loop, so it cannot see a collision between two planned targets that do not exist yet.

Concrete reproduction (script at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-bard/bc79d8b1-4642-451c-ada3-6efc2657779a/scratchpad/verif/collide.py, run in the Dune env against the real repo). Two `resunet`/`conv`/hungarian/K=5/hv/param_l1_1 runs with `use_active_normalization=True` in one parent:
  - flagless-era dir: `resunet-conv-hungarian-K_5-hv-param_l1_1`
  - presence-era dir: `resunet-conv-K_5-hv-A-param_l1_1`
  - both plan to: `resunet-conv-hungarian-K_5-hv-A-param_l1_1`
Dry run printed both renames as clean, with no warning. `--apply` renamed the presence-era dir, patched its `meta/run_summary.json`, then raised `FileExistsError: ... already exists; refusing to overwrite` on the second, aborting the whole script (the exception propagates out of `_rename_runs` -> `_process_runs` -> `run`, so no further parents are processed and `_patch_file` on `train_scheduler_results.json` / pipeline result files never runs). Post-apply directory listing showed one renamed dir and one untouched dir with mutually inconsistent internal metadata.

The auditor's secondary evidence also checks out: `LegacyNaming.presence_letters` (line 48) emits `F` for `amp_focal_gamma > 0`, while the live `RunNaming.presence_tag` (pipelines/shared/training/run_naming.py:37-39) emits only `A`/`B` — and tests/pipelines_shared/test_run_naming.py:50 asserts exactly that (`presence_tag(_loss(amp_focal_gamma=2.0)) == "none"`), so the drop is deliberate and the collision it enables is real. The dual branch has the same hole: `_plan_dual_run` old_tags (line 249) accept both the `extras=(input_tag,)` and the no-extras form, so an input-tagged and an untagged dual run of one config also converge on one `new_tag`.

Test coverage: tests/dual_training/test_rename_runs.py is the only test file for this script (7 tests, dual-only) and contains no collision case, so nothing encodes an intended behaviour that would contradict the finding. This is not one of the known non-issues (it is not a legacy-fallback question; the migration is meant to succeed, and it does not fail before mutating state).
correction: Two details in the write-up are off. (1) "Unrepairable half-migrated state" is overstated: the abort is loud, nothing is overwritten or deleted, and recovery is renaming the one moved directory back and undoing the `_boundary_replace` patches in its `meta/run_summary.json`, `docs/trainer_config.json`, `docs/resolved_entry_config.json` — tedious but bounded. (2) The `underscore_stem`/`run_prefix` reasoning as phrased ("carry no K, no augmentation and no weights") does not by itself create the collision, because a legacy suffix is preserved verbatim (`f"{new_tag}{name[len(old_tag):]}"`, line 205) and two runs sharing a legacy tag cannot share a directory name. The real and reproducible collision path is cross-generation: two directories written under different naming eras (flagless vs presence, or `run_<model>` vs underscore, or dual with vs without the input tag) for the same configuration. Line reference 141 is correct for the missing check; line 301 is correct for the lazy guard. Severity is closer to minor than major: this is a cold, manually invoked one-shot migration script, it fails loudly rather than silently corrupting, and the collision requires two same-config runs from different naming eras under one parent.

title: Only train_scheduler_results.json is patched; the seed-sweep and inference scheduler result files keep the old run names
description: `PATCH_FILES` and `SCHEDULER_FILE` cover `meta/run_summary.json`, `docs/trainer_config.json`, `docs/resolved_entry_config.json` and `batch_train_logs/train_scheduler_results.json`. Three sibling artifacts written next to that last one are missed: `pipelines/shared/training/seed_sweep.py:76-77` writes `<group>/batch_train_logs/seed_sweep_results.json` and `seed_sweep_infer_results.json` whose `name` entries are `"<group_tag>/seed<N>"`, and `pipelines/backbone/training/launcher.py:147` writes `<parent>/batch_train_logs/infer_scheduler_results.json`. Note also that the seed-sweep files live *inside* the renamed group directory, whereas `_process_runs` only looks at `parent / SCHEDULER_FILE`, so they are not reachable at all. After renaming `runs/context/<old_tag>` these files still name the old directory; nothing currently reads them, so the damage is limited to a misleading audit trail.
suggested_fix: Make the scheduler-results patch a glob over `batch_train_logs/*_results.json` at both `parent` and inside each renamed group directory, rather than one hardcoded filename at one location.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source. rename_runs.py patches PATCH_FILES (meta/run_summary.json, docs/trainer_config.json, docs/resolved_entry_config.json) inside each renamed run dir plus its seed children (_rename_runs, lines 309-311), and parent/batch_train_logs/train_scheduler_results.json (_process_runs, line 127), plus pipeline/{training,inference}_results.json for benchmark collections (lines 129-131).

Miss 1 (infer_scheduler_results.json): pipelines/backbone/training/launcher.py:145-147 sets log_dir = runs_root/"batch_train_logs" and writes BOTH train_scheduler_results.json (line 270) and infer_scheduler_results.json (line 239) there, via ExperimentStage._write_results with names = the same unit run names ("<base>" or "<base>/seed<N>", built by _seed_units/SeedSet.run_name). The infer file therefore contains the identical run-name strings, sits in the exact directory rename_runs already opens, and is simply not in the patch set. Concrete failure: after `scripts/rename_runs.py runs/context --apply` on a run launched with infer_at_end, runs/context/batch_train_logs/train_scheduler_results.json has the new names while runs/context/batch_train_logs/infer_scheduler_results.json still names the old, now non-existent directories.

Miss 2 (seed_sweep_results.json / seed_sweep_infer_results.json): pipelines/shared/training/seed_sweep.py:75-77 puts them under run_dir/"batch_train_logs", where run_dir = Path(config.logdir)/runner_factory(probe)._resolve_run_name() and TrainingRunMetadata.resolve_name (pipelines/shared/config/run_metadata.py:62-63) returns the supplied run_name verbatim — so the sweep directory name IS the tag rename_runs renames. Their "name" entries are "<base>/seed<N>" (SeedSet.run_name, line 20; asserted verbatim by tests/pipelines_shared/test_seed_sweep.py:154 -> ["exp/seed3","exp/seed0","exp/seed17"]). _discover registers such a directory (it has seed children) under groups[directory.parent], so _process_runs only inspects <logdir>/batch_train_logs/train_scheduler_results.json — one level above where these files live. They are structurally unreachable by the current code, exactly as the claim states.

Impact: `grep -rn "batch_train_logs"` over .py/.js/.json outside tests/ returns only the two writers and rename_runs.py; grep for the four filenames returns writers + rename_runs only. Nothing reads them, so the consequence is a misleading/stale audit trail, not a functional break — "minor" is the right severity. This is not the "no legacy fallbacks" non-issue (no shim involved) nor any other listed deliberate quirk; the script's existing patching of the train scheduler file and the benchmark pipeline result files shows the intent is to keep result files consistent with renames, and _boundary_replace's (?<![A-Za-z0-9_]) lookbehind already handles "<old>/seedN" correctly, so extending the patch set is mechanically trivial.
correction: Line number is off: PATCH_FILES is line 71, but the quoted SCHEDULER_FILE evidence is scripts/rename_runs.py line 74; the patching sites are _process_runs line 127 and _rename_runs lines 309-311. Mechanism otherwise accurate, with one clarification: the two misses differ in kind. infer_scheduler_results.json (launcher.py:147) sits in the very directory rename_runs already opens and is a pure omission from the patch set — a one-line fix. The two seed-sweep files (seed_sweep.py:76-77) live inside the renamed group directory, one level below anything _process_runs looks at, so covering them needs the patch to run on the renamed target (like PATCH_FILES) rather than on parent. Also worth noting the launcher's infer file is only written when infer_at_end is set (launcher.py:239 under _run_inference_pass), and the seed-sweep infer file likewise (seed_sweep.py:135), so the stale-name condition only arises for batched-inference runs.

title: Only script in scripts/ that uses print() instead of the shared Logger
description: The four summary lines go to stdout via `print`, while every other script in this directory routes output through `tools.monitoring.logger.Logger` — the repo rule is to always use `Logger`, never `print`. The practical consequence is that the drift summary (how many curated repomap nodes point at deleted files, how many modules no diagram covers) leaves no log file behind, so a drift check run before editing `webui/repomap_data.json` cannot be diffed against a later one.
suggested_fix: Instantiate `Logger(log_dir=str(REPO_ROOT / "logs"), name="derive_repomap_skeleton")` and emit the four lines through it, matching the other six scripts.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. /home/bard/Bard/code/DLR-TomoSAR/scripts/derive_repomap_skeleton.py lines 28-31 emit four bare print() calls. All six sibling scripts in scripts/ (backfill_completion_markers.py, backfill_profile_dataset_config.py, backfill_track_parameters.py, fix_config_names.py, generate_state_dict_baseline.py, rename_runs.py) import tools.monitoring.logger.Logger and route every message through it; none contains a print(). tools/monitoring/logger.py:120 Logger.__init__ attaches a logging.FileHandler writing logs/<name>.log, so the siblings persist their output and this script does not. Repo-wide the only other print() sites are tools/runtime/config_cli.py (--help text), tools/runtime/detacher.py (notice emitted before a logger exists) and webui/web_logger.py (intentional stdout streaming into the web console) — none of which is this situation. webui/repomap_derive.py does no logging of its own, so the script is the only reporting surface. This is a straight violation of the standing "always use Logger, never print" rule, not one of the listed known non-issues.
correction: The stated practical consequence is overstated and should be dropped: lines 22 and 26 write logs/repomap/derived_skeleton.json and logs/repomap/drift.json, so the full drift payload (missing_files, uncovered_modules) is persisted on disk and IS diffable between a before-edit and after-edit run. What is lost is only the four-line console summary, which leaves no log file. The defect is the convention break itself, not data loss. Worth adding to the finding: the same file is also the only script in scripts/ that puts its logic in a free main() function instead of a class with an orchestrator method, so it breaks both halves of the same house style at once. Severity minor is correct.

title: Every tuning worker registers BestConfigWriter as an Optuna callback, so N processes race on one fixed .tmp path
description: BestConfigWriter is passed as a per-trial callback to study.optimize() in Tuner.run (line 151), AeTuner.run (line 207) and JepaTuner.run (line 268). TuningScheduler._dispatch_workers launches one worker per GPU for the SAME model, and every worker builds its writer at the identical path Path(log_dir)/'best_config.json' (tuners.py:101, 175, 231 — log_dir is run_dir/model_name in workers.py:82/93/103/116, which is exactly the path the scheduler also writes at pipeline.py:160). FileIO.save_json(..., atomic=True) writes to a FIXED sidecar name `path.with_name(path.name + '.tmp')` (tools/data/io.py:24) and then os.replace()s it. With 4 workers finishing trials of the same model, two writers can open the same best_config.json.tmp concurrently: the second open() truncates the first writer's buffer, and whichever process calls os.replace() second raises FileNotFoundError because the source was already renamed away. That exception propagates out of the Optuna callback, out of study.optimize(), and kills the worker mid-study; in the interleaved case the file that does get published is truncated/garbled JSON. The atomic=True flag makes the write atomic against readers, not against other writers of the same path.
suggested_fix: Give each writer a unique temp name (e.g. include os.getpid() in the suffix) in FileIO.save_json, or stop registering BestConfigWriter as a per-worker callback and let only the scheduler write best_config.json after the queue drains (it already does so at pipeline.py:160-161).
verdict_notes:
Every cited line checks out and the failure is reproducible.

1. Concurrency is real. `TuningScheduler._tune_model` (pipelines/tuning/pipeline.py:157-158) splits the remaining trials across `len(self.config.gpus)` workers for ONE model and calls `_dispatch_workers(model_name, counts)`, which builds one `GpuJob` per worker and hands them all to `GpuQueue.run` (pipeline.py:85-94). `GpuQueue.run` (tools/orchestration/gpu_queue.py:348-374) pops jobs while GPUs are free and `subprocess.Popen`s each one, so N worker processes for the same model run simultaneously.

2. All N workers target the identical path. `TuningWorker.run_worker` builds the tuner with `log_dir = str(self.run_dir / model_name)` (workers.py:82/93/103/116 — the per-GPU suffix is only on the Logger dir, line 137, not on the tuner log_dir), and each tuner constructs `BestConfigWriter(..., Path(log_dir) / "best_config.json")` (tuners.py:101, 175, 231). Same path in every worker, and the same path the scheduler writes at pipeline.py:160.

3. The writer runs per trial in every worker: `study.optimize(..., callbacks=[self.best_writer])` (tuners.py:151, 207, 268), and `__call__` -> `write` -> `FileIO.save_json(payload, self.path, indent=2, atomic=True)` (tuners.py:68).

4. `FileIO.save_json` uses a FIXED sidecar `path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")` and `os.replace` (tools/data/io.py:24-29) — no pid/uuid/lock. Atomic against readers, not against a second writer of the same path.

5. Reproduced both failure modes with the real `FileIO` (optuna 4.8.0 env Dune): writer A opens the shared `.tmp`, writer B completes its full write+replace, A's buffered flush then lands inside the already-published inode giving garbled JSON (`{"model": "unet", "trial": 1}": 2\n}`), and A's `os.replace` raises `FileNotFoundError: ... best_config.json.tmp -> best_config.json`.

6. The exception does propagate and kill the worker: optuna/study/_optimize.py:173-177 invokes callbacks in the optimize loop outside any try/except (`catch` only wraps `_run_trial`), so it escapes `study.optimize`, the worker exits non-zero, `GpuQueue._reap` records FAILED and the scheduler records PARTIAL.

Mitigating facts that bear on severity, not on correctness: the race window is the few hundred microseconds of a tiny JSON write per finished trial, against trials that last minutes to hours, so collisions are rare; completed trials live in the shared SQLite study and survive a worker death; nothing reads `best_config.json` during the run (repo-wide grep finds only the writers, tests, repomap_data.json and the webui animation, no loader), and the scheduler rewrites it single-writer from the study at pipeline.py:160-161, so a transiently corrupt file self-heals. Damage when it fires is one worker losing its remaining trial budget plus a `PARTIAL` status.
correction: Mechanism and all line references are correct. Two refinements. (a) Severity: major overstates it. The collision window is a sub-millisecond write per completed trial against multi-minute trials, and the consequences are recoverable — completed trials are in the shared optuna SQLite study, no consumer reads best_config.json mid-run, and the scheduler regenerates it single-writer at pipelines/tuning/pipeline.py:160-161 after the workers finish. The concrete loss is one worker aborting its remaining trials and the model being recorded PARTIAL, not lost or permanently corrupted tuning results. Minor is the right level. (b) The claim's "the file that does get published is truncated/garbled JSON" is right but by a slightly different route than "the second open truncates the first writer's buffer": both processes write into the SAME inode at independent offsets, and once the first `os.replace` publishes that inode, the stalled writer's flush writes into the published best_config.json itself. Fix is one line in tools/data/io.py:24 — make the sidecar per-process/unique (e.g. `path.name + f".{os.getpid()}.tmp"`, or `tempfile.mkstemp` in `path.parent`) so each writer renames its own file; `os.replace` is then atomic between writers and last-writer-wins with valid JSON.

title: _fail_stale_trials FAILs every RUNNING trial with no ownership/heartbeat check, crashing live workers on resume
description: _fail_stale_trials takes every trial in state RUNNING and forces it to FAIL through the private storage API (study._storage.set_trial_state_values). Nothing distinguishes a trial abandoned by a dead worker from a trial a *live* worker is still executing: the study has no heartbeat_interval, and RDBStorage is constructed from a bare URL so no heartbeat/failed_trial_callback is configured. The scheduler is killable (webui detach/kill-front-end, SIGKILL) without its GpuQueue signal handler running, which orphans the worker subprocesses; the documented console 'orphan adoption' behaviour shows such orphans are a normal occurrence in this repo. Re-launching with --resume then marks the orphans' in-flight trials FAIL, and when the orphan finishes its trial Optuna's check_trial_is_updatable raises RuntimeError('Cannot change ... state of the finished trial'), killing the still-useful worker and discarding its epochs. The same call also re-issues those trial numbers, so GPU hours are spent twice on the same search budget.
suggested_fix: Configure RDBStorage with heartbeat_interval/grace_period and let Optuna's own stale-trial detection fail abandoned trials, or gate the repair on a recorded scheduler PID/lock so a live scheduler's trials are never touched. At minimum stop reaching into study._storage.
verdict_notes: The code fact is accurate: pipelines/tuning/pipeline.py:106-112 FAILs every RUNNING trial through study._storage.set_trial_state_values with no ownership/PID/heartbeat check, and the study is created from a bare sqlite URL (lines 98-104) so no heartbeat_interval or failed_trial_callback is configured. I reproduced the consequence against the pinned optuna 4.8.0 in the Dune env: while a worker is mid-trial on a sqlite study, running exactly line 110 from a second process makes the worker die at the next trial.report with UpdateFinishedTrialError('Trial#5 has already finished and can not be updated.'), after which study.optimize raises ValueError('Cannot tell a FAIL trial.') and the worker exits nonzero, discarding its epochs. study.optimize is called without catch= (pipelines/tuning/tuners.py, Tuner.run / AeTuner.run), so nothing absorbs it. However the claim's causal story is substantially wrong: webui/process_manager.py launches jobs with start_new_session=True (line 199-205) and stops them with os.killpg SIGTERM then SIGKILL (lines 608, 719, 733, 741), which reaches the GpuQueue children (gpu_queue.py:320, plain Popen, same group), and SIGTERM/SIGINT to the scheduler runs GpuQueue._terminate_running (gpu_queue.py:220-236) which terminates workers. Kill-front-end stops only the console server and leaves the whole job tree alive; the documented 'orphan adoption' behaviour concerns untracked main/ processes launched outside the webui, not workers orphaned by a dead scheduler. So the trigger reduces to kill -9 on the scheduler PID alone, an OOM kill, or an unhandled scheduler exception (GpuQueue.run's finally only restores signal handlers, never terminates children) — abnormal paths, in a state that is already unsupported because the orphans still hold GPUs the resumed scheduler re-assigns. The claimed trial-number reuse is also false: Optuna issues fresh numbers, and _count_done (line 114-115) counts only COMPLETE/PRUNED, so the budget is re-dispatched with or without the FAIL call. tests/tuning/test_pipeline.py:115-127 asserts the blanket FAIL as intended behaviour, but only for the abandoned-worker case.
correction: Mechanism confirmed at the cited line, but two details are wrong and the severity is inflated. (1) The webui does not orphan workers: process_manager.py launches with start_new_session=True and kills via os.killpg (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL in stop_all), which reaches the GpuQueue Popen children; GpuQueue._terminate_running also handles SIGTERM/SIGINT delivered to the scheduler; kill-front-end stops only the console server. The reachable triggers are 'kill -9 <scheduler pid>' alone, an OOM kill of the scheduler, or an unhandled scheduler exception (GpuQueue.run's finally restores signal handlers but never terminates children). (2) No trial numbers are re-issued and no extra GPU hours are attributable to this call: _count_done counts only COMPLETE/PRUNED, so leftover RUNNING trials are re-dispatched regardless. The actual damage is bounded: on a resume with a surviving orphan, each orphan crashes loudly (UpdateFinishedTrialError, then ValueError('Cannot tell a FAIL trial')) and loses its in-flight trial's partial epochs. A fix would be an ownership/liveness check (worker PID or host recorded as a trial user attr, or enabling Optuna heartbeats) before failing a RUNNING trial.

title: n_seeds in the sweep report counts seed directories, not the seeds that contributed to the mean
description: SweepRecord.n_seeds is set to len(runs), i.e. the number of seed subdirectories found on disk, but the mean/std come from SeedAggregation.aggregate, which drops entries whose value is None (tools/metrics/scoring.py:41-45). A unit whose 5 seed jobs produced only 1 test_metrics.json therefore renders in the markdown table (report.py:348-362) as 'Seeds 5' next to a test loss with no ± term, and patch_sweep.json records n_seeds=5 alongside test_loss_std=null. Since the table is the paper-facing artefact that decides the best patch size per dataset, a single-seed number is silently presented as a 5-seed number.
suggested_fix: Count the runs that actually contributed each aggregated metric (e.g. store n_test_loss / n_best_val_loss) and render that in the Seeds column, or drop runs with no metric from the record before aggregating.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source.

Mechanism, end to end:
1. `pipelines/patch_sweep/stages.py:19,42-43` — the training stage enqueues one GpuJob per (unit, seed) with `log_path = stage_dir/<unit>/seed<N>/worker.log`, and `QueuedStage.stage_dir = run_dir/"training"` (tools/orchestration/stages.py:51), the same directory the collector scans.
2. `tools/orchestration/gpu_queue.py:316` — `job.log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` runs before the subprocess starts, so `training/<unit>/seed<N>/` exists on disk for every seed that was *launched*, including one that crashes instantly (OOM, import error, killed).
3. `report.py:80-86` `_seed_runs` returns one entry per `seed\d+` directory found on disk, unconditionally.
4. `report.py:58-63` `_test_loss` returns None when `meta/test_metrics.json` is absent. That file is only written after a full successful `trainer.train(...)` (pipelines/backbone/training/pipeline.py:222-223), so a crashed seed has none.
5. `report.py:115` passes the runs to `SeedAggregation.aggregate`, which at tools/metrics/scoring.py:41-45 drops None entries per key, and `mean_std` (line 32) returns `std=None` when fewer than 2 values survive.
6. `report.py:124` sets `n_seeds = len(runs)` — the disk count from step 3, never the surviving count from step 5.

Concrete failure: sweep launched with `seeds=[0,1,2,3,4]`; seeds 1-4 die on GPU OOM. Five seed directories exist, one `test_metrics.json` exists. The unit renders in `_group_table` (report.py:347-362) as `Seeds 5` with a test loss and no `±` term, and `patch_sweep.json` records `"n_seeds": 5, "test_loss_std": null` (report.py:279-283). `_best` (report.py:257-262) ranks purely on `record.test_loss` with no regard for status or how many seeds contributed, so this single-seed, high-variance number can win the best-patch-per-dataset selection that the summary table and `best_patch_vs_dataset.png` publish.

Tests do not cover it: tests/patch_sweep/test_report.py only populates fully-complete seed runs (`populate_seeded_runs`) and asserts `n_seeds == 2` with all metrics present (lines 168-224). Nothing exercises a seed directory without `test_metrics.json`, so no test encodes the current behaviour as intended.

Not a KNOWN NON-ISSUE: it is not a legacy-fallback question, not dead code, not one of the listed deliberate quirks.
correction:
The mechanism is right but the "silently" framing is somewhat overstated, which is why minor (not major) is the correct severity:

1. In the realistic crash scenario the Status column is a partial guard. `_status` (report.py:104-112) returns "PARTIAL" whenever some but not all seeds report DONE in `pipeline/training_results.json`, so the row reads `Seeds 5 | ... | PARTIAL`. A missing `test_metrics.json` essentially implies a non-DONE status, because the file is written unconditionally at the end of a successful run. So the number is wrong, but the row is flagged. The absent `±` is a second (weaker) tell, since `std` is None only when fewer than two values survived.

2. The failure is not confined to test_loss. `n_seeds` is a single scalar covering four independently aggregated keys (`test_loss`, `best_val_loss`, `best_epoch`, `duration_s`, report.py:115). A seed killed after checkpointing but before the test pass contributes `best_val_loss` (read from `best_model.pt` via `rglob`, report.py:65-78) but not `test_loss`, so even the "surviving seeds" count is per-key, not one number.

3. Same pattern, same fix, in two sibling collectors: `pipelines/shared/comparison/trial_collection.py:75` and `pipelines/cross_validation/workers.py:99` both set `"n_seeds": len(runs)` alongside stds from the same `SeedAggregation.aggregate`. If this is fixed it should be fixed in all three, or the "Seeds" column should be relabelled "seeds launched" and a separate contributing-count reported.

4. There is a related inflation the claim does not mention: `_seed_runs` scans the disk, so seed directories left over from an earlier sweep with a different seed list are also picked up, get `status="MISSING"` from `results.get(name, {})`, yet their stale `test_metrics.json` *does* feed the mean.

title: The tuning worker silently falls back to a default TuningEntryConfig when --run-dir is absent
description: In the --worker branch the worker requires --model, --study-name and --storage-url but treats --run-dir as optional: `if args.run_dir:` loads the scheduler's resolved config, otherwise the worker proceeds with a freshly constructed TuningEntryConfig(). That default carries the hard-coded /ste/rnd/... paths, default epochs, default curriculum and default n_epochs, so a worker started without --run-dir would train on a different dataset and a different objective than the study it writes into, and nothing reports the discrepancy. The sibling entry point does this correctly: sweep_patches.py uses ConfigCli.load_worker_config, which raises FileNotFoundError when the resolved config is missing (tools/runtime/config_cli.py:235-236). This is precisely the silent fallback the project's 'break loudly' policy forbids.
suggested_fix: Add --run-dir to the worker's required-argument check and use ConfigCli.load_worker_config so a missing resolved config fails loudly.
verdict_notes:
Reproduced from source.

main/experiments/tune.py:40-51 (worker branch): it hard-fails on missing --model / --study-name / --storage-url, then does `config = TuningEntryConfig()` and only overwrites it `if args.run_dir:` via `ConfigCli.load_resolved(config, Path(args.run_dir) / "resolved_config.json")`. With --run-dir absent the worker runs with a freshly constructed default config and nothing logs or errors. Also `tag = args.run_tag or RunTag.now()`, so such a worker additionally invents a fresh run tag and writes its logs into a new directory under the default log_base_dir.

The default config is genuinely divergent from any real study: configuration/tuning/general.py:41-61 shows `paths = RunPathsConfig(log_base_dir=Path("/ste/rnd/User/vice_vi/DLR-TomoSAR/runs/tuning"))`, default `gpus=[0,1,2,3]`, `heads=["conv"]`, `curriculum=default_curriculum()`, default training/normalization/augmentation blocks. Trials produced by such a worker would be written into the study named by --storage-url/--study-name (pipelines/tuning/workers.py) while having been trained under a different dataset/objective than the scheduler resolved — i.e. silently poisoned study results.

The sibling comparison holds: main/experiments/sweep_patches.py:36, main/experiments/benchmark.py:32 and main/experiments/cross_validate.py:36 all call `ConfigCli.load_worker_config(...)` unconditionally; that helper derives `log_base_dir/run_tag/pipeline/resolved_config.json` when --run-dir is omitted and `load_resolved` raises FileNotFoundError if it does not exist (tools/runtime/config_cli.py:229-236, covered by tests/training_runtime/test_config_cli.py:208-210). main/inference/_inference_entry.py:86-88 likewise sys.exits when --run-dir/--config are missing. tune.py is the only worker entry with the conditional load, so this is an inconsistency with the repo's own contract, not a deliberate pattern.

Not a KNOWN NON-ISSUE: this is a silent fallback onto defaults, which the stated policy explicitly counts as a finding rather than a legacy-shim exemption. Tests do not sanction it — tests/entrypoints/test_main_entrypoints.py:271 only checks that --worker without --model exits; there is no test asserting the default-config path is intended.

Reachability caveat: pipelines/tuning/pipeline.py:76 always passes `--run-dir str(self.run_dir)` in `_worker_job`, and nothing in webui/ or scripts/ spawns tune workers itself, so the bad path is only reachable via manual/external invocation or a future caller. That keeps the practical impact at minor.
correction: Two details to sharpen. (1) Blast radius: the only in-repo launcher (pipelines/tuning/pipeline.py:76) always passes --run-dir, so today the fallback fires only on manual/external worker invocation — the finding is a contract/robustness violation rather than an actively firing bug; minor is the right severity. (2) The suggested fix is not a drop-in swap to ConfigCli.load_worker_config: the tuning scheduler saves its resolved config at `run_dir/resolved_config.json` (pipelines/tuning/pipeline.py:189), whereas load_worker_config looks for `<base>/pipeline/resolved_config.json` (tools/runtime/config_cli.py:231). The minimal correct fix is to make --run-dir (or --run-tag) mandatory in the worker branch and call load_resolved unconditionally, matching the sys.exit style already used for --model/--study-name/--storage-url. Secondary related defect at the same site: the worker also accepts a missing --run-tag and silently substitutes RunTag.now(), producing a fresh unrelated run directory.

title: The tuning objective is hard-labelled 'normalized param L1' although the default curriculum's val loss also carries the physics terms
description: The scheduler prints "best validation loss (normalized param L1)" and StudyPlotter.OBJECTIVE_NAME (plots.py:20) labels every axis "best validation loss (normalised params, lower is better)". The objective is whatever the trainer's criterion reports, which follows trainer_cfg.curriculum (set from config.curriculum in workers.py:70). The project default curriculum has enabled=True and swap_epoch=15 (configuration/training/backbone.py:44-49) with a complete stage that adds use_coherence_resyn and use_covariance_match; TuningConfig.n_epochs defaults to 30, so trials spend their last 15 epochs minimising param L1 + cosine + coherence resynthesis + covariance matching. Every study plot and the summary line therefore mislabel the quantity being optimised.
evidence: self.logger.subsection(f"Best — trial {payload['trial']}  best validation loss (normalized param L1) = {payload['val_loss']:.6f}")
suggested_fix: Derive the label from the active curriculum stage (or use a neutral 'validation loss (active curriculum stage)') in both pipeline.py:169 and StudyPlotter.OBJECTIVE_NAME.
verdict_notes: Reproduced from source. pipelines/tuning/pipeline.py:169 prints "best validation loss (normalized param L1)" and pipelines/tuning/plots.py:20 sets OBJECTIVE_NAME = "best validation loss (normalised params, lower is better)", used as target_name for optimization_history / parallel_coordinate / param_importances and to relabel every "Objective Value" axis. The reported value is study.best_trial.value (tuners.py BestConfigWriter.write, line 64), returned by Tuner._objective as best_val_loss from TrialPipeline.run(), which is tools/training/trainer.py:496 `self.checkpoint.best_val_loss` — the min over epochs of the full criterion's average validation loss (evaluate() aggregates `self.criterion(pred, gt, kz)` totals). The criterion follows trainer_cfg.curriculum, which workers.py:70 assigns from config.curriculum; TuningEntryConfig.curriculum defaults to default_curriculum() (configuration/tuning/general.py:54 -> configuration/training/backbone.py:19-49): enabled=True, swap_epoch=AblationCatalog.CURRICULUM_SWAP_EPOCH=15, warmup = param_l1(1.0) + cosine_curve(0.05), complete additionally = coherence_resyn(0.05) + covariance_match(0.05). TuningConfig.n_epochs=30 (configuration/tuning/general.py:27), so the last 15 epochs are trained/validated under the complete stage and their val losses are the ones minimized and reported. Hence the printed summary line and every study plot axis mislabel the optimized quantity. No test encodes the label as intended semantics (tests/tuning/test_plots.py:96 only checks the "Objective Value" -> OBJECTIVE_NAME substitution), and this is not one of the listed deliberate quirks. Two details in the claim are incomplete rather than wrong: the warmup stage itself already carries use_cosine_curve=True, so the objective is not pure param L1 even before the swap; and the same line/label is printed for all four SUPPORTED_TYPES (pipeline.py:23), including profile/image autoencoder and JEPA tuning where the objective is a reconstruction/embedding loss containing no param L1 at all, so that mislabel is unconditional. Impact is reporting-only; the search itself is unaffected, so minor severity stands.
correction: Mechanism is broader than stated. (1) The mislabel does not begin at the curriculum swap: default_curriculum()'s warmup stage already sets use_cosine_curve=True with weight 0.05, so the objective is param_l1 + cosine even during epochs 0-14; after epoch 15 it additionally carries coherence_resyn and covariance_match. (2) TuningScheduler.SUPPORTED_TYPES (pipelines/tuning/pipeline.py:23) covers backbone, image_autoencoder, jepa and profile_autoencoder, and the same hard-coded line at :169 plus StudyPlotter.OBJECTIVE_NAME are used for all of them — for the two autoencoder families and JEPA the objective is a reconstruction/embedding loss with no param L1 term whatsoever, so that mislabel holds regardless of any curriculum configuration. Fix should derive the objective label from the active loss configuration / training_type rather than hard-coding it in two places.
